schools.name: AGH University of science and technology
schools.overview:
Founded in 1919, the University of Science and Technology AGH is one of the best and most renowned Polish universities.

The school has nearly 32,000 students and consists of sixteen faculties.

The Faculty of Computer Science, Electronics and Telecommunications includes key research areas such as information society technologies, cloud computing technologies, fast optical networks, global wireless communications Internet of the future, the Internet of Things and sustainable development, for example. embedded systems in electronics, industrial electronics, telemedicine, electronic system design, signal recognition, microwave techniques, optoelectronics, photovoltaics, sensor systems, spintronics and nanotechnology.

In the "Perspektywy 2015" university rankings, the Faculty of Computer Science, Electronics and Telecommunications ranked first in Poland in the "Computer Science" category and the second among the Faculties of Education in Electronics and Telecommunications.

Classes take place in modern, well-equipped classrooms and laboratories, for example at the AGH UST Computer Center, which became operational in 2012 - a building that has received numerous awards and accolades for its original architecture.

The faculty also offers activities in student research groups: KNE (student interest group in electronics engineering), SPECTRUM (signal processing) and BIT. Curricula tailored to the needs of modern industry, combined with high standards of education, offer graduates of the Faculty of Computer Science, Electronics and Telecommunications a real advantage in the job market and enable them to become valuable members of engineering teams working for international companies. located in Krakow, such as IBM, Cisco, Motorola, Delphi, Comarch, ABB, Nokia Solutions and Networks.

schools.name: Asia Pacific University (APU)
schools.overview:
Asia Pacific University of Technology & Innovation (APU) is among the most diverse university in Malaysia, located in Kuala Lumpur, one of the most vibrant cities in Asia. Today, more than half of its students are international citizens, and come from 130 countries. The University has a long experience of recruiting, selecting and supporting international students.


APU is amongst Malaysia's Premier Private Universities, and is where a unique fusion of technology, innovation and creativity works effectively towards preparing professional graduates for significant roles in business and society globally.

APU's Ultra-Modern University Campus in MRANTi -Technology Park Malaysia is designed to be state-of-the-art teaching, learning and research facility providing a conducive environment for students and staff. TPM is the ideal location for this new and contemporary campus due to its strong positioning as Malaysia's primary hub for leading-edge and hich-tech developments in a wide variety of areas. It is also located in one of the most rapidly developing areas in Kuala Lumpur, and is well served and accessible through major highways, LRT and other forms of public transportation.

APU has earned an enviable reputation as an award-winning University through it achievements in winning a host of prestigious awards at national and international levels.

APU’s iconic campus is setting a new benchmark for design excellence among Malaysian Universities, combining an eco-friendly campus with a dynamic blend of technology and innovation to enable professional learning. It is a magnificent teaching & learning space for our students & staff designed by our award-winning architects & consultants.
schools.administrative:
Application process

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Transcript
  • Tepitech


Student Pass - Visa Processing

You will receive the Letter of Offer if you meet the eligibility criteria. You can confirm your enrolment and to enable the University to submit an application for your Student Visa, the payments of RM 3,400 (approx. USD 895) as Pre-Arrival Application Processing Fees is required immediately along with the documents stated below.

  • The Stage-1 Payment of Pre-Arrival Application Processing Fee of RM 3,400 (approx. USD 895) .
  • English Transcript
  • 4 Passport-sized photographs with WHITE background (35mm x 45mm). The photos must meet the requirements set by EMGS (Education Malaysia Global Services)
  • Copies of all pages of passport including blank pages. Passport must be valid for at least 24 months from the Intake Date.
  • Health Declaration Form signed by the student. You are advised to ensure that you are in good health prior to departure to Malaysia. APU recommends that all students attend the Pre-arrival Medical screening to ensure that they are in good health. You can download Health Declaration Form from the link below: https://visa.educationmalaysia.gov.my/media/docs/Lampiran_B_-_Health_Declaration_Form_For_Applicant.pdf
  • Please refer to the Medical Screening Guidelines here at: https://visa.educationmalaysia.gov.my/catalog/category/view/id/126 for more details. 
  • English proficiency certificate
  • Recommendation letter from Epitech
  • Any other requirements/documents as required by the University in support of your visa application.

Once APU receives your complete documents together with the International Student Visa Application Fees; they will submit your application to EMGS (Education Malaysia Global Services).

This may take about 2-3 weeks on receiving complete documents, together with the payment. We advise that all application forms arrive at least eight (8) weeks before the intake dates to ensure early approval. You can also track your application process at EMGS Website and you will be able to download your Visa Approval Letter (VAL) once approved.

Please note that you should avoid entering Malaysia during your visa process, to avoid any delay and queries from Malaysian Immigration. It is required that the student is outside Malaysia while the visa is processed and Visit Visas at the same time could result in rejection of your Student Pass Application. Transfer Students may process their application while being in Malaysia; however they will need to apply for a Special Pass for this process and is subject to Malaysian Immigration Approval.

If your VAL (Visa Approval Letter) is approved, you will be notified via email or by Post together with the necessary steps and guidelines. You can also check your application status at EMGS website and download the VAL

If you have a French passport, you are required to get a SINGLE ENTRY VISA (SEV) before your travel to Malaysia. Kindly proceed to the nearest local Malaysian Diplomatic Mission (i.e. Malaysian High Commission or Consulate); show them the Student Pass Approval Letter together with other required documents to obtain your Single-Entry Visa (SEV) to be stamped on your passport with the Student Pass Approval Letter “Reference Number” [BVP/STU/XXXXX/XXXXXXXX]. The Student Pass Approval Letter is usually valid for three months from the date of issuance; you must arrive in Malaysia one month prior to the expiry of your Student Pass Approval Letter (VAL).


Arrival in Malaysia

BEFORE YOUR DEPARTURE: please ensure that you go through your letter of offer as well as the arrival guideline for your scrutiny so as to fully understand and adhere to the requirements. Please also ensure that all your documentation is in place before traveling i.e. passports, health certificates, student pass approval letter, visas, etc. for the immigration clearance. Your passport must be valid for at least a 13 month-duration at the time of your departure.

In order to facilitate and expedite your airport pick-up, immigration clearance (compulsory for all arriving students) and transfer to the accommodation, you must notify us at least 7 (seven) days prior to your arrival in Malaysia by filling up the APU Student Arrival Form. This is necessary for us to facilitate accommodation arrangements and airport pick-up. You are required to furnish us with details of your date and time of arrival in Kuala Lumpur, flight number and also the number of luggage.

You are strongly advised to arrive in Malaysia at least one week before the intake commences to avoid missing the Orientation and International Student briefing. In order to help you settle into the professional environment at APU, you will be provided with a comprehensive orientation briefing. You will be given information on the course schedule, timetable, facilities, academic regulations and other necessary details. Students are not permitted to join the class if they arrive 2 weeks after the course has commenced.


Health Insurance

You will need to go for a Medical Check-up at EMGS appointed Clinics within 7 days of your arrival in Malaysia. Please meet our staff at the International Office and we will guide you on where to go for the medical screening. Once your medical check-up is done, please HAND OVER YOUR PASSPORT & MEDICAL CHECK-UP SLIP TO OUR STAFF AT THE INTERNATIONAL OFFICE. We will then wait for your Medical Result (normally 4-5 days) before we can submit your passport for long-term endorsement of student visa sticker for the duration of your studies, maximum 1 year initially and subject to course duration. The endorsement indicates your visa type, the length of stay in Malaysia, the number of entries permitted into Malaysia and the validity of the student pass.

schools.name: Auckland University of Technology
schools.overview:
Overview

Auckland University of Technology (AUT) is one of New Zealand's leading modern universities, recognised for its innovative teaching, strong industry partnerships, and commitment to preparing graduates for successful international careers. Established as a university in 2000, AUT has quickly earned a reputation for academic excellence, research impact, and a practical, hands-on approach to learning.

Located in Auckland, New Zealand's largest and most dynamic city, AUT welcomes more than 29,000 students, including over 5,000 international students from more than 140 countries. This diverse and multicultural environment provides students with the opportunity to study alongside peers from around the world while experiencing New Zealand's unique culture and lifestyle.

AUT's programmes are designed in close collaboration with industry partners to ensure students develop the technical knowledge, professional skills, and practical experience sought by employers. Project-based learning, laboratory work, internships, and real-world industry projects are integrated throughout many programmes, enabling students to apply their learning in authentic professional settings.

The university operates across three modern campuses—City Campus, North Campus, and South Campus—each offering state-of-the-art teaching facilities, collaborative learning spaces, research laboratories, libraries, innovation hubs, and student support services. The City Campus, located in the heart of Auckland's central business district, provides easy access to major technology companies, start-ups, cultural attractions, restaurants, and public transportation.

AUT is internationally recognised for its strengths in Computer Science, Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Engineering, Business, Design, Health Sciences, and Communication Studies. The university places a strong emphasis on innovation, entrepreneurship, sustainability, and interdisciplinary collaboration, encouraging students to develop creative solutions to real-world challenges.

Beyond academics, AUT offers a vibrant student experience through numerous clubs and societies, sporting facilities, volunteering opportunities, cultural events, leadership programmes, and career development services. International students benefit from comprehensive support before arrival and throughout their studies, including orientation programmes, academic assistance, wellbeing services, and dedicated international student advisors.

Consistently ranked among the world's leading young universities, AUT combines academic excellence with an outstanding quality of life. Auckland is regularly recognised as one of the world's most liveable cities, offering beautiful beaches, parks, hiking trails, a thriving technology sector, and a safe, welcoming environment for international students.

Studying at AUT provides EPITECH students with the opportunity to experience a globally recognised education, strengthen their technical and professional skills, and immerse themselves in one of the Asia-Pacific region's most innovative and internationally connected cities.
schools.administrative:
Administrative Information

Auckland University of Technology (AUT) provides comprehensive support to international and exchange students throughout the application process, from admission to arrival in New Zealand. Students are expected to complete both the EPITECH administrative requirements and AUT's online application process.

1. Application Dossier

You will find information about the general EPITECH application process on the Global Campus platform.

Once nominated by EPITECH, AUT's International Office will contact you by email with instructions on how to complete your application through the AUT Student Portal.

You will work directly with AUT regarding your application and admission.

Documents your host university may request:

  • Completed online application form

  • Official academic transcript (provided by EPITECH)

  • Proof of current enrolment at EPITECH

  • Copy of your passport (valid for the duration of your stay)

  • English language proficiency certificate (if required)

  • Personal statement

  • Course selection or study plan

2. Student Visa

International students studying in New Zealand for more than three months are generally required to obtain a Fee-Paying Student Visa before travelling.

Once AUT has issued your official Offer of Place and you have completed the required acceptance procedures, you will be able to apply for your student visa through Immigration New Zealand.

Students are responsible for submitting their visa application in sufficient time before departure and ensuring they comply with all immigration requirements.

You are strongly advised not to purchase non-refundable flights until your student visa has been approved.

For the latest visa information, students should consult Immigration New Zealand and follow the official application process.

Student Visas and Permits - International Students - AUT

3. Insurance & Health

International students must hold appropriate medical and travel insurance for the entire duration of their stay in New Zealand.

Mandatory for EPITECH students to pay student's levy fees = $611 NZD

AUT requires all international students to have insurance that complies with the New Zealand Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice.

AUT can arrange an approved insurance policy for eligible students, or students may provide evidence of an equivalent policy that meets university requirements.

Insurance should include coverage for:

  • Medical and hospital treatment

  • Emergency healthcare

  • Prescription medication

  • Personal liability

  • Repatriation

  • Travel disruption and emergency assistance

Students should ensure that their insurance remains valid from the day they leave their home country until they return after completing their studies.

New Zealand's healthcare system is excellent; however, international students are generally not entitled to publicly funded healthcare unless specific agreements apply.

Medical and Travel Insurance - International Students - AUT

AUT student accommodation offers options from approximately NZ$363 per week at Akoranga Student Village to NZ$506 per week for a studio at Te Āhuru Mayoral Drive for 2027. Internet and power are included in these accommodation fees.

Food

Students can save money by preparing meals at home and shopping at supermarkets such as Pak'nSave, Woolworths and New World. Auckland also offers a wide range of international food markets and supermarkets.

Transport

Auckland has an extensive public transport network including buses, trains and ferries. Students can use an AT HOP card, and eligible full-time students can benefit from student discounts on public transport. Walking and cycling are also convenient options depending on where you live.

Budget recommendation

For a comfortable student lifestyle in Auckland, we recommend budgeting approximately NZ$2,200–3,500 per month, including accommodation and everyday living expenses.

The Australian Catholic University (ACU) is a public university funded by the Australian government.

ACU has more than 16,000 students, including nearly 3,000 foreign students, who benefit from the advantages of small, welcoming campuses and small classes, as well as direct contact with highly qualified teachers and access to quality support services.

ACU offers services to international students allowing them to facilitate their integration, including:

  • Accommodation assistance
  • Airport reception
  • Computer and internet access
  • Clubs and sports committees
  • Services for the disabled
  • And more...

The University has 6 campuses. Computer classes take place on the Mackillop campus in North Sydney.

To find out more about advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here.
schools.administrative:

The visa will have to be done online as soon as the final admission by ACU and reception of the CoE ('confirmation of enrollment').

When you receive your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), you can apply for a student visa (subclass 500), Non-Award Sector.

It is your responsibility to get your visa in a timely manner and to understand fully your obligations and responsibilities when applying for a student visa.

Students are advised not to book a non-refundable travel ticket until their visa has been issued.

https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500#Overview

The cost for this visa is AU$ 2000 (2025).


3. Compulsory International Insurance

You must subscribe to Australian insurance, the Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), to obtain your student visa. It can go up to AUD$700.

ACU offers to take out the insurance through the university, but you may prefer another insurance company that is licensed by the Immigration Department.

Please note: you must have an OSHC for the duration of your visa and the duration of your program.

You must therefore choose a duration of 14 months, even if the program lasts 12 months.


More information:

http://www.health.gov.au/internet/main/publishing.nsf/Content/Overseas+Student+Health+Cover+FAQ-1

You can therefore compare the rates if you wish.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

On-campus accommodation

ACU doesn't offer on-campus accommodation.


Off-campus accommodation

There are many different accommodation options available in Australia. The ACU Rental Advisory Service can help find housing that best suits your needs and budget. It is important to ensure you have secured accommodation prior to your arrival in Australia.

ACU student accommodation: the Miguel Cordero Residence

ACU a residence called Miguel Cordero located within a short commute from ACU's North Sydney campus.

Living in ACU student accommodation is a great way to get the most of your university experience. Students will experience community living in an inclusive and supportive environment with students from Australia and the world. ACU student accommodation offers fully secured, 24-hour support, WiFi and on-site facilities including laundry and recreation rooms.

Our modern residence is comprised of studios and multi-share apartments. All rooms are fully furnished and located over three floors, all with lift access. 

You must apply online through the ACU website. Email: studentaccommodation.nsw@acu.edu.au

The 2026 room rates are the following:

Room Multi-share: $445 (Weekly / 1 Semester) | $430 (Weekly / 2 Semester) | $415 (Weekly / 6 months) | $405 (Weekly / 12 months)

Studio: $470 (Weekly / 1 Semester) | $455 (Weekly / 2 Semester) | $440 (Weekly / 6 months) | $435 (Weekly / 12 months)

Premium studio: $540 (Weekly / 1 Semester) | $515 (Weekly / 2 Semester) | $500 (Weekly / 6 months) | $490 (Weekly / 12 months)


You can also go for private housing options (see more detail below). The neighborhoods close to the North Sydney campus are : Crows Nest, Kirribilli, Milsons Point, Chatswood, St Leonards, Waverton, Wollstonecraft. It is up to you to calculate the transport costs to add before making your decision. Please note that housing near the North Sydney campus is often expensive and in high demand.


Private housing: Semester in Australia (SiA)

Semester in Australia provides housing and support services in Brisbane, Sydney and Melbourne, specifically for students in Australia on a short term basis (semester/year) for exchange and study abroad programs. The service provides accommodation, local support, includes most utilities, and can also provide arrival assistance. They have a great deal of experience and helpful, friendly staff.

Students should visit the SiA website for details, and contact SiA directly if they are interested in the offered housing options. Applications and bookings are made directly with SiA


Private housing: Australian Home Stay Network

Homestay accommodation is when a local family provides accommodation in their home. Students will have a bedroom with linen provided, a place to study, and access to a bathroom, kitchen and other facilities in the home.

The cost is approx. $260-$300 AUD per week and includes:

o Two meals on weekdays (Breakfast and Dinner). Three meals on weekends.

o Basic furniture

o 30-60 minutes transport time away from the University

o Minimum stay is 4 weeks and maximum stay up to 1 year

Students can book their homestay through the Homestay Network’s website.


Private housing: Independent student accommodation providers, eg UniLodge, Scape, Urbanest, Iglu, StudentOne

Student accommodation is also offered by a range of providers. These providers offer secure, apartment-style living. Please consult their website for more information.


Private housing: private/shared rentals

You should budget approximately AUD$150 - $250 per week to rent a property shared with others. Utilities and food are not included in this estimate. For this option, ACU does not recommend you secure your accommodation before arriving in Australia as it is best to view each property in person.

For more information on accommodation, please visit this page on the university's website.

Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Yuan (RMB or CNY). 1 € = 8.26 RMB (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


We advise you to plan a monthly budget of minimum 300€ for your expenses (can go up to 700€ depending on your lifestyle according to former students), rent excluded.


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "When traveling, expenses could rise to around €1,200–1,300, especially for destinations like Zhangjiajie or Guilin. Food is generally cheaper than in France, but in Beijing, prices are higher than in most other Chinese cities. You can eat for under €5 per day if you mostly eat at the school cafeteria, but you’ll probably want to explore more local restaurants too, they’re inexpensive and delicious."


"If we don't take the accommodation in account, I was around 500-600€ a month, but you can easily stay between 270-400€ (but try to have fun, you won't have many opportunities such as this one). You can also easily get higher than that depending on your needs."

  • Housing: 200-1000€ depending on whether you live in the dormitory or not
  • Food: 100-150€
  • On-campus cafeteria: Self-serve meals cost less than €2.50 for a hearty dish
  • Off-campus meals: Around 20–25 yuan, depending on the food and venue
  • Transportation
  • Metro: Around 5 yuan (~€0.60)
  • Bus: 1 to 2 yuan
  • Taxi in Beijing: Around €6 from city center to the university
  • Phone, internet / 16€ internet /6€ phone
  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure: 100-200€
  • For nightlife, if you are European, entry and drinks are usually free
  • For monuments and cultural sites, most have an entry fee
  • In 80% of cases, you get student discounts with your student card

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.

Additional Programme Specifics

Beijing Jiaotong University

Beijing Jiaotong University (BJTU) is one of the most important universities in China. Its history dates back to the Qing Dynasty in 1896.

Located in downtown Beijing in the Haidian district, which is recognized as the "Cradle of Higher Education" in China, BJTU covers an area of 78 hectares and is made up of two campuses, East and West. The two campuses are very well laid out, and offer many facilities and a beautiful environment. Just north of the university is Zhongguancun, the computer village known as the "Silicon Valley" of China.

BJTU is one of the first universities to have been selected for the national programs “National 211 Project” and “985 Strength Discipline Innovation Platform.” It plays an important role in the development of the Chinese railway industry, having contributed massively at each stage of the sector’s development.

Epitech students will study at the School of Software Engineering (SSE). Created in 2001, it employs practice-based learning, and in 2009 received first prize for the best computer training program among the 36 software engineering schools of China.

The host university will assist you with visa conversion procedures, medical examinations, and obtaining the resident permit.

Related costs are the responsibility of the students (see estimated budget at the bottom of the page).


Please note:

  • For the latest information regarding visa application, you should contact your nearest Embassy/Consulate of China.
  • After you arrive in the Chinese mainland, the X visa for single entry cannot allow you to exit and re-enter the Chinese mainland. You must stay in the Chinese mainland until the Residence Permit is granted.


4.Insurance and Health

You will be asked to undergo medical examinations after arriving in Beijing.

The results must be presented to the Beijing Bureau of Exit and Entry Administration of the Ministry of Public Security when you apply for a residence permit.


The costs of these exams will be borne by the student (see “Estimated Budget”).


According to the regulations made by Chinese Ministry of Education, all the international students in China are required to purchase comprehensive insurance and the valid period should cover the duration of their studies. You may subscribe to the insurance on the registration day at BJTU if it's not required for your visa application. The steps to subscribe to BJTU insurance must only be carried out once in China.


In order to be fully covered for medical care, we recommend that you take out international insurance as well. It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/chine

Note: It is advisable to register on the French registry established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html 


5.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on China, click here.


Campus life

Student's feedback (2024-2025): "Life there was good, there was a lot of free time to go to the gym, swim, play basketball. Things are cheap so you can do a lot of things. There are a zoo and an aquarium next to the school; as well as a lot of restaurants, multiple coffee shops and supermarkets on campus. There are 8 different cafeterias, even some with halal food. There are also multiple student associations (hard to get in though) dedicated to archery, volleyball, Chinese lion dance..."
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

BJTU Student Apartments is the preferred option for our international students. There are four buildings are available for international students. On-campus dormitories (four people in a room) are equipped with public kitchen, laundry room, private bathroom, TV set, phone, WIFI, air-conditioner, single bed (including bedding), bookshelves and wardrobe.

Students must take care of their rooms (cleaning products are not provided by the university) and respect the curfew.

Students who voluntarily leave their university accommodations during their studies are not allowed to sublet their room to a third party.

The rent for university accommodation will not be reimbursed.

The accommodation cost of campus residence is about CNY16,200-21,600/year/person (about 2500€ - for reference only and subject to final adjustment of prices each year).

Exchange students can pay by day: CNY40-60/day/person.

A deposit will be required before you have access to the room (1000 yuan per person).


Off-campus accommodation

Students can also rent apartments outside the campus by themselves.

Student's feedback (2024-2025): "It’s not as cheap as you might think. I stayed in the university dormitories for the first semester, then moved to an apartment nearby. I paid around €1,100 per month, which is quite expensive because the area around BJTU (Haidian District) is costly. If you’re on a budget, staying in the dorms or sharing a flat with other students is a better option."


Finding accommodation via reputable rental agencies

Due to its close proximity to Tsinghua University, many students living off campus choose to live in apartment blocks located in the Wudaokou and Liudaokou areas.


Below are the main rental agencies in China. Before your arrival, you can first access their websites to learn of their accommodation options. Then once in China, you can go to their neighborhood shopfronts to request to view properties.


Ziroom is a popular choice for foreigners renting in Beijing. They have an easy-to-use app that also has an English interface for searching for accommodation. Once securing accommodation via Ziroom, on the app you can find the details of your accommodation, including the contract and details on your payments made. Included in the contract is a service fee, which includes regular cleaning of the public spaces of the apartment, and also easy servicing for repairs. You will also be advised to add your agent on WeChat for ease of contact.

Lianjia

5i5j


Notes:

  • always keep copies of all payments and the contract;
  • always sign a contract. Without a contract you have no legal rights;
  • when you live off-campus, never forget to register at your local police station to obtain a Registration Form of Temporary Residence within 24 hours after your arrival in China or signing of the rental contract.
  • please note that it could be difficult finding an apartment if you don't speak Chinese.

  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.

schools.cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 1000€ depending on the company & the dates
  • Insurance from BJTU: about 100€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage
  • Visa: between 110-130€
  • Medical examinations in China: about 100€
  • Accommodation deposit: 1000 yuan (about 120€)
  • Chinese residence permit: 500 yuan (60€), etc.


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Yuan (RMB or CNY). 1 € = 8.26 RMB (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


We advise you to plan a monthly budget of minimum 300€ for your expenses (can go up to 700€ depending on your lifestyle according to former students), rent excluded.


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "When traveling, expenses could rise to around €1,200–1,300, especially for destinations like Zhangjiajie or Guilin. Food is generally cheaper than in France, but in Beijing, prices are higher than in most other Chinese cities. You can eat for under €5 per day if you mostly eat at the school cafeteria, but you’ll probably want to explore more local restaurants too, they’re inexpensive and delicious."


"If we don't take the accommodation in account, I was around 500-600€ a month, but you can easily stay between 270-400€ (but try to have fun, you won't have many opportunities such as this one). You can also easily get higher than that depending on your needs."


  • Housing:
  • about 2000€/year if you live on-campus
  • 300€-1000€/month if you live off-campus (but please note that the city is huge and that living near campus is costly. Living on-campus is recommended.)
  • Food: 100-150€
  • 1€ a meal to 15€ (good meal in a restaurant)
  • Transportation
  • Metro: Around 5 yuan (~€0.60)
  • Bus: 1 to 2 yuan
  • Phone, internet: 12€/month for internet in the studios / 6€ phone
  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure;100-200€
  • For nightlife, if you are European, entry and drinks are usually free
  • For monuments and cultural sites, most have an entry fee
  • In 80% of cases, you get student discounts with your student card

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.

schools.name: Binus University
schools.overview:
Bina Nusantara University, also known as BINUS University, is a private university located in Jakarta, in the south of Tangerang in Bekasi, Indonesia. All of its campuses are located in the Greater Jakarta Region.


Founded in 1974, BINUS University has more than 30,000 students and links with nearly 5,000 companies.

BINUS University is ranked among the 251–260 universities in the QS University Rankings: Asia 2018, and is one of the top 9 universities in Indonesia.


For travel advice issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Indonesia, click here.
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier


You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • You will receive your login credentials for the online application called iMobilio from your host university
  • Passport (make sure to have your passport valid at least 18 months from the application date)
  • Passport-size Photo
  • Academic transcript (available on your intra)
  • English Proficiency Test Certificate (Tepitech available on your intra)
  • Enrollment Statement from Home University (please ask the IAFF office to provide you this document)
  • Statement of Purpose


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Receipt of the acceptance letter


Once the application file has been sent to the partner university, you will receive an admission letter and can then take the following steps (visa, accommodation search, insurance ...).

The format of the letter of admission is exclusively electronic. The documents you will receive include:

  • Admission letter. The letter of admission is written in English. It confirms that you will be a student at BINUS.
  • Visa sponsor & Guarantee letter. They are documents written in Bahasa. These documents are intended for the Embassy or Consulate of Indonesia.
  • Study permit: document proving that you have the right to study in Indonesia. You will need this document for your visa application.
  • TELEX: authorization document. The TELEX will be sent to the embassy / consulate where the visa process takes place. It is the student’s responsibility to retrieve this document. TELEX has an expiration date. Once it has expired, it must be re-started.


3. Visa procedures


Once the admission file has been received, you can do your visa procedures.

You must have a VITAS (Limited Stay Permit Visa for Study Purpose). This Visa "C316" is valid for 6 or 12 months and for multiple entries.

In particular, you will need to provide financial documents (bank statements with a net income of 1,500 euros per month).

Please consult the website of the Indonesian Embassy in Paris to finalize your request for a 'Long stay Education 316' visa: https://kemlu.go.id/paris/en/pages/visa_/532/etc-menu


Once there, you have 30 days to register with the immigration authorities. Please note that you will need this permit to open a local bank account. These steps are very important, because one month after your arrival in Indonesia, you must have a "KITAS" card which will be useful in everyday life. It will, for example, allow you to pay the same price as the "locals" for certain tourist attractions.


4. Insurance and Health


In order to be better covered for medical care, we recommend that you take out international insurance in France at the same time. It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/indonesie

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.

INUS University offers a dormitory "Binus square- Hall of residence." This dormitory is located about an hour away from the campus. You can make the commute via free shuttle. The dormitory has laundry facilities and a canteen, but also a curfew, shared shower/ toilet facilities. 

Rent goes from 1150USD to 2500USD per semester depending on the room type and the residence.


Off-campus accommodation


Students can rent apartments or single rooms in the dormitory pavilions and private homes. The prices vary ranging from 50 USD to 300 USD monthly.

Tenants usually browse through the website:

  • E-Visa: to pay and have before entering the country which costs 2,525,000 Rp (140€).

  • IMEI registration for phones worth less than $500 is free (ONLY ON THE DAY OF ARRIVAL). In addition, the fee for foreigners is 40% of the cost of the phone*, exceeding the $500 rate if you register the phone on the day of arrival.

  • 1kg of rice: 0,70€
  • Package of pasta: 2€
  • Bottle of coca cola 1.5L: 1€

schools.overview: The Polytechnic Institute of Bragança (IPB) is a Portuguese University of Applied Sciences with 8000 students and 500 teachers and researchers. It has an internationalization programme with widely recognized success, including the annual mobility of more than 900 incoming and outgoing students and 300 teaching staff members. IPB is also recognized by its performance in applied research and regional engagement.

BUDAPEST UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY AND ECONOMICS


Founded in 1782, Budapest University of Technology and Economics (BME) was the first European institution to train engineers at university level.


It is a prestigious Hungarian university, and counts several Nobel Prize winners and many renowned scientists among its alumni.


There are some 24,000 students enrolled at the university, in over 8 faculties with approximately 1300 academic staff.


The Budapest University of Technology and Economics seeks to promote the characteristics of a traditional research university, while simultaneously unifying theory and practice through high standard theoretical foundations and practical training based on industrial relationships.


BME's mission is to train industry professionals in the following disciplines:

  • Technology
  • IT
  • Natural Sciences
  • Economics
  • Business and Management

1. Application Dossier

1. Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to the university, you will receive an acceptance letter and an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2.     Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3.     Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4.     Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3.Insurance and Health (more information here)

CSULB requires students to purchase their compulsory insurance.

Please check the coverage of the insurance.

On campus, there is a medical center for non-emergency cases.

If you are off campus or cannot wait, check the JCB / Anthem partner doctors/hospitals for affordable rates.

Be aware of “copay” or “coinsurance” amounts that remain your responsibility.


To be fully covered abroad, we recommend all students take out international insurance during their Tech 4. It is imperative that you take out an international insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information. 


In addition, CSULB requires proof of vaccinations prior to course registration (more information here). CSULB will assist if you have questions.

If you cannot get vaccinated or provide proof before departure, vaccines can be administered upon arrival at the CSULB Student Health Center.


If vaccinated in France, bring a copy of your health book. All documentation must be in English.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the US, click here.

The campus offers many activities that help students meet others.

Car Rental: avoid renting from Dollar. Recommended: Alamo (professional), Turo (individuals). Always purchase DMV insurance.

In California, you can drive with your French license for 30 days after arrival.

After 30 days, you must obtain the California driving permit. Your I-94 and/or passport stamp are used as proof of entry.

Driving beyond 30 days without a U.S. license is a serious offense, which can lead to: court appearance, high fines, and potential prison/community service (especially in case of an accident)

California State University San Marcos (CSUSM) is part of the 23 California State University network.

San Marcos has quickly become the main educational center in northern San Diego County with modern buildings, advanced computer technology and state-of-the-art scientific laboratories.

San Marcos is located in the north of the San Diego region (in the heart of the southern California coastal region), 50 kilometers north of the city of San Diego and 150 kilometers south of Los Angeles. You can also easily reach the San Diego Zoo, Sea World, Disneyland and Hollywood.

You must submit a petition to the Office of Global Education to approve your alternative policy. The petition must be accompanied by documentation clearly describing (in English) the policy benefits and restrictions.

You must make your own travel arrangements from the airport to San Marcos.  We recommend that you arrive at the San Diego International Airport. If you arrive in San Diego, and you are living in homestay, then you may reserve airport transportation with the homestay company. You may also reserve an airport shuttle from Los Angeles International Airport, but this can cost about $200 and can take 2 hours to get to San Marcos. Flights from Los Angeles to San Diego cost between $50 - $150. You must reserve a shuttle or arrange your transportation before you leave your home country.  CSUSM does not provide airport transportation.

The number of students per class is limited, which allows individualized instruction, and the classrooms and laboratories are new and equipped with the latest technology.


There are apartment-style university residences on campus, where life is buzzing with more than 80 clubs and organizations, art conferences, movies, concerts, and guest speakers.

  • Host family

Price : $800- $900/month (may be subject to fluctuations). Breakfasts and dinners are included from Monday to Friday. Well located in San Marcos and the surrounding cities. Please note : registration fees and a deposit may be required.


- How are they selected?

Students submit an application with choices & personal details (e.g. willingness to live with young children/pets, any allergies, etc.) and then the host provider will provide them with options that the students can then rank. This is the ideal circumstance that students get choice. That said, when availability starts to decrease, it is possible that the homestay provider may place based on the preferences written in the application.


- Are they generally close to campus or would students need a car?

The general guideline is that students should be able to get from their host family to CSUSM campus in 45 minutes or less. This could mean walking, biking, or public transportation. So, a car is not necessary. That said, if a student plans to buy a car, they should mention this in their application as it could provide more host family options.

For non-Europeans students or students with a non-European citizenship, please check the immigration office of the host country to check the visa process and fees.

Students in France can use this website: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/


3) Insurance

For European students

The European Health Insurance Card (CEAM in French) is nominative and individual. This card certifies your rights to the Health Insurance in Europe. To obtain your card, log in to your Ameli account at least two months before your departure. It is free of charge and will be sent to your place within two weeks. You can also download it online.

For more information: https://www.ameli.fr/assure/droits-demarches/europe-international/protection-sociale-etranger/etudes-etranger


For non-European students

You must register for a private health insurance to cover your full stay. Please check with your parents, bank, or any private insurance company for more information depending on the wanted coverage.

Please register via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ariane) platform to be aware of any news (terrorist attack, tsunami, earthquake…) in your host country for French citizens only: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/ public / login.html



Campus life

The following places are recommended to visit when in Cardiff:

  • Cardiff Bay

You can get to the area by either car, bus or train (Cardiff Bay station). The old Cardiff docklands have been redeveloped in the last decade to create Cardiff Bay, home to a large freshwater lake for sailing and water sports; the swanky five star St David's hotel and spa, and Mermaid Quay – hotspots with restaurants with everything from Italian to Turkish cuisine.


  • The Senedd / Pierhead Building

The Welsh Assembly Government's new debating chamber, The Senedd, was opened by the Queen on St David's Day 2006. Visitors can explore the building, have coffee and cakes in the café or watch Assembly debates from the public viewing gallery. Next door to the Senedd is the historic Pierhead Building, which contains an interactive exhibition on the role of the National Assembly. (free entry)


  • Wales Millennium Centre

Dominating the skyline in Cardiff Bay, the Wales Millennium Centre is home to seven major arts organizations, including the Welsh National Opera and Diversions Dance Company. The Centre presents international opera, ballet, modern dance and musicals, all with prices to please arts novices as well as arts lovers. 'Arts Sherpas' also run tours around the front and backstage areas and if you're lucky you may even catch a glimpse of a rehearsal. (Tours take about one hour and run throughout the day. Book in advance, please check their website for admission fees.)


City centre

  • Cardiff Castle, Castle Street

Cardiff may only have been a city for 100 years, but there has been a castle here for nearly 2000 years. Tours of the castle interior take place throughout the day, or visitors can just enjoy a stroll around the picturesque Castle gardens. Please check their website for admission fees.


  • National Museum

Two wealthy Welsh sisters bequeathed their large art collection to the museum and gallery in the mid 20th century, resulting in Cardiff owning one of the largest collections of Impressionist paintings outside of Paris, with works by Renoir, Monet and Cezanne on display. (free entry, closed Mondays). The grand civic centre that surrounds it is worth a walk around, in particular Cathays Park, with the National War memorial within it.


  • Millennium Stadium

When the Stadium isn't hosting major sports matches or concerts you can take a tour of the 74,000 seater stadium. Walk down the players' tunnel, try out the Queen's seat in the Royal box and discover how they removed the curse from the away-team changing rooms. Please check their website for admission fees.


  • The Cardiff Arcades

The main arcades can be reached from St Johns Street, High St, Duke St or St Mary Street. Each arcade is home to an array of independent shops offering bits 'n' bobs for the home and top-notch fashion. Cool. Visit the High Street and Duke Street arcades for a fetish fumble in Eccentrixs, or cool individual clothes brands Pussy Galore and Drooghi. Budding Imelda Marcos's will be happy in the long established shoe heaven Buzz and homebodies will spend a small fortune in Nice interiors.

Cross the road and head down the Castle Arcade. Get se-juiced by a health-kick beverage at the Organic Juice Company. Take a sharp exit into the DJ record shop and get the latest vinyl releases to add to your collection. If you're still standing at this point, walk back to St Mary Street and towards the bus station to find the Morgan and Royal Arcades. Morgan's is home to some good cafes. Go back out onto St Mary Street and turn left into the Royal Arcade. Refuel at Fresh with their excellent baguettes, then move on to Room for 'Look how well travelled I am' furniture. Plus a lot more that we can't even hope to include here – get browsing. Other arcades not to be missed out are the Oxford Arcade off the Hayes and the Dominions and Andrews Arcades off Queen Street.


Outside the centre

  • Roath Park

Stands in a beautiful location at the centre of the busy capital city of Wales, Cardiff, just outside the area of Roath itself. The park still retains the classic Victorian Park atmosphere where local inhabitants and visitors alike can enjoy their leisure time in many different pursuits in particular the rose garden and boating lake.


  • St Fagans National Museum of Wales

St Fagans opened on 1 July 1948. Since then, it has established itself as one of Europe's foremost open air museums and become Wales's most popular heritage attraction. The Museum shows how the people of Wales lived, worked and spent their leisure time over the last five hundred years, and over the past fifty years it has inspired generations of visitors with its exploration of Welsh history and tradition. The Museum stands in the grounds of the magnificent St Fagans Castle, a late 16th-century manor house generously donated to the people of Wales by the Earl of Plymouth.


Near Cardiff

  • Caerphilly Castle (7 miles north of Cardiff)

Caerphilly Castle is one of the largest Castles in the United Kingdom, built in 1268-1271 by the Anglo-Norman lord, Gilbert de Clare. It can be accessed either by car, bus or train by going to the town of Caerphilly.


  • Castell Coch (4 miles from city centre)

Castell Coch is a late nineteenth-century 'fairytale'-style castle, built on medieval remains, designed for the third marquess of Bute by William Burges. Lavishly decorated and furnished in the Victorian Gothic style; a Romantic vision of the Middle Ages. It is set above the village of Tonygwynlais which is on the outskirts of Cardiff and can be accessed off the A470 road.


  • Duffryn Gardens (10 miles from city centre)

Duffryn comprises a series of gardens, broad sweeping lawns, shrubberies, water features and various compartments enclosed within clipped yew hedges. The gardens are currently being restored. The Round Garden, the Pompeiian, the Theatre garden where plays are performed, the Mediterranean and the Physic gardens are in their full glory. There is a tea room, free parking, some public conveniences, a souvenir shop and many picnic areas. From Penarth take the A4232 towards the M4 (J33), take the second exit (to Culverhouse Cross) At the Culverhouse roundabout take the A48 signposted Cowbridge. In St Nicholas village turn left at the traffic lights. The gardens are about a mile down the narrow road on the right. Open all year, free December-March, charge April-November. Tel; 029 2059 3328.


To familiarise yourself further with a number of Cardiff's main cultural institutions please click the links below.

The New Theatre,Sherman Theatre,St David's concert hallandMillennium Centre(Cardiff main theatres and concert venues)

ADDITIONAL PROGRAMME SPECIFICS

CHITKARA UNIVERSITY


Chitkara University is located in the North of India, near the city of Chandigarh.

Founded in 2010, it offers bachelors, masters and doctoral programs, entirely in English, in the fields of Engineering Management, IT, Pharmacy and many others, and welcomes nearly 7,000 students.

This very modern University has connections with influential companies such as Google, Accenture, and Deloitte. Chitkara University makes it a point of honor to promote research, innovation and entrepreneurship through these partnerships.

Once your application has been accepted by Chitkara University, you will receive an admission letter and can then start the following steps.


3. Visa Application


Once your file has been accepted by Epitech and by Chitkara University, a good part of the process is done, but not all. The last step is to obtain your visa following the procedures indicated below.

Chitkara University is located 30 km from Chandigarh, which serves as the capital of the two neighboring states of Punjab and Haryana.


Chandigarh is one of the first planned cities in India and is internationally known for its urban design and architecture, particularly that of architect Le Corbusier.


It also boasts one of the highest per capita incomes in the country, and is reported to be India’s happiest and cleanest city.

schools.overview:
Chung-Ang University (CAU) is a private institution with more than 30,000 students and nearly 1,000 faculty members.

It consists of 10 undergraduate colleges and 16 graduate schools. It has two campuses, in Seoul and Anseong, Korea.


Chung-Ang has a 6% acceptance rate, which is lower than most other Korean universities, showing that the acceptance process is very rigorous. This proves how prestigious the university is.


Founded in 1916, Chung-Ang University has traversed Korea's modern history by upholding its ideal of "Justice and Truth."


Since then, CAU has played a leading role in the education of the nation's intellectuals.


Fully accredited by the Korean Ministry of Education, CAU offers a wide range of bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral programs, including a law school, international MBA programs, and a medical school. Through the dynamic activities of these schools, Chung-Ang University has gained a leading recognition in the country.


In addition, CAU is recognized as the best in the country in the fields of pharmacy, culture, and art education.


As a prestigious private institution, Chung-Ang University is fully committed to guiding its Korean and international students to envision their life goals and realize their maximum potential in an increasingly competitive global society.


Having become one of Korea's top institutions of higher education since its establishment 90 years ago, Chung-Ang University, joined by the Doosan Group (one of Korea's leading global business groups), is rapidly making strides to achieve its goal of becoming a prestigious academic institution admired by the world.
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier


You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

The nominated students approved by CAU will receive an email from CAU explaining the different procedures. You should fill out and submit an online application (link to come). The online application system has been designed for Google Chrome, although it should be compatible with other browsers. If you are not able to complete the online application using a different browser, we recommend that you complete the application using Internet Explorer.

Your host university may ask you the following documents:


For non-OECD students :


  • Transcripts (available on your intra)
  • Financial Proof: Official document IN ENGLISH provided by the bank. You are required to bring the original copy together with you and submit the document to the international office of CAU. We recommend that your financial statement clearly states the USD equivalent of your bank balance. It must show a minimum balance of 12,000 USD. The required amount is subject to change according to the actual living cost every year. If your financial statement is not in your name, you must attach a letter from the bank account holder, together with the document. Please make sure that he/she includes his/her relationship with you in the letter and states that he/she will be financially responsible for you during your stay at CAU.


For everyone :

  • Copy of Passport
  • Digital Passport-size Photo (Image File): Size: 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm. Color photograph of face, front view, on white background, taken within the past six months


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Acceptance letter


After reviewing your application, CAU will send you these three documents (mandatory to apply for a visa):

  • Certificate of (University) Business Registration
  • Certificate of Admission
  • Certificate of Exchange Student


3. Visa and ARC (more information here and here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.

If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2025 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; the university will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4.Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


If you choose to live in the dormitory on campus, a Tuberculosis (TB) Test result in English or Korean, taken within 4 weeks before the dormitory move-in date is also required. The test should include student’s name, hospital/clinic name, date of the test, and test results in English/Korean. The test can be conducted in Korea, and in the form of a skin test, blood test, or X-ray. You'll need to bring the original test result to the dormitory move-in.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/coree-du-sud


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5.Prepare your arrival


For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.

You can create a Korean bank account on campus.

Please install KakaoTalk before arriving and bring cash.


6.Campus life


The Office of International Affairs organizes a GLAM buddy program, staffed by local CAU student volunteers, to help international students adjust to live in Korea.

The Office of International Affairs is located on the 2nd Floor of Building 310 and is open every day.


Nearby restaurants: the canteen, Chipoleon, Back mas, Boumbata, Delacourt, etc.

There are many clubs at CAU: sports (soccer, tennis), martial arts, music, artistic and cultural activities (literature clubs, calligraphy workshops, etc.).


Many activities dedicated to international students are organized, like the Exchange student booth, where exchange students can talk about their country and home university.
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)


CAU provides on-campus orientation held the week before semester starts. Students are recommended to arrive at least a day before the orientation.


Students living on campus should arrive between the dormitory check in period. It is usually 2 to 3 days before the semester begins. The dormitory check in period will be announced later to accepted students via email. Any student arriving earlier than the official move-in date of the dormitory should find their own accommodation until they can move-in.


Students can apply for dormitory housing in June (subject to change). Students who wish to live in on-campus dormitory needs to apply through the online application page from a link provided by the Office of International Affairs (OIA), which will be sent when the dormitory dates are fixed. It is on a first-come, first-served basis. Please make sure to not miss the deadline as the dormitory availability is very limited and competitive.


Rooms have two or four beds. Please note that there are no kitchens, students usually eat out. Facilities include: LAN and Internet access, computer lab, phone line accessible in each room, TV with access to foreign TV channels, study rooms, a weight-training center, convenience stores.


Please note that there is a curfew at the dorms.


Cost per semester: about 760€ (without meal plan, which is mandatory). A deposit of about 65€ is needed.


Off-campus accommodation


If you'd rather live by yourself or choose who you live with, you can go for a shared apartment with roommates or an apartment of your own.
schools.courses:
Credits


You will need to obtain 30 local credits, equivalent to 60 ECTS credits.

Chung Ang University allows you to take up to 19 credits in a single semester; however, Epitech recommends taking 15 credits per semester.

The allocation of credits across semesters is flexible and can be tailored to individual student needs (e.g., 12+18 or 15+15), as long as the total accumulates to 30 credits.


Academic calendar


  • 1st semester: From September to late December
  • 2nd semester: From March to late June


You will have to choose your classes as follows:

  • Option 1: 3 computer classes, 1 Korean class, 1 elective class (non-computer)
  • Option 2: 4 computer classes and 1 Korean class
  • Computer classes must be at the 3rd and 4th year level
  • Business classes, Korean language, and Korean culture classes are at the 1st year level



Department and Courses


You will study on the Seoul campus. Courses at Chung Ang are delivered in English and are typically theoretical.

Most classes share the same time slot, and some are held in different buildings, making it difficult to attend multiple classes in a timely manner. Therefore, pay attention to the class schedule and location when registering.

The list of classes taught in English is only available one month before the start of each semester and is subject to change year to year.


Registration


As an exchange student, you will be given priority in course selection. Follow the university’s instructions each time new modules open to avoid late registration and limited availability.

Class registrations occur in three installments at the beginning of each semester. Most classes tend to fill up by the second round of course registration. It is advisable to register for all desired courses and drop any unsuitable ones during the course drop-out period, which is one month after registration.

Class registration is on a first come, first served basis, often occurs early in the morning (European time) and fills up quickly due to limited space. We recommend staying awake or waking up early to secure your preferred classes.


Courses to choose


Please refer to this link: Courses Offered in English (Spring 2024).

The selected computer science classes must be at the third- and fourth-year (Bachelor) level. You are considered at Bachelor level at Chung Ang.

You are permitted to take classes from the College of Software and the College of General Education.

Please note that the ratio of IT to non-IT classes for the year should be 2:1. For example, you might take six classes from the College of Software (Department of Computer Science or Department of Artificial Intelligence) and four non-IT classes from the College of General Education or other departments. Any classes from other departments will be counted as non-IT, and you may be denied access if you are not from the respective department. Therefore, you cannot take as many or more non-computer science classes as computer science classes.

You must register for only third- and fourth-year classes, some of which may have prerequisites. Please consult the syllabus before registering.

Due to the low number of third and fourth year classes in the first semester, you may also choose the following first and second year courses, which have been approved by Epitech:

  • AI Design
  • Logic Circuit
  • Computer Architecture
  • Formal Language and Automata
  • Mathematics
  • Multicore Programming
  • Computer Application
  • Computer Application Practice
  • Database Design
  • Mobile Programming


Course Format and Workload


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "15 hours of classes and 8 hours of work a week (can be less). Classes last three hours in general. Please note that some courses require a level in maths, but it's not insurmountable."


Important notes


  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.

  • You will receive an email from the partner university concerning a "scholarship". There are very few places, and you must make arrangements directly with the partner university.
  • Make sure to check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut. You'll be able to create a bank account in South Korea only when you have your ARC.
  • Useful apps: Coupang and Karrot (online shopping - equivalents of Amazon and Leboncoin), KakaoTalk and Google Translate/Papago/Deepl (communication), Baemin and Ubereats (food delivery), Uber, Naevar/Kakao maps because Google maps doesn't work (transport)
  • Use the Kakao Subway app, very useful for navigating Seoul’s subway. You can buy a metro card at a 7/11 or C&U (your student or bank card may also be used after about a month).
  • It is not compulsory to get a SIM card, as free wifi is often available in the streets. However, SIM cards provide access to more wifi, especially in the subway.
  • Korean people don't really cook and, rather, eat out a lot. You have options like restaurants (like pochas) and convenience stores which are open 24/7. Food is less expensive than in France. Typically, people share a few dishes.

schools.name: Cologne University of Applied Sciences
schools.overview:
The Cologne University of Applied Sciences (TH Köln) was founded in 1971.

The university has 11 faculties on 4 campuses. It welcomes around 21,300 students each year, including 3,500 international students from 120 countries. It offers its students:

  • 38 Bachelor programs
  • 30 Master programs
  • 10 international Masters

The university is also developing its international dimension with in particular 290 Erasmus partner universities.


Campus & Location

Epitech students will take the majority of their courses on the campus of Gummersbach, a small town of 53,000 inhabitants located in the heart of a wooded area, 55 km from the city of Cologne, or 1h10 by train.

The city of Cologne hosts the world's largest video game event, "GamesCom" every year in August. The companies IBM and Microsoft have established themselves in Cologne. Cologne is a dynamic city with around 90,000 students. It is also known for its Carnival which attracts many tourists every year.


Academic Structure

Epitech students will join the Faculty for Computer Science and Engineering Science in Gummersbach or Cologne. The latter has nearly 4,500 students, 20% of whom are international students, and brings together numerous institutes:

• Institute for Computer Science

• Institute for Electronic and Information Engineering

• Institute for Automation & Industrial IT

• Institute for Process Development, Production and Quality

• Institute for Technology and Materials and Applied Mathematics

• Institute for Business Sciences Gummersbach (BIG)

• Institute for Distance Learning and Further Education (IDF)

The classes are practical oriented. In fact, students have the opportunity to work in the form of projects.


Travel Advisory

For travel advice issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs for Germany, click here.

Insurance

For European students

The European Health Insurance Card (CEAM in French) is nominative and individual. This card certifies your rights to the Health Insurance in Europe. To obtain your card, log in to your Ameli account at least two months before your departure. It is free of charge and will be sent to your place within two weeks. You can also download it online.

For more information: https://www.ameli.fr/assure/droits-demarches/europe-international/protection-sociale-etranger/etudes-etranger
