You must register for a private health insurance to cover your full stay. Please check with your parents, bank, or any private insurance company for more information depending on the wanted coverage.

Students from previous years have told us that it is very difficult to find a rental alone. It is better to look for shared accomodation which is more available, especially since it is easier to integrate while being in shared housing.

schools.courses:
Academic Load

  • Number of credits to be earned per year: 45 ECTS (instead of 60 ECTS)
  • Number of credits to be earned per semester: 23 ECTS (instead of 30 ECTS)


Study Programmes Offered

The study programmes are offered cooperatively by the Faculties of Computer Science and Engineering, and Information and Communication Sciences at TH Köln and offer a diverse range of courses in the disciplines of Computer Science, Information Science and Data Science.

You can choose from different programmes, some of them being taught in German:


Gummersbach campus

  • Master in Digital Sciences
  • Specializations:
  • IT Management (ITM) – in German
  • Business Information Systems (BIS) – in English
  • Software Architecture (SAR) – in English
  • Master in Media Informatics– in German
  • Bachelor in Computer Science – in German
  • Bachelor in IT Management – in German
  • Bachelor in Media Informatics – in German
  • Bachelor in Business Information Systems – in German


Cologne campus

  • Master in Digital Sciences - Specialization: Data and Information Science (DIS) in English (Cologne Südstadt)
  • Bachelor in Code & Context – in German, partly English (Cologne Mülheim)


Special Note for Students Interested in Code & Context

Students who are interested in Code & Context should get in touch with us as far in advance as possible. There are several reasons:

  1. The programme is predominantly taught in German, but some courses are offered in English. Which specific courses those are can change from semester to semester, and there's room for negotiation if you contact us early enough.
  2. Most courses aren't taught over the course of a whole semester, but rather as a project block. This means that arrival and departure times might be different than expected – depending on the specific course selection.
  3. Students might not be able to gain a full semester's worth of ECTS with English courses alone. Depending on the workload required by ISCTE, they might have to take German-taught courses as well.


Language Requirements

  • You will have compulsory German lessons and get 5 credits.


Additional Notes

  • You can find more information here. about the modules offered in the programs. (Link placeholder as per original note)
  • Please note: the Gummersbach campus is several kilometers from the city of Cologne.
  • We remind you that attendance is compulsory, under penalty of exclusion from the university.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year. If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • EIP: Any Tech4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance them.

_____________________________________________________________________


CONCORDIA UNIVERSITY

Concordia is a large university located in Montreal, Quebec (Canada). It has two campuses approximately seven kilometers apart:

  • Sir George Williams Campus – located in downtown Montreal
  • Loyola Campus – located in a residential area in the west of the city

They are linked by a free shuttle service available to students, teachers and staff.

The university has about 40,000 students.


Academic Vision

The university claims to have always favored access to higher education and to give priority to the person. Its mandate is to offer:

  • Excellent study programs
  • High-caliber research activities
  • Courses geared to the needs of the population


Living in Montreal

Montreal is a very beautiful city. You are also free to enjoy the pleasures of the countryside by going to the Laurentians or the Eastern Townships. You can:

  • Go sailing
  • Go skiing
  • Or simply admire the beauty of the landscape

All of this is possible within an hour or two from downtown.

1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline).

If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

Documents you will need to take with you:

  • Certified copies of the bachelor's degree and the transcript of the bachelor
  • CAQ and proof of obtaining a study permit

Please note: upon arrival, you will be asked to provide official copies of all transcripts and diplomas obtained (i.e. your baccalaureate diploma and transcript) at the Office of the Registrar.


2. Visa

The steps must be taken at the green light from the University, because the procedures can take a long time. Check out updated information directly on the university's website.

Once you have your admission letter in hand, you must obtain:

  • The Quebec Acceptance Certificate for studies (CAQ), issued by the government of Quebec (At the expense of the student: 120$ CA) The application of the CAQ must be done online and takes approximately 4 weeks to be issued. The steps to apply for the CAQ:
  • Go to: www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/electronic-services/caq-electronic/index.html
  • Complete the online CAQ application
  • Print:
  • Declaration and commitment form (must be signed)
  • The personalized checklist
  • Review and ensure you have the appropriate support documents – remember to include ALL pages of your Offer of Admission.
  • We boldly recommend that you mail your application package with all supporting documents by express mail to the address indicated on the personalized checklist.


Note: Whether you apply online or mail your application, you must mail the required documents to MIFI's Montréal office, regardless of your current place of residence. Your application will not be considered until all supporting documents have been received, so don't delay. Processing time is 4 to 6 weeks!


The bank letter in French will be required for the CAQ request (see corresponding paragraph below). As an indication, the minimum amount requested in 2026 is 24 617CA $ . Please follow the sample letter available by clicking here. For the tuition fees, you will pay those of Epitech.


PLEASE NOTE: if the bank letter is not in your name but that of your parents, for example, you must attach the declaration of financial support (you must also attach it for the CAQ request): http://www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/publications/fr/etudes/D09.pdft


  • The study permit, issued by Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada – IRCC (Cost to be borne by the student: 150 $ CA + 85$ for biometrics fee). Once you have received the electronic version of your CAQ, immediately apply for your Study Permit. The application must be done online on the IRCC website. This study permit application automatically includes a visa or Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) at no additional cost.


  • Apply online: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/apply.html The IRCC website allows you to pay fees, apply for the study permit, and verify the status of your application.
  • Estimated process time: 12 weeks.
  • Guide: Guide 5269 – Présenter une demande de permis d’études de l‘extérieur du Canada - Canada.ca


  • Biometrics: Citizens of all countries except the United States and other minor exceptions have to give their biometrics to obtain a visa or permit.
  • You will receive an "instruction letter" in your MyCIC account with instructions to submit your biometrics at a collection service point.
  • More info: https://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/information/ou-fournir-donnees-biometriques.asp


  • Medical exam:
  • Students who reside or have resided for six months or more in the past year in certain countries need a medical exam by a IRCC-approved physician. You should allow at least one month for this process.
  • TRV or eTA:
  • Citizens of certain countries must obtain a temporary resident visa (TRV) or eTA. A TRV is placed in your passport; an eTA is linked electronically.
  • Designated learning institution number (PST):
  • On your study permit form (imm1294f), indicate the level of study as "University Baccalaureate" and include your institution's PST:
  • http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/etudier/etudier-etablissements-liste.asp
  • AVE (eTA) check:
  • Upon receiving your document, check your Electronic Travel Authorization (AVE) number. If it does not appear, request one online: http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/visiter/ave.asp
  • Processing time: 72 hours. Cost: $7.
  • Important: Start the CAQ application upon receiving your letter of admission. Delays may result in refusal of entry.


3. International Insurance

You can find here some information about the health and hospitalization insurance from Laval University for international students:

Enrolling in the health and hospitalization insurance plan for international students | Université Laval (ulaval.ca)


- Basic Social Protection

There is a specific agreement between France and Quebec for French nationals. It allows you to benefit from support for your health expenses (up to the equivalent of French student social security).


Before departure:

Upon arrival in Quebec:

  • Register with the RAMQ using the validated form.
  • You will access RAMQ healthcare, maternity coverage, and work-related protection via the CSST.
  • Important: Submit your RAMQ certificate to the Bureau du Registraire to avoid being billed for the university's insurance and late fees.


- Social Protection and Complementary Health

You must also take out international insurance covering medical/hospital expenses and repatriation.

schools.name: Conestoga College
schools.overview:
Conestoga is a leader in polytechnic education and one of Ontario's fastest growing colleges, delivering a full range of career-focused education, training and applied research programs. Labs equipped with the latest technology, project-based courses, field and clinical experiences, international exchange, applied research and co-op opportunities engage our students as they learn to connect theory, research and practice. Their focus on technology-enhanced learning through online and mobile technologies ensures that students are prepared to excel in our increasingly digital world.

  1. The “Technology Triangle” - comprising Kitchener, Waterloo, and Cambridge – nurtures a thriving technology scene. Many startups and innovation hubs have sprung up, earning the region the nickname “Silicon Valley of the North.”
  2. Kitchener hosts Canada’s largest Oktoberfest, reflecting its German heritage. Dating back to 1969, it has grown into a nine-day festival attracting over 700,000 attendees.
  3. Though separate cities, Kitchener and neighboring Waterloo are often jointly referred to as “Kitchener–Waterloo” or K-W. Their proximity and shared history as 19th-century German settlements fostered intertwined identities.

schools.overview:
California State University San Marcos (CSUSM) is part of the 23 California State University network.

San Marcos has quickly become the main educational center in northern San Diego County with modern buildings, advanced computer technology and state-of-the-art scientific laboratories.

San Marcos is located in the north of the San Diego region (in the heart of the southern California coastal region), 50 kilometers north of the city of San Diego and 150 kilometers south of Los Angeles. Just minutes from campus are the most beautiful deserts, the most beautiful mountains and the most beautiful beaches in California where you can swim, surf, hike, bike and ski. You can also easily reach the San Diego Zoo, Sea World, Disneyland and Hollywood.
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • Photocopy of passport / Residence permit (valid more than 6 months after return)
  • A letter from the bank (less than 3 months old) stipulating the amount of $16,500 or more for the full year format and for the deferred start. Unlike in previous years, the university now only accepts a bank letter for the entire stay. If the bank letter is made from a parent's bank account, an additional letter, written by the parent in question in English, must be provided attesting to the relationship and mentioning that the amount available may be used for your expenses for your academic stay in the United States.
  • Registration form.
  • The partner university will contact you directly for the choice of courses.
  • Certificate in English with your Tepitech score

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


2. Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.

1. Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to the university, you will receive an acceptance letter and an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2.Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3.Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4.Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3.Insurance and Health

Option 1: Subscribe to CSUSM insurance (more information here and here)

To meet the health insurance requirement, we suggest you purchase the CSU-sponsored health insurance which meets the Health Insurance Requirements.

Annual costs: $1788 (2026). Costs for 5 months: $745.


Option 2: Choose a private international insurance (more information here)

You must submit a petition to the Office of Global Education to approve your alternative policy. The petition must be accompanied by documentation clearly describing (in English) the policy benefits and restrictions.

Please note that alternate insurance plans must meet these requirements:

  • The medical benefit is unlimited, with a deductible of no more than $150.
  • The policy is valid as long as you are enrolled at CSUSM.
  • The repatriation benefit is at least $7,500.
  • The medical evacuation benefit is at least $10,000.
  • The policy provides equal benefits for men and women.
  • The policy includes prenatal (pregnancy) and maternity coverage at no extra cost.
  • The policy pays for pre-existing conditions after six months of continuous coverage. 


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


Additionally, CSUSM requires proof of vaccinations prior to course registration. Your vaccines must therefore be up to date before returning to school.

  • Tuberculosis (TB): You must provide a negative tuberculosis test, done within 6 months of entering the USA.
  • Measles, rubella and mumps (MMR): You must be vaccinated against measles, rubella and mumps before your arrival.
  • Hepatitis B (for those under 18): If you are under 18 during the orientation session, you must provide proof of your hepatitis B vaccination.

"Immunization form" which confirms the vaccination of students is to be provided to San Marcos once there but you must send it to us before on the intra for verification.

For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/conseils-par-pays-destination/etats-unis/

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.

Check out the university’s page for international students here.

Check the International Student Checklist provided by the university here.

Make your travel plans early. San Marcos is about 60 km north of the San Diego International Airport (SAN) and 160 km south of the Los Angeles International Airport (LAX). We strongly recommend that you arrive at the San Diego International Airport. If you have to change planes in the U.S., you must allow at least three hours to go through immigration and find your connecting flight. 

You must make your own travel arrangements from the airport to San Marcos.  We recommend that you arrive at the San Diego International Airport. If you arrive in San Diego, and you are living in homestay, then you may reserve airport transportation with the homestay company. You may also reserve an airport shuttle from Los Angeles International Airport, but this can cost about $200 and can take 2 hours to get to San Marcos. Flights from Los Angeles to San Diego cost between $50 - $150. You must reserve a shuttle or arrange your transportation before you leave your home country.  CSUSM does not provide airport transportation.

Shuttles at the airport include Supershuttle, Seabreezeshuttle, or Vango.


5. Campus life

The 120 hectare campus is located in San Marcos, a small, quiet community with many restaurants and shops.

The number of students per class is limited, which allows individualized instruction, and the classrooms and laboratories are new and equipped with the latest technology.

There are apartment-style university residences on campus, where life is buzzing with more than 80 clubs and organizations, art conferences, movies, concerts, and guest speakers.

Off-campus accommodation (more information here)

The San Marcos, Carlsbad, Escondido, Oceanside, and Vista communities near CSU San Marcos offer many reasonably priced apartments. The following sites may be useful in your search for off-campus housing, apartments and room rentals.

A 2 bedroom apartment is around $2,100 / month. It is cheaper to find a house / apartment for 3 or more (a 3-person apartment in a residence is about 2400$, or ~800$ per person compared to + 1000$ for two)

Price : $800- $900/month (may be subject to fluctuations). Breakfasts and dinners are included from Monday to Friday. Well located in San Marcos and the surrounding cities. Please note : registration fees and a deposit may be required.

- How are they selected?

Students submit an application with choices & personal details (e.g. willingness to live with young children/pets, any allergies, etc.) and then the host provider will provide them with options that the students can then rank. This is the ideal circumstance that students get choice. That said, when availability starts to decrease, it is possible that the homestay provider may place based on the preferences written in the application.

- Are they generally close to campus or would students need a car?

The general guideline is that students should be able to get from their host family to CSUSM campus in 45 minutes or less. This could mean walking, biking, or public transportation. So, a car is not necessary. That said, if a student plans to buy a car, they should mention this in their application as it could provide more host family options.

You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa. If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2025 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; Keimyung will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, ID checks, online shopping, etc.)

Dankook University provides on-campus dormitories for exchange/visiting students at each campus. Securing on-campus housing is assured for all incoming exchange students who apply on time. Although residing on campus is not mandatory, it's strongly recommended for reasons such as safety, community building, and cost-effectiveness.


Each room is furnished with 2 single beds, bedding, desks, chairs, wardrobes, a telephone, internet connection, and a private bathroom.


A variety of facilities are also available for students’ convenience such as a coin operated laundry room, restaurant, fitness center, convenience store, etc.

  • One semester: 1200€ (1 600 000KRW)
  • Two semesters: 3000€ (3 800 000KRW)

Although living on campus is recommended for reasons such as safety, building a sense of community, and cost-effectiveness, students are free to choose off-campus accommodation if they prefer. However, Dankook University does not arrange off-campus housing for students, nor does it endorse specific real estate agents or service providers.


Therefore, students who wish to secure off-campus accommodation must independently locate suitable housing and carefully review and understand any contracts or agreements they enter into.

schools.cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)


  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses


  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Visa: 126€
  • ARC: 20€
  • Insurance from university: 70€/month
  • Additional Insurance: 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage
  • Books and supplies: 60€
  • Beddings if you live in the dormitory, etc.


Estimated Monthly Budget


The local currency is the Won. 1 € = 1667,19 KRW (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


You should plan a budget of about 600€ a month, excluding rent.


Housing : 1200€ for one semester / 3000€ for two semesters


Food : maximum 300€ / meal at the cafeteria: 4000-8000KRW, about 3-5€ / dining out: 10000-20000KRW, about 6-12€ / a water bottle: 1000KRW, 0.6€


Transportation : Rechargeable T-money card: 35€ / In Seoul Metro: 0.7 to 1.20€ / Bus: 0.8 to 2€ / Monthly Climate card: 40€


Phone, internet : 12€ for unlimited 5G / Please note that if you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes 35G data in South Korea. / Former students (2024-2025) have recommended Chingu Mobile.


Leisure : 100€+ / movie ticket: 11000KRW, 6.5€ / admission to museum, temple or palace: 3000KRW, 1.8€


These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)


  • For scholarships at Dankook, click here
  • Your visa allows you to work in South Korea up to 20 hours a week, Monday to Friday, during your study stay. However, to be able to work, you must change your visa to an S3 on site. Please note that it is still very difficult for a foreigner who does not speak Korean to find a part-time job.
  • Make sure to check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut. You'll be able to create a bank account in South Korea only when you have your ARC.
  • Useful apps: Coupang and Karrot (online shopping - equivalents of Amazon and Leboncoin), KakaoTalk and Google Translate/Papago/Deepl (communication), Baemin and Ubereats (food delivery), Uber, Naevar/Kakao maps because Google maps doesn't work (transport)
  • Use the Kakao Subway app, very useful for navigating Seoul’s subway. You can buy a metro card at a 7/11 or C&U (your student or bank card may also be used after about a month).
  • It is not compulsory to get a SIM card, as free wifi is often available in the streets. However, SIM cards provide access to more wifi, especially in the subway.
  • Korean people don't really cook and, rather, eat out a lot. You have options like restaurants (like pochas) and convenience stores which are open 24/7. Food is less expensive than in France. Typically, people share a few dishes.

schools.name: De La Salle University
schools.overview: Founded in 1911, De La Salle University is an internationally recognized institution of higher learning with an established tradition of excellence and service. The University is a hub for higher education training, renowned for its academic excellence, prolific and pioneering research, and empowering community engagement. The University seeks to develop leadership quality in its students through a liberal Christian education. It adopted the Transformative Learning Framework, a path-breaking paradigm of instruction that is student-centered and geared towards the development of innovation scholars. Topnotch faculty members who are acknowledged experts in their respective fields engage students in multidisciplinary and collaborative research and other academic undertakings. La Salle is the only Philippine private university among the founding members of the ASEAN University Network (AUN), a prestigious organization composed of the top universities in the ASEAN, numbering from one to four in each member country. With over a century of being a leading resource for God and Country, DLSU invites no less than the best and the brightest students to be part of its global Lasallian network.

Application Process

STEP 1 : Nomination by the Home University


STEP 2 : Submission of application requirements

The nominated student emails the application documents to the DLSU exchange coordinator at the email address ovperi.exchange@dlsu.edu.ph, copies are furnished to the DLSU exchange coordinator (miriam.abayan@dlsu.edu.ph), on or before the Application Deadline.

To complete your application you may be asked the following documents:

  • DLSU Inbound Student Exchange Application Form
  • Official Transcript of Records / Academic Records
  • Tepitech
  • Copy of valid passport bio-page
  • Letter of recommendation
  • Copy of Enrollment Form (or list of subjects enrolled for the current semester at the home university)


STEP 3 : Issuance of Acceptance Letter

DLSU exchange coordinator will email the student's Acceptance Letter to the student, with a copy furnished to the student's Home University exchange coordinator


REMINDERS :

All documents MUST be in English (or translated into English)

Scan the documents and save as one file. Please use the filename: Inbound Application-Home University-LASTNAME (Example: Inbound Application-National University-CRUZ)


For Inbound students with scores lower than the required English Proficiency Score, they will be required ti take at least two (2) modules of English in the DLSU Center of English Speakers of Other Languages or CIESOL. Visit the CIESOL website Center for International English for Speakers of Other Languages (CIESOL) - De La Salle University for more information.


Admission and enrollment process

STEP 1 : Selection of courses using the Inbound Cross-Enrollment Form


STEP 2 : Enrollment

The DLSU university exchange coordinator will enroll the student at DLSU


STEP 3 : Issuance of the Enrollment Assessment Form (EAF)

The DLSU university exchange coordinator will email the EAF to the student. The EAF contains the following information: class list, class schedule, names of professors, and room assignments.


Admission and enrollment policies

  1. The DLSU International Center will only process complete applications and include all required documents.
  2. Course enlistment and enrollment must be done in coordination with the DLSU exchange coordinator
  3. While DLSU will make every effort to accomodate course requests, access to specific courses cannot be guarantee
  4. Students are advised to review prerequisites and restrictions during th application process to ensure suitability
  5. Students must ensure that all enrolled courses have been approved by their home university
  6. Once classes have started, dropping, withdrawal, or changing of courses are not allowed
  7. Inbound Students must comply with the rules and regulations of the DLSU Student Handbook
  8. Inbound Students are required to undergo and complete the Lasallian InSPIRE


Visa Requirements

De La Salle University (DLSU) considers all non-Filipinos as INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS. Before they are admitted to their program/degree, they must have a valid visa for study. List of valid visa accepted for study at De La Salle University The Philippine Bureau of Immigration (BI) mandates that foreign students who wish to study in the Philippines should have a valid visa for study (please refer to E.O. 285). BI consistently reminds schools and universities to admit only foreign students who have student visa or permit to study.

 Inbound Exchange Students (IES) who wish to enter and stay to study in the Philippines are required to secure a Special Study Permit (SSP). SSPs are issued in conjunction with or accompanied by a Temporary Visitor’s Visa (TVV) or 9A visa. SSP is valid for 3 months but can be extended co-terminus with the length of the course/program. Hence, IES must continuously update their authorized stay or extend their 9A Visa for the duration of their stay in the Philippines.


The International Center (IC), through its BI-accredited Liaison Officer (LO), assists IES in processing and filing the SSP application at the BI Student Visa Section. Approved SSP comes with the ACR I-Card required by the BI.


An ACR I-Card is a micro-based, credit card-sized, identification card issued to all registered aliens whose stay in the Philippines has exceeded 59 days. It also has an embedded computer chip with biometric security features capable of data management and can be updated electronically.


1. For international students who will use a Special Study Permit (SSP) or Student Visa, the International Center will handle the processing with the Bureau of Immigration. The international student needs to submit his/her Student Visa or SSP application documents and requirements (please refer to this link: www.dlsu.edu.ph/students/international/requirements/ visa-conversion-process.pdf) during the Confirmation Period before they can get the Clearance for Confirmation. Make sure to accomplish and submit also the Personal Data Sheet for international students.


SSP application requirements :

1.     Letter request addressed to the Commissioner from the representative of the petitioning school (provided by the Liaison Officer)

2.     Duly accomplished BI Consolidated Application Form or CGAF for the Student Visa and Special Study Permit. If the applicant is a minor, it shall be signed by the parent or the legal guardian

3.     Photocopy of passport bio-page and latest admission with valid authorized stay

4.     Certificate/Notice of Acceptance (NOA) issued by the host university (IC Liaison Officer shall request the certificate or NOA at the Office of University Registrar)

5.     2 pieces 2 inches by 2 inches (2x2) cloe up photo for CGAF; and

6.     Duly accomplished IC Application Form

7.     Official receipt of SSP payment

A foreign national whose stay will exceed 59 days should apply for 9A Visa extension with the BI Main Office or any BI offices.


SSP Fees

 

SSP New Application with 3 months validity and an ACR I-Card valid for 1 year

Php16,000

SSP Extension (another 3 months validity)

Php14,000


Note : SSP fee must be paid at DLSU Finance and Accounting Office. Fees are updated as of July 2025 and may change without prior notice.


2. For international students who will use other visa types (not SSP or Student Visa), submit the following documents in order to get the Clearance for Confirmation :

a. Accomplished Personal Data Sheet for International Students

b. Photocopy of the following (bring original for verification purposes):

i. Latest Visa / Visa stamp on passport;

ii. Passport Bio-page and stamps of latest departure and arrival in the Philippines;

iii. ACR I-Card (front and back) / SRRV Card / SIRV Card (whichever is applicable);

iv. Receipt of Annual Report for the current year

v. 1 pc. 2x2 colored picture

3. For international students with visa still under process at the Bureau of Immigration, they need to submit a Certificate of Pending Application from the Bureau of Immigration. 4. After getting the Clearance for Confirmation, the international student will submit this to the Office of Admissions and Scholarships during the scheduled Confirmation Period. 5. For inquiries, please contact our telephones numbers at (02)525-6727 (Direct) or (02)524-4611 Local 289. You may also email erio@dlsu.edu.ph.


Health Care

The University Clinic is staffed with three full-time physicians, two dentists (one full time and one part-time), two full-time nurses, and one full-time midwife working in shifts. It services the Lasallian community for first aid, consultations and starting medication for common ailments.

A Physical Fitness Center is also available in the university, which is located at the Enrique M. Razon Sports Center. Both faculty and students can avail of the services the center offers.

Several other medical and health centers are available near the campus. For a full listing, click here.

schools.overview:
Dublin City University (DCU) is a fairly young university, located on a 30-hectare campus north of the River Liffey. It’s a 15-minute drive from both Dublin Airport and the city center, where students can enjoy social and cultural activities while benefiting from the security and vitality of campus life.


University Overview


Established in 1980, DCU was initially founded on four specialties:

  • Business (DCU Business School)
  • Sciences (Faculty of Science & Health)
  • Engineering & IT (Faculty of Engineering & Computing)
  • Languages & Communication (Faculty of Humanities & Social Sciences)


With new ideas and a break from tradition, DCU quickly earned a reputation as an unconventional university.


Examples include:

  • One of the first universities to introduce internships as an integral part of its curriculum through the INTRA (Integrated Training) program
  • One of the first to offer interdisciplinary courses, allowing:
  • Science students to take business courses
  • Language & communication students to take computer science courses


School of Computing


The DCU School of Computing maintains close ties to industry and offers innovative programs to equip students with the personal and professional skills necessary for careers in Ireland and internationally.


Campus Life


DCU’s campus design and modern architecture make it a pleasant environment for study, combining academic excellence with an active student life.


Key infrastructure includes:


  • John & Aileen O'Reilly Library:
  • 1,200 seats
  • 18 group work rooms
  • 400 PCs
  • The Hub: Student association center
  • Sports complex
  • Helix Arts Center

schools.accomodation:
Campus life


It is difficult to find accommodation in Ireland!


Types of accommodation


International students are generally housed in Hampstead or College Park Apartments. About 200 rooms are reserved for international students who spend the whole year at DCU. As the number of rooms is limited, room allocation will therefore neither be automatic nor guaranteed, and you will need to apply quickly once admitted to DCU.

For more information: http://www.dcuaccommodation.ie/accommodation/dcu-international-students/how-do-i-apply.

Hampstead Apartments and College Park Apartments have around 60 apartments each. Each apartment consists of 4 to 5 single rooms (3 or 4 standard rooms and 1 larger room) with private bathroom and a common living room. Each room has a desk and internet access. A telephone (for incoming calls only) is available in each apartment.

The College Park Apartments also include around fifty "deluxe" rooms. These rooms are double and have direct internet access, telephone (for incoming calls only), TV and desk.


Costs

Here are the rates in effect for 2018/19:


Hampstead Apartments

The annual rent for a standard single room at Hampstead Apartments is € 5,729, payable in two installments (€ 2,978 to be paid in August & € 2,751 to be paid in January).


College Park Apartments

The annual rent for a standard single room at College Park Apartments is € 6,026, payable in two installments (€ 3,132 & € 2,893).

The amount for a large single room is € 6,211, payable in two installments (€ 3,229 in August & € 2,982 in January).


College Park Apartments (deluxe)

The annual rent for a deluxe double room at College Park Apartments is € 6,396, payable in two installments (€ 3,325 in August & € 3,071 in January).

If you are allocated a room, you will also be asked to pay a deposit of € 300 and an amount of € 330 to cover electricity and internet connection.

As for the rent, the first payment is to be made in June and the second in January.


How to Apply

You will need to apply on the DCU website http://www.dcuaccommodation.ie/home/apply-for-accomodation.412.html as soon as you receive your letter of admission (link opened in early March). The rooms will be allocated starting in July. Once your student number is received from DCU, contact the accommodation office to add this to your registration. You will be notified of the allocation of a room by mail and you must accept the offer within 2 weeks of receipt of the mail. If you are not assigned a room, your file will be placed on the waiting list in case of withdrawal. If you want to share an apartment with specific people, you can indicate this when you apply. There is no guarantee, however, that DCU will be able to satisfy all such requests.

Your room will be available from the Sunday preceding the orientation week (for insurance reasons, DCU cannot allow you to move in before). If you wish to arrive earlier, DCU can provide you with a list of hotels and hostels. Details regarding key collection will be sent to you before.


If you don’t get a room in one of these 2 residences, you can also apply for a room in the Shanowen Square Student Residence, which is a 5-minute walk away and whose quality and comfort are comparable to the 2 previous on: http://www.shanowensquare.com/


This residence has 86 rooms in 13 buildings. The apartments are made up of 3, 4 or 5 bedrooms. Each room has its own bathroom, a desk and an internet connection.


Costs (2012/2013 prices given for information):

Semester 1: €2300 – 15th September until the 26th January

Semester 2: €2100 – 3rd February until the 26th May

Does not include the price of the internet connection which is 150 € for the year.

A deposit of 350 € must be paid to secure your reservation.

A limited number of parking spaces is available for € 50 per semester.

Guideline for international students regarding finding off-campus accommodation: https://www.dcu.ie/students/accommodation-guidelines-international-students


Please note: It can be very difficult to find accommodation on your own in Dublin. You have to do it well in advance. Rates are variable. For practical and economic purposes, consider colocation.

You can find accommodation on the following sites:

http://www.daft.ie/, http://www.rent.ie/, http://campus.ie/surviving-college/student-accommodation, and www.collegecribs.ie.

We advise you to favor contact by telephone. It takes at least two to three weeks to find accommodation. And a lot of persistence!

Please note: If you rent accommodation to a private individual, you will certainly be asked to pay the first month's rent and a month's deposit in cash. You should plan this with your bank.

Beware of scams, they are present in all countries!

About the city


Barcelona is the capital city of the region of Catalonia in Spain and the country’s second most populated city after Madrid, with a population of 1.6 million. Its urban area extends beyond the administrative city limits with a population of around 4.7 million people, being the seventh most populous urban area in the European Union. It is the largest city on the Mediterranean Sea. Founded as a Roman city in the Middle Age and besieged several times during its history, Barcelona has a rich cultural heritage and is today an important cultural center and a major tourist destination.


The redevelopment of the city for the Olympic Games of 1992 created a new Barcelona open to the sea. The old docks were torn down, and tons of sand was brought to create miles of sandy beaches which now stretch from Barceloneta to the Port Olimpic. The city is probably nowadays the most important and vibrant city of the Mediterranean.


City of free, open culture, Barcelona is a modern, cosmopolitan and dynamic city that is proud of its diversity, figuring among the top European cities in quality of life rankings. It offers a wide range of cultural and tourist attractions, with nine of its buildings recognized as Human Heritage Sites by UNESCO. It is also one of the top 15 safest cities in the world and one of the ten most appealing cities in the world for launching a digital business.
schools.administrative:
1. For internships in a Spanish company


Please note: Spanish agreement to be signed once on site.

For those who wish to do an internship / work during the year, you can do it every Monday and Tuesday. It is an excellent opportunity that we encourage. During these two days there will be no scheduled courses so as not to prejudice those who decide to work. But on Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays you will have face-to-face courses on campus. You will have to attend, and will not be able to use work / internship as an excuse in case of absence.

Remember to inform EPITECH BARCELONA by email of the steps you take with companies, especially if you have already found an internship.

For information, for workers who are not resident for tax purposes (and you cannot be a tax resident if you spend less than 183 days in the territory during the calendar year - not academic - which will often be your case) the rate tax is high: 19% or 24%. Consider talking to companies about it so you don't have any surprises about your final net compensation.


2. Application for NIE (Numero de Identididad de Extranjero)


No visa is necessary for students who are nationals of a member state of the European Union or for students resident in one of the member states of the European Union and who hold a residence permit in that country.


Any foreigner wishing to reside in Spain for more than 3 months must request a NIE once arrived in Spain and within 30 days of entering the country.


Remember to start taking steps in April to obtain your NIE. You will need it to start working legally, even on an internship, and the steps to obtain it can take a long time being that it is difficult to obtain an appointment because of the saturation of the police stations in Barcelona.

You can start the process from France by making an appointment on the internet (try a few weeks in advance to obtain an appointment for the month of September).

One possibility is also to try without an appointment outside Barcelona, arriving and queuing from the earliest hour in the police stations of one of the following cities: Bellaterra, Sant Andreu de la Barca or Badalona.


3.Insurance and Health


For students wishing to do an internship, it is imperative to take out a complementary medical insurance covering accidents / hospitalization / repatriation AND civil liability in Spain before leaving. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

It is also recommended to apply for the European "Améli" insurance card on ameli.fr. The card is nominative and individual. This card certifies your rights to Health Insurance and allows you to pay for your care in Europe.


To obtain your card, log into your Ameli account at least two weeks before your departure (more information here).

  • You have no documents to provide.
  • This card is valid for one year. If, upon receipt of your card, your card indicates cover until December of the calendar year, please apply again in October / November of the fourth year so that it covers the rest of the school year (up to to June).
  • At the doctor, the pharmacist, and in public service hospitals, present your card or your provisional certificate.
  • Thanks to your European health insurance card, your medical expenses are covered under the same conditions as for the insured in the country that welcomes you.


It will also be imperative to obtain a Spanish social security number (ask us for precise explanations on site).


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4.CROUS scholarship (French students)


If you're going to Epitech Barcelona for your Tech4, you can have access to the CROUS scholarship.


5.Prepare your arrival


To find out more about daily life in Barcelona, visit the following website: BCN student.


For more information about current events on our campus and to get a sense of what it's like to study at EPITECH Barcelona, feel free to check out our Instagram page or Tiktok account.


To find out more on travel advice issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Spain, click here.


6.Campus life


The BDE organizes various activities for students throughout the year.


Team-building activities are a great tool to help students learn to work together, listen carefully, communicate clearly and think creatively. They also give our students the chance to get to know each other, build trust as a community and, best of all, have fun!


In order to do so and engage with the local ecosystem, at EPITECH Barcelona we organize plenty of fun events throughout the year:

BBQs on campus, Epitech Fun Days, Presentations and Spanish classes, Attendance to international fairs and events, etc.

Department and Courses


The fourth year abroad is a chance to hone the focus of your future career aspirations by specializing in a specific domain. Additionally, an IT expert must now be a professional capable of analysing the missions of his company. An IT expert is now at the heart of strategic development projects in his or her company and must be able to connect with and understand the professions that surround him.


In light of this, the programs at Epitech’s European campuses plunge you into the techniques you need to learn for a specific domain so that you can develop the skills necessary to transition seamlessly into the sector of your preference. Because IT is now interlaced with every aspect of society, Epitech chooses to form you as dual experts – IT of course, but also business, communication, and strategy.


The Barcelona Tek4 program mainly focuses on Innovation & Entrepreneurship in the IoT domain. The main goal of this course is to provide the Innovation and Entrepreneurship key points and main tools to our students, with the objective to be applied in a real innovation project during the year (also known as the Capstone Project).


Examples of modules

  • AIOT Fundamentals, prototyping and UX/UI
  • Introduction to hardware
  • Cloud and Smartcities and business developement
  • Deaplearning, Machine learning and digital Economy
  • Metaverse and autonomous car
  • LLM and 5G


Course format and Workload


The Capstone Project, the “pièce de la resistance” of the Campus Euro program, incorporates all the technical skills you learn with your projects over the course of the year with these “soft” skills to lend a completely new dimension to your year. The Capstone Project is the determining element in receiving your certificate.


Throughout the year, via a series of hands-on projects, you will develop just as many technical competencies related to your specialization as you will skills that intersect with the fields surrounding IT. Meanwhile, other technical courses will be developed on both semesters to enrich this innovation proposal, most of them related to the IoT domain, thanks to the relevant position of Barcelona’s ecosystem on this context. In addition to that, all the technical and transversal courses will be developed by a great team of experts and professionals in these areas of expertise.

The program is therefore centred on developing two strengths at once – technical and entrepreneurial, leading to the deliverance of an additional IoT certificate which will incontestably attest to your expertise.

schools.name: Epitech Cotonou
schools.overview:
Epitech vous accueille sur son campus de Cotonou pour une année d'immersion afin de mener des projets en lien avec la transformation digitale, la cybersécurité, les Big Data et l'IA dans les réalités africaines.

Le campus est situé au coeur de Cotonou.


La ville, le pays

Le Bénin est un pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest, qui s’étend sur 700 kilomètres de long, du fleuve Niger au nord, à la côte atlantique au sud. Le pays fait partie de la CEDEAO et de la Francophonie. Sa population s’estime à 11 496 140 habitants en 2018, d’après les statistiques de la Banque Mondiale.

Le pays depuis plusieurs décennies est un lieu d’alternances démocratiques sans violences notables, une situation atypique sur le continent. La capitale du Bénin s’appelle Porto-Novo et est située dans le sud du pays, près de la côte Atlantique. Cotonou est la capitale économique et la plus grade ville du Bénin avec 760 000 habitants lors du recensement de 2013. Elle abrite aussi de nombreux services gouvernementaux et diplomatiques.

Le Bénin offre un environnement propice à l'épanouissement personnel et professionnel des étudiants. Le pays dispose d'un système éducatif de qualité et d'une population accueillante.


Le Bénin est riche en histoire et en culture. Il offre une variété d'attractions touristiques, des sites historiques aux paysages naturels. Chaque année, environ 350 000 visiteurs viennent découvrir ce pays chaleureux et accueillant. De nombreux monuments et sites historiques témoignent de son passé glorieux. Parmi les plus populaires, on peut citer :

  • La Place de l'Amazone, à Cotonou, est un monument dédié à la reine Ghézo, une figure importante de l'histoire du Bénin.
  • Le monument aux dévoués, à Ouidah, commémore la traite négrière et le sacrifice des esclaves qui ont été vendus au Nouveau Monde.
  • Le Parc national de la Pendjari, situé dans le nord du pays, abrite une faune et une flore exceptionnelles, notamment des lions, des éléphants et des girafes.
  • La Porte du non-retour, à Ouidah, est le lieu où les esclaves étaient vendus aux négriers avant d'être embarqués vers le Nouveau Monde.
  • Les chutes de Tanougou et les chutes de Kota, situées dans le sud du pays, sont des cascades impressionnantes qui offrent une vue imprenable sur la nature.

L'écosystème béninois favorise également l'innovation et l'entrepreneuriat avec de nombreuses facilités. Le marché béninois et plus généralement ouest-africain est à la recherche d’experts en informatique capables de solutionner des problématiques spécifiques. Il y a donc beaucoup d’opportunités de carrière qui s’offrent aux jeunes dans ce secteur.
schools.administrative:
1. Le dossier de candidature

L’intégration de la Tech4 à Cotonou est surtout subordonnée à la motivation des étudiants. Si vous êtes intéressé.e par les sujets comme la transformation digitale, la cybersécurité et la big Data dans des contextes en pleine croissance et en plein développement comme l’Afrique, la Tech4 de Cotonou saura parfaitement répondre à vos attentes.

Le dossier de candidature à fournir comprend une copie du passeport en cours de validité.


2. Le visa

Les ressortissants des pays membres de la CEDEAO sont exemptés d'un titre de séjour pour leur séjour d'études au Bénin. Pour ceux qui ne bénéficient pas de cette exemption, une demande de visa en ligne devra être effectuée sur la plateforme officielle de demande de visa pour le Bénin.

Ce visa sera valable pour les trois premiers mois du séjour d’études. Les formalités pour l’obtention d’un visa d’une plus longue durée devront ensuite être effectuées auprès de la Direction de l'Émigration et de l'Immigration (gouv.bj).


3. Assurance et santé

Afin d'être entièrement couvert pour les soins médicaux, nous vous recommandons de souscrire une assurance internationale. Il est impératif que vous souscriviez une assurance qui couvre vos frais médicaux et hospitaliers, votre rapatriement et votre responsabilité civile. L'assurance internationale doit couvrir toute la durée de vos études dans le pays. Les frais d'assurance sont à la charge de chaque étudiant.

Pour souscrire une assurance internationale, le marché est assez ouvert. Veuillez cliquer ici pour plus d'informations.

Pour plus d'informations, vous pouvez consulter le dossier santé du pays à l'adresse suivante : https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/benin

Remarque : il est conseillé de s'inscrire sur le registre français établi hors de France et de se signaler au ministère des Affaires étrangères via la plateforme Ariane : https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. La vie sur le campus

Découvrez la présentation d'EPITECH Bénin par sa directrice ici.

Les étudiants peuvent pratiquer de nombreuses activités sportives et associatives (football, basket, MMA, self-défense).

Vous aurez l'opportunité de voyager à Lomé (Togo) et à Abidjan (Côte d'Ivoire). Ces voyages inclus dans le programme pédagogique vous permettront de rencontrer les entreprises qui façonnent la scène technologique de la région. En quatrième année, vous serez régulièrement invités à vous déplacer dans des villes éloignées de la capitale pour contribuer à des projets sociaux et promouvoir l'inclusion numérique. Au-delà des opportunités professionnelles, ces voyages vous feront découvrir la diversité culturelle et la richesse du patrimoine béninois et africain. Des visites de salons et d'entreprises locales sont également prévues pour vous immerger dans le tissu économique béninois.

Une cantine est disponible offrant des repas savoureux et équilibrés à des tarifs abordables, entre 500 (0,80 €) et 1500 FCFA (2,30 €).

Le campus dispose également d'une salle de repos et d'une salle de jeux vidéos.

Le campus est facilement accessible en transport. Des services sont à disposition des étudiants : zemidjan (taxi-motos), GoZem (divers services de transport, d'e-commerce, de livraison), Bénin Taxi, etc. Les frais de déplacement en taxi-moto sont d’environ 700 FCFA (1.10 €) pour l’aller-retour. Le port du casque à moto est obligatoire au Bénin. Il faudra également en acquérir un (prévoir environ 15 €). Un parking adapté et sécurisé est disponible pour les étudiants.

Les loyers pour un appartement 1 chambre + 1 salon équipé sont compris autour de 150 000 FCFA (230 €) à 250 000 FCFA (382 €) par mois.

Plusieurs options s'offrent à vous : résidences étudiantes, appartements partagés avec des colocataires, logement privé.

schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application. Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Filled out application form with your photo above.
  • Transcripts in English (transcripts will be provided by IAFF).
  • Study plan in English (Indicate the courses you have chosen and your motivation for attending this university as well as your objectives after this year of study).
  • 2 letters of recommendation (teacher, internship tutor).
  • Copy of passport (non-Taiwanese passport).
  • Tepitech score certificate downloadable from the intra.

To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.

2. Visa

Once you’ve submitted your application, FCU will review your documents and will issue an Acceptance Letter.

Students have mentioned it takes about a month.

Once you arrive in Taiwan, within 30 days, you must obtain a residence permit (ARC). You must provide the university with your proof of residence permit.

Please note:

  • If you hold a Chinese nationality, you will have to obtain and complete an additional document ‘Entry and Exit Permit Taiwan Republic of China’. This document will be sent to you by FCU.
  • As you are staying a full year at FCU, you must apply for Resident Visa at the Taipei representative office in France: http://www.roc-taiwan.org/fr_fr/post/8905.html
  • You must also complete the Health Report (Form B), that FCU will send you.
  • For your visa application, you will be asked to provide proof of financial resources (personal resources of at least 600 euros per month).

3. Insurance and Health

You must subscribe to the insurance provided by Feng Chia University according to the regulations for welcoming international students in Taiwan.

All international students are asked to complete a medical exam upon arrival in Taiwan. This includes in particular:

  • a chest X-ray for tuberculosis
  • a measles test
  • a rubella test

If you have been vaccinated against these last two diseases, you will need to provide a certificate of vaccination. For this exam, you will have to pay the sum of NT $750, or about 20 euros.

We also highly recommend you to purchase an international insurance in France that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

After holding ARCs for over six months, students are obliged to carry National Health Insurance (NHI). Fee: about about NT$749/month (20€).

For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/taiwan

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.

4. Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Taiwan, click here.

To familiarize yourself with the city of Taichung, please consult the information below:

  • http://en.fcu.edu.tw/wSite/lp?ctNode=45175&mp=3&idPath=19354_45172_45175
  • http://eng.taichung.gov.tw/mp.aspx?mp=49

5. Campus life

Every exchange student will be assigned 1–2 volunteer students. Our buddy group will help with airport pick-up, registration, and course selection. Airport pick-up service requires an extra fee.

Utilities fees are mandatory to pay for each semester (around 40 euros).
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation

FCU has on-campus accommodation but the dorms are not available for exchange students.


Off-campus accommodation

It is difficult to generalize because comfort and location criteria vary and affect rent prices but monthly rent for a room in a shared apartment can go between 7000NT to 8500NT (200-250€), plus a deposit fee of two months' rent. Make sure to ask for a contract in English. When you sign the lease, in addition to the first month's rent, the landlord will generally ask for two months' rent as a deposit. The deposit will be returned in full or deducted based on the condition of the accommodation at the time of departure. As photos are not always reliable, we suggest you not to sign a long-term lease before you arrive in Taiwan and inspect the accommodation in person. You can book an AirBnb or a hotel room two weeks before school to visit studios.

You can refer to this link for housing information in Taichung.

  1. Private room in an apartment with roommates

There are active Facebook groups. You should start looking during the summer (about 1 month/1 month and a half before back to school in September).

  1. Private accommodation

You can choose to live in an apartment of your own. Please note that in this case you probably won't have a kitchen in your studio. Some websites include Myroomabroad (English) or 591 (Chinese).

Credits

You will need to obtain 30 local credits per year; i.e., 15 per semester to validate 60 ECTS credits, not counting EIP credits.

Chinese courses represent 2-4 credits.


Academic calendar

The academic year at Feng Chia University lasts 2 semesters:

  • From the beginning of September to mid-January of the following year
  • Winter Vacation: mid January to mid-February
  • From mid-February to mid-June


Department and Courses

The lessons are given in English.

Our students have access to the Master program of Information Engineering and Computer Science (English program), as well as courses in the Department of Information Engineering and Computer Science.



Course format and Workload

Courses are generally theoretical and mathematically oriented.

Important notes 

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
schools.cost:
Financial overview (4th year at Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).

Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: 700-1000€ depending on the company and dates
  • Visa: about 60€
  • Administration fee: 90€ (student group insurance, internet, student card, airmail fee)
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the company and coverage
  • Medical examinations: about 20€
  • ARC (within thirty days after your arrival): 30€
  • NHI after living in Taiwan for over 6 months: 20€/month
  • Deposit: usually one or two months, so about 800€ depending on your rent

Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the New Taiwanese Dollar. 1 € = 35.84NTD or TWD (rate October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


Prices are indicative and may change.

Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • You need to have cash on hand because in Taiwan most payments are made by cash.
  • Make sure to check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut (no fees with at Cathay United Bank ATMs).
  • Make sure you pack thick clothes, as it is very humid in Taiwan and can be cold during the winter.
  • It rains a lot in Taiwan, make sure you have an umbrella with you at all times. You can wait until you get there to buy one, they're cheap and get stolen easily!
  • For transport, you have: the HSR (equivalent of TGV in France), the TRA (the local, slower trains), buses (can be less reliable), the MRT, and the bikes.
  • Taiwanese people eat out a lot and you have all sorts of options: night markets, local stalls, breakfast restaurants, buffets, convenience stores, Japanese chains, etc.
  • Scams are quite rare in Taiwan: prices are pretty reliable and it is very safe.

schools.name: Fontys University of Applied Sciences
schools.overview:
The Fontys University of Applied Sciences is a Dutch university with more than 44,500 students on several campuses.

It is a multicultural university welcoming around 100 nationalities each year.

Located in the south of the Netherlands, it is close to the borders of Germany and Belgium, in one of the most dynamic regions of Europe.

Fontys has 3 campuses, which are in the cities of:

  • Eindhoven
  • Tilburg
  • Venlo


Eindhoven Campus

The Eindhoven Campus has nearly 30,000 students and is made up of a group of buildings close to the central station.

During your year abroad, you will be studying at the Rachelsmolen Campus of Fontys University.

This campus was created some years ago and it is extending.

You will be able to benefit from the different facilities such as the sport center.

The Eindhoven campus is 5 minutes away from the city center.


Tilburg

Tilburg is a dynamic and cultural city, with many artistic events and festivals.


Venlo Campus

The Venlo campus is in a green area, 'De Wylderbeek', located near the banks of the 'Meuse'.

It is the tiniest campus of the Fontys University.

More than 70% of students in the Venlo campus are foreigners, making Venlo one of the most international campuses in the Netherlands.

GRIFFITH COLLEGE


Established in 1974, Griffith Dublin College has grown to be the 3rd largest independent university in Ireland, with over 9,000 students, including around 1,400 from 77 countries.


Its largest campus is located less than 1 km from the city center and St Stephen’s Green, in the southern part of Dublin.


With a solid international reputation, the university offers its students first-class training in various fields, as well as excellent structures and state-of-the-art equipment.


Faculties and Academic Highlights


Griffith Dublin College has five faculties, including one in computer science, which has bold ties to industry.


Ireland, and especially Dublin, is home to many large European IT companies, including:


  • Microsoft’s European operations center
  • Google’s European headquarters
  • Intel and Hewlett-Packard in Leixlip (west of Dublin)


Griffith College’s Faculty of Computer Science won the Robocode award (Java programming game) in 2008.


Student Life in Dublin


Dublin is a university city that attracts students from all over the world.


The city offers a wide range of cultural and leisure activities, including:

  • Museums
  • Theaters
  • Cinemas
  • Restaurants
  • Cafés


All of these are easily accessible from Griffith College.

schools.name: Hanze University of Applied Sciences
schools.overview:
The Hanze University of Applied Sciences in Groningen is the largest technical and professional university in the northern Netherlands.

It is located in Groningen, a student city, dynamic and steeped in history.

Hanze University of Applied Sciences has campuses in Groningen, Assen, Leeuwarden, and Amsterdam, with around 27,000 students.

The name Hanze UAS comes from the Hanseatic League (grouping of trading cities), which was essential for international commerce, trade, and cooperation.

You will take courses in English at the School of Communication, Media and Computer Science, which offers a creative and inspiring curriculum with companies, computer scientists, and over 500 international students from over 40 countries.

schools.name: Hartwick College
schools.overview:
Hartwick College is a private liberal arts college in Oneonta, New York. The institution's origin is rooted in the founding of Hartwick Seminary in 1797 through the will of John Christopher Hartwick.

In 1927, the Seminary moved to expand into a four-year college and was offered land by the city of Oneonta to move to its current location. The college has 1,103 undergraduate students from 30 states and 22 countries, 187 faculty members, and a student-faculty ratio of 11:1.
schools.administrative:
1. Application (work directly with Hartwick)

  • Official Transcripts in English (stamped & signed by home institution)
  • Passport copy (valid 6 months after the program end date)
  • Proof of Financial Support in English
  • Health Insurance is mandatory


2. Reception of the letter of acceptance from the partner university

Once you are admitted by the host university, Hartwick will send us your admission package with your acceptance letter & original documents for your visa. You can request a visa only after your application has been approved.


3. Visa

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website. You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1/Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to CSU LB, you will receive an acceptance letter and an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


4. Insurance and health

Option 1: insurance recommended by Hartwick

International students have the option of choosing health insurance plans that are recommended by Hartwick, or they can choose a health insurance provider from their home country. The International Student Office at Hartwick is happy to assist you in finding the perfect fit for your health insurance provider.


Option 2: private international insurance

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/conseils-par-pays-destination/etats-unis/


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.

Students will be in on-campus housing and must sign up for the meal plan (on-campus dining hall). There is a fee of 17,000 USD that covers housing and the meal plan for the entire year.


The residences with double occupancy that students are likely to be placed in are Saxton Hall, Wilder Hall, Holmes Hall, Smith Hall, Van Ess Hall, Oyaron House and Hilltop House. (As Leitzell Hall, The Townhouses and the Day Apartments are offered to full time Juniors and Seniors on priority). Students can certainly indicate their preference for which hall they would like to be in, and we can work with our Res Life to help process that request, though it may not always be guaranteed.


Each double occupancy dorm room includes 2 of the following: Bed, nightstand, desk, chair and dresse. Typically for bed sheets (and bed-in-a-bag), students can order these ahead of time through Dormify, or if they arrive on campus in time, we usually are able to go to Walmart to purchase these. However, we are starting to collaborate with our event coordinator to access rental sheets, and we can request that graduating or leaving students donate furniture such as desk lamps for Northeast Experience students to use moving forward.


All Northeast students get the All-Access plan which includes 3 meals per weekday and 2 meals per day (brunch and dinner) on Saturdays and Sundays.

schools.name: Heriot-Watt University
schools.overview:
IMPORTANT - ADDITIONAL PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS


Students must have a Tepitech score of at least 810 at the moment of the International Jury in order to be eligible for this destination


_____________________________________________________________________________


Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh is the eighth oldest university in the United Kingdom.


Its name refers to George Heriot, Minister of Finance for King James VI of Scotland in the 16th century, as well as to James Watt, famous inventor of the 18th century.


Since February 1, 2006, neurologist Susan Greenfield has been Chancellor, thereby confirming a real feminist tradition.


In fact, women were admitted to Heriot-Watt in 1869, more than 20 years ahead of other universities.


Heriot-Watt University has five different campuses:

  • Riccarton (main campus, just outside Edinburgh)
  • Galashiels (Scottish Borders)
  • Stromness (Orkney)
  • Dubai (Dubai Academic City)
  • Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia)


The university welcomes nearly 17,700 students each year (around 7,000 at Riccarton), less than half of whom are Scottish.


In fact, more than 11,000 students from around 150 countries are enrolled in the international program.


The campus is equipped with sports facilities, and hosts the training and training center for the Heart of Midlothian professional football team, which plays in the Scottish first division.


In 2017, Edinburgh was ranked 18th globally and 2nd nationally in the Best Student Cities ranking.


Here you will find a presentation made by the partner university.
