schools.name: Inha University
schools.overview:
Inha University is a private university located in Incheon, South Korea, traditionally known for research and education in engineering and physical science. The university was established by the first president of South Korea in 1954. The university is the result of cooperation between South Korea and the United States. It is ranked the 10th university in Korea and 4th in the field of Engineering and Science.


Inha University has 12 faculties in the fields of Natural Sciences, Engineering, Economics and Commerce, Business and Administration etc.


The campus is a half hour drive from Incheon International Airport and an hour and a half drive from Seoul.
schools.administrative:
1. Application Dossier


You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application. You will receive an email from Inha University to create your user session and apply online.


Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Photo (JPG format)
  • Letter of recommendation (use the template provided by Inha University)
  • Housing Application Form (use the template provided by Inha University)
  • Transcripts (available on intra)
  • Copy of passport
  • Financial proof (bank certificate of min. $8,000 for one year of study in Korea, the issuance day, account holder’s full name, balance of account, the signature of the bank) in English and a family relations certificate if you are not the holder of the bank account (translated in English)
  • Certificate of English level (Tepitech): available on intra
  • Certificate of Enrollment: available on intra


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Acceptance Letter

Once your application has been accepted by Inha University you will receive the necessary documents to apply for a visa:

  • Certificate of Admission
  • Letter of Acceptance
  • Certificate of Business Registration


3. Visa and ARC (more information here and here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.


If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2025 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; Keimyung will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4.Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open.


Please click here for more information.


When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


If you choose to live in the dormitory on campus, a Tuberculosis (TB) Test result in English or Korean, taken within 4 weeks before the dormitory move-in date is also required. The test should include student’s name, hospital/clinic name, date of the test, and test results in English/Korean. The test can be conducted in Korea, and in the form of a skin test, blood test, or X-ray. You'll need to bring the original test result to the dormitory move-in.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/coree-du-sud


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5.Prepare your arrival


For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.

Please install KakaoTalk before arriving and bring cash.


6.Campus Life


Free shuttles offered by Inha University from the airport to the university. (3 dates available)


Inha buddy program is intended to promote different cultures and exchange between international students and Korean students. Every year, Inha buddies and international students make great memories together and continue their friendship over the border. Applicants for buddy program should click check box when applying for exchange program through the online application system.


You will benefit from a Football Field, a Gym facility etc., Various monthly cultural activities organized by ISL (International Student Lounge), Internet and scanner [location: student building 5F] available at ISL office, Language exchange and tutoring program
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here and here)


1. Woongbijae

"Woongbijae" , Dormitory 1, a five-story building with one basement level and five aboveground, can accommodate up to 1,010 students. In addition to regular Inha students, Woongbijae houses exchange students, and is fully accessible for handicapped students. Woongbijae also offers LAN access ports, satellite TV reception, DID telephones, and a computer room. Other facilities include a cafeteria, a laundry room, a small lounge area, providing students with a comfortable living environment.


2. Biryongjae

Inha University opened the new Dormitory 'Biryongjae' , resembling an undulating wave, outwardly appearing a design of nature in 2006. Accommodating over 1,150 students, the new 13 story dormitory is equipped with various modern facilities such as LAN connection, digital satellite receivers, and DID telephones. The dormitory also provides students with access to a fitness room, Internet Cafe and various welfare facilities.


Dormitory fees (as of Fall 2025): approx. USD 950-1000 per semester (including a meal per day)


Condition: quadruple rooms or double rooms


Payment can be made in cash upon arrival


Off-campus accommodation (more information here)


You can choose to live in a share house with roommates or in a studio.


There are a number of housing options around the school area and in Incheon. International students who are not living in the dormitory are recommended to go and see firsthand any housing before signing a contract.


If you need a help with finding off campus housing for your stay in Korea, you can contact the housing agency at https://www.stay14.com.


You can choose to live in Seoul but please not that it'll take you an hour and a half to go to Inha University.


Tips:

  • There have been many cases of foreigners being the targets of inflated rental prices and scams in Seoul. So be very careful and if possible, get a Korean friend to help you in your search.
  • In March 2004, Korean laws were changed and it became illegal for landlords to force foreigners to pay more than three months rent in advance.
  • Check to see if you have to buy official waste disposal bags, which are sold in local through out stores. They come in different sizes, and recyclable material should be put out separately. Different neighborhoods have different recycling systems.

Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Your visa allows you to work in South Korea up to 20 hours a week, Monday to Friday, during your study stay. However, to be able to work, you must change your visa to an S3 on site. Please note that it is still very difficult for a foreigner who does not speak Korean to find a part-time job.

Credits

Each module consists of 200 in-class hours.

Total workload per semester: approximately 30 ECTS credits.


Academic calendar

  • Semester 1: early August to mid December
  • Semester 2: early February to late June


Department and Courses

At Inteli, courses are organized into a module-based system, where the curriculum is divided into thematic units called modules. Each module focuses on a specific subject or skill area, allowing students to build knowledge progressively throughout the academic year.

The academic year is divided into four quarters. In each quarter, students take one or more modules depending on their program. Flexibility: Students can choose between alternatives depending on their interests or seat availability.


Examples of modules in English in 2026:

1st quarter (Feb-Apr): Cloud Computing Services

2nd quarter (Apr-Jun): Hyperscalable Applications

2nd quarter (Apr-Jun): Business Intelligence Systems for Decision-Making

3rd quarter (Aug-Oct): Logic for Prediction with Artificial Intelligence

4th quarter (Oct-Dec): Integration, Management, and Big Data Analysis

Please note that the modules available in English vary each year.


Course format and workload

The PBL methodology includes guided self-study, research, and group work, effectively doubling the total workload.

In one semester, students complete two modules, each involving a project with a partner company. Modules are designed to combine theoretical learning with hands-on projects, enabling students to apply concepts in real-world scenarios. This modular system promotes focused learning, flexibility, and practical experience, supporting students in developing skills that are directly applicable to their future careers.

schools.name: Istanbul Technical University
schools.overview:
Founded in 1773, Istanbul Technical University is one of the oldest technical universities in the world.

It is a renowned university with a research center, connecting the past to the present and designing projects for the future.

In the heart of Istanbul, ITU offers numerous bachelor, master and doctorate degrees within its 13 faculties on 5 campuses.

It is one of the top three Turkish universities and has 369 laboratories and 13 research centers. With 23 engineering programs accredited by ABET, ITU is one of the world leaders.

Since its creation in 1773, the Technical University of Istanbul has managed to stay on the cutting edge by keeping abreast of global technological developments.

The university offers its students an educational environment that is steeped in tradition, yet open to the latest in educational techniques and settings.

The accommodation units are all located within 25 minutes by public transportation from the university.

Delta House:

This five story dormitory style house is located in the middle of the city center. The university is only a five minute walk away. The bottom floor of Delta House is occupied by a night club, so the first and second floors might sometimes be noisy. Step outside and within minutes you have everything you need within reach, including grocery stores, restaurants, shops, gyms, clubs and the central bus / train station.

schools.name: Keimyung University
schools.overview:
Keimyung University (abbreviated KMU) is located in Daegu, the 4th largest city in South Korea in terms of inhabitants (over 2.5 million).


Daegu is an hour and a half from Seoul by KTX (express train). It is a true college town.


KMU was founded in 1954 and has become one of the most prestigious private universities outside of Seoul.


It maintains very close relations with more than 226 universities and organizations in 46 countries around the world, which makes it the university with the most extensive international exchange network in the country.


It also welcomes 27,000 students from around the world on three different campuses:

  1. Seongseo – just over 1.8 km² (most courses, student residences, and the main library are located here)
  2. Daemyung – located in the city center
  3. Dongsan – also in the city center, home to Dongsan Hospital


The Seongseo library benefits from very sophisticated multimedia equipment.
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier


Once nominated by the Epitech IAFF team at Keimyung University, you will receive an email about the application process from Keimyung University.

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.


Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • ID photo (3.5 x 4.5 cm with a white background)
  • Passport color copy
  • Epitech transcripts in English
  • Recommendation letter in English
  • Medical form completed
  • Agreement on personal information form completed


*If you are a non-EU student, some additional documents may be requested for your Korean visa application. A bank certificate in English may be required and it must clearly state the USD equivalent of your bank balance showing a minimum of $20,000. The required amount is subject to change according to the actual cost of living each year.


If your financial statement is not in your name, you must attach a letter from the account holder, indicating their relationship to you and stating that they will be financially responsible for your stay at KMU.


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Acceptation by KMU


Your host university will review your application and then send you the three documents needed for the visa application:

  • Certificate of Business Registration
  • Certificate of Admission (COA)
  • Certificate of Exchange Student


3. Visa and ARC (more information here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.


If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2026 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€ (please note that the visa fee may change every 6 months)
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • You may be asked to send the following documents : valid passport, certificate of admission, business registration of the host university, completed visa application form, recent certificate of school record, verification of bank account balance, visa processing fee
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; Keimyung will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4.Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open.


Please click here for more information.


When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


If you choose to live in the dormitory on campus, a Tuberculosis (TB) Test result in English or Korean, taken within 4 weeks before the dormitory move-in date is also required. The test should include student’s name, hospital/clinic name, date of the test, and test results in English/Korean. The test can be conducted in Korea, and in the form of a skin test, blood test, or X-ray. You'll need to bring the original test result to the dormitory move-in.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/coree-du-sud

  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).

In Daegu

  • Metro: about 1€
  • Bus: about 1€

In Seoul

  • Metro: 0.7 to 1.20€
  • Bus: 0.8 to 2€

  • Please note that if you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes 35G data in South Korea.
  • Former students (2024-2025) have recommended Chingu Mobile.


Leisure : 100€+


These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Your visa allows you to work in South Korea up to 20 hours a week, Monday to Friday, during your study stay. However, to be able to work, you must change your visa to an S3 on site. Please note that it is still very difficult for a foreigner who does not speak Korean to find a part-time job. Student jobs through KMU include: English teacher, French teacher, Language advisory support.
  • Make sure to check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut. You'll be able to create a bank account in South Korea only when you have your ARC.
  • Useful apps: Coupang and Karrot (online shopping - equivalents of Amazon and Leboncoin), KakaoTalk and Google Translate/Papago/Deepl (communication), Baemin and Ubereats (food delivery), Uber, Naevar/Kakao maps because Google maps doesn't work (transport)
  • Use the Kakao Subway app, very useful for navigating Seoul’s subway. You can buy a metro card at a 7/11 or C&U (your student or bank card may also be used after about a month).
  • It is not compulsory to get a SIM card, as free wifi is often available in the streets. However, SIM cards provide access to more wifi, especially in the subway.
  • Korean people don't really cook and, rather, eat out a lot. You have options like restaurants (like pochas) and convenience stores which are open 24/7. Food is less expensive than in France. Typically, people share a few dishes.

schools.overview:
Keimyung University (abbreviated KMU) is located in Daegu, the 4th largest city in South Korea in terms of inhabitants (over 2.5 million).


Daegu is an hour and a half from Seoul by KTX (express train). It is a true college town.


KMU was founded in 1954 and has become one of the most prestigious private universities outside of Seoul.


It maintains very close relations with more than 226 universities and organizations in 46 countries around the world, which makes it the university with the most extensive international exchange network in the country.


It also welcomes 27,000 students from around the world on three different campuses:

  1. Seongseo – just over 1.8 km² (most courses, student residences, and the main library are located here)
  2. Daemyung – located in the city center
  3. Dongsan – also in the city center, home to Dongsan Hospital


The Seongseo library benefits from very sophisticated multimedia equipment.
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier


Once nominated by the Epitech IAFF team at Keimyung University, you will receive an email about the application process from Keimyung University.

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.


Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • ID photo (3.5 x 4.5 cm with a white background)

  • Passport copy
  • Epitech transcripts in English
  • Recommendation letter in English
  • Medical form completed
  • Agreement on personal information form completed


*If you are a non-EU student, some additional documents may be requested for your Korean visa application. A bank certificate in English may be required and it must clearly state the USD equivalent of your bank balance showing a minimum of $20,000. The required amount is subject to change according to the actual cost of living each year.


If your financial statement is not in your name, you must attach a letter from the account holder, indicating their relationship to you and stating that they will be financially responsible for your stay at KMU.


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Acceptation by KMU


Your host university will review your application and then send you the three documents needed for the visa application:

  • Certificate of Business Registration
  • Certificate of Admission (COA)
  • Certificate of Exchange Student


3. Visa and ARC (more information here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.


If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2025 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; Keimyung will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4.Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open.


Please click here for more information.


When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


If you choose to live in the dormitory on campus, a Tuberculosis (TB) Test result in English or Korean, taken within 4 weeks before the dormitory move-in date is also required. The test should include student’s name, hospital/clinic name, date of the test, and test results in English/Korean. The test can be conducted in Korea, and in the form of a skin test, blood test, or X-ray. You'll need to bring the original test result to the dormitory move-in.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/coree-du-sud


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.

You can create a Korean bank account at iMBank on campus.


Please install KakaoTalk before arriving and bring cash.

schools.name: Kent University - MSc
schools.overview:
IMPORTANT: ADDITIONAL PROGRAMM REQUIREMENTS

  • Tepitech 810 minimum at the moment of the International Jury

_______________________________________________________________________________


KENT UNIVERSITY

The University of Kent is a British university with one of its campuses located in Canterbury. The premises are filled with more than 11,000 students each year. The university has its own residence as well as amphitheaters, study rooms, computer rooms and resting areas. The campus has a typical "American" atmosphere.

The University of Kent has much to offer international students and almost 21% of the student body comes from outside the country (139 different countries).

The campus overlooks the city of Canterbury with large green spaces. It’s situated about two hours by train from London.

Kent University is a very popular university. Its former students are regularly in the top 20 of the best salaries for graduates. It was declared the best university in London and the South East by students in 2007.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on England, click here.

Feel free to read the University of Kent presentation (November 2019) here.
schools.administrative:
1) Application Dossier

Once the IAFF office has sent your nomination, the partner university will contact you directly by email to start your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see EMEA Teams channel for each application deadline).

If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.

To be completed with your Epitech bachelor campus administration during the registration period for Tech4 (usually in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


2) Visa

For European students, a valid passport/national ID card is sufficient to travel to Europe (exception for the UK).

For non-Europeans students or students with a non-European citizenship, please check the immigration office of the host country to check the visa process and fees.

Students in France can use this website: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/


3) Insurance

For European students

The European Health Insurance Card (CEAM in French) is nominative and individual. This card certifies your rights to the Health Insurance in Europe. To obtain your card, log in to your Ameli account at least two months before your departure. It is free of charge and will be sent to your place within two weeks. You can also download it online.

For more information: https://www.ameli.fr/assure/droits-demarches/europe-international/protection-sociale-etranger/etudes-etranger


For non-European students

You must register for a private health insurance to cover your full stay. Please check with your parents, bank, or any private insurance company for more information depending on the wanted coverage.

Please register via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ariane) platform to be aware of any news (terrorist attack, tsunami, earthquake…) in your host country for French citizens only: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html


Campus Life

We remind you that the electrical outlets are different from those in France: so don't forget your adapter! You can find some near the university, but the price is much higher than in France!

The surroundings of the campus are pleasant with lots of vegetation and a nice city center. Maybe it will interest some to know that the Internet connection is good on campus (~ 80 Mb/s).
schools.accomodation: You can find more information about housing on the Canterbury campus here.
schools.courses:
Number of Local Credits Recognized by EPITECH

120 UK credits (equivalent to 60 ECTS).


By studying at University of Kent, you can study in one of the three different programmes:

  • Advanced Computer Science (GPA 2.5)
  • Artificial Intelligence (GPA 2.5)
  • Cyber Security (GPA 3.5)

All the programs are taught in English, within the School of Computing.


The number of places is limited for each Masters. The University of Kent will be the sole decision-maker regarding your final admission to one of the three. You can list your choices in order of preference when you make your destination choices.


The classes are mainly composed of EPITECH but with some international and local students.

  • The first semester lasts from September 15 to mid-January (approximately).
  • The second ends around the beginning of June.


For the students deciding to take part in the programs awarding an MSc, you will work on a dissertation/project until September 15. However, Kent University allows you to return to France at the end of August for the return of Tek5.


Types of Diploma

By selecting one of the three programmes, you can obtain the diploma below:

  • Master of Science (MSc)
  • (number of local credits obtained: 180 local credits)


MSc is a diploma awarded in the UK, equivalent to two years of Master in France.

You will study a variety of modules for two semesters and you will study for a third semester, writing your dissertation/project until the beginning of September. Obtaining the thesis enables you to receive the Kent Double Diploma. The thesis (dissertation) is not counted in the Epitech credits.


Obtaining the double diploma requires handling a significant workload.


Please, read carefully the additional fees linked to each diploma offered at University of Kent on the Application Guide.


There is a fees difference between the two diplomas.

3 diplomas (please see the course list here):

  • MSc Advanced Computer Science
  • MSc Artificial Intelligence
  • MSc Cyber Security (certified by GCHQ, the UK government intelligence and security agency) – open since 2017-2018 (choose this course for a discovery in cyber sec) (image analysis module)


Notes

Attention: If you have already taken Java courses at EPITECH, you will not be able to take certain modules in Kent:

https://www.kent.ac.uk/computing/postgraduate

All students who obtain between 750 and 810 at the TOEIC EPITECH (tepitech) must include an English class in their course. Those who get 810 or more will be exempt.


Please note the following criteria:

  • High GPA required!
  • Higher GPA required for MSc Cyber Security
  • Tepitech at 810 recommended (if not, compulsory English module at Kent University)
  • Tepitech at 810 compulsory (to follow the MSc Cyber Security)


Attention: Presence in class compulsory, under penalty of exclusion from the university.

The course list is given to you for information purposes.

It can change from year to year. If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible.


EIP

Any Tech4 abroad involves an EIP!

Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance them.
schools.cost:
Estimated Budget of a Student On Site

  • Round trip train ticket or plane ticket: anything from 50 to 300 euros.
  • Insurance: You will need to pay an Immigration Health Surcharge to cover your access to the National Health Service (NHS), the fees are £470 as of now (early 2022).
  • Accommodations: See the school prices, which change from one year to the next.
  • Sports Center: Access to the sports center is not free. Prices vary depending on the activities. All students will be informed of these prices during the “freshers week,” where ALL associations (sports and others) will be present.
  • Food: €35 to €60 per week. Students will have the choice between Tesco, Sainsbury, and ASDA.
  • The cheapest is Tesco, right in the city center.
  • ASDA is a little behind the city, hence the need for a car.
  • Sainsbury is a large supermarket, easily accessible by bus.
  • The bus:
  • For the whole year: around €180 before October and €270 after October.
  • The bus is very economical in England, and is an excellent traditional means of transport.
  • Count approximately £3.50 for a day-long ticket.


These prices are for personal use only, so they may vary.

To get an idea of the cost of living, you can also find out more here.

Have a look at the application for the tuition fees to be paid.

For the cost related to the Brexit, please check here

schools.name: King Mongkut’s University of Technology Thonburi (KMUTT)
schools.overview:
King Mongkut's University of Technology (KMUTT)

King Mongkut's University of Technology (KMUTT) stands as a leading institution in Thailand, renowned for its innovation, research, and educational excellence in engineering, technology, and applied sciences. Established in 1960, KMUTT has evolved into a dynamic hub for academic and technological advancement, fostering a vibrant environment for learning and discovery.


The university's commitment to producing highly skilled graduates is reflected in its rigorous curriculum, state-of-the-art facilities, and bold industry partnerships. KMUTT's campuses, particularly the Bangmod campus, are equipped with cutting-edge laboratories and research centers, supporting groundbreaking work in fields such as renewable energy, robotics, biotechnology, and nanotechnology.

The university also places a bold emphasis on sustainable development and environmental stewardship, integrating these principles into both its operations and academic programs.


The diverse and multicultural student body at KMUTT benefits from a wide range of extracurricular activities, international exchange programs, and collaborative projects, enhancing their global perspective and professional readiness.

With a focus on innovation, KMUTT nurtures entrepreneurial spirit and critical thinking, preparing students to tackle complex challenges and contribute meaningfully to society.


Recognized globally, KMUTT continues to expand its influence through strategic partnerships with top-tier universities and research institutions worldwide. Its alumni network, comprising successful professionals and leaders across various industries, stands testament to the university's impactful education and its role in shaping the future of technology and industry.
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Photocopy of passport/residence permit (valid more than 6 months after return)
  • ID photo (JPEG, 1200x1400 px, plain blue background, white collared shirt only)
  • Resume
  • A medical certificate or a recommendation letter from a doctor or an authorized medical specialist certifying that you are physically and mentally able to take the course and/or are in good health.
  • Transcripts in English (available on intra)
  • Tepitech certificate (available on intra)
  • Copy of your highest diploma (baccalauréat)
  • Certificate of enrollment (available on intra)
  • A nomination letter (ask the IAFF team)
  • Application form (sent by KMUTT) / New-KMUTT Learning Agreement.docx
  • Recommendation letter from a supervisor of the home university


To be given to the campus administration:

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


A. Membership Registration : Go to the OneKMUTT registration page at https:// join.kmutt.ac.th/en/register to complete membership information.


There are 2 options to register :

1) Register via Main Website

Fill in you personnal details and receive a Confirmation Code via Email or Mobile (email is recommended to receive the confirmation code)

Click on "register to create a new account.


OR


2) Register via Google (gmail) or Facebook

Enter the OTP sent to your email

Click Confirm OTP Button

Set your password

Tick the checkbox to accept the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy

Click "Confirm Register" to complete the process


B. Log In: After verifying your email, log in to your account using your email address and password.

C. Access the Application Form

  • Select Program/Major
  • Click "Check Program Requirements"
  • Fill in all required information
  • Upload the necessary documents
  • Review and confirm your details before submitting

D. Track Application Status : After logging in, click on "Track Application Status" to monitor the progress of your application

E. See Additional Information: Click on "See additional information" to view more details about your application.

F. Monitor Updates and Notifications


2. Admission letter

Once KMUTT has reviewed your application file, you will receive your admission letter. This letter is proof that you have been officially accepted by KMUTT.


3. Visa


In France: getting an ED visa

The official letter of admission from KMUTTwill allow you to obtain a non-immigrant "ED" (Education) visa at the Embassy of Thailand in France. This visa is generally valid for 3 months. Check out the necessary documents for the application here.


Arrival in Thailand: Stay Permit PAD

Upon arrival in Thailand, an immigration officer will provide a permit stamp with the mentions "Admitted": Date of arrival and "Until": Date of validity (typically 3 months).

This "until" date might differ from your visa’s printed date, and it will determine when you must apply for an extension.


During your stay in Thailand: Extension

If staying longer than the "until" date, apply for an extension at the Immigration Office (Soi Suan Plu, next to Sathorn Road). You need to bring: 2000THB, your passport, and a letter from SIIT/Thammasat confirming study dates. The letter can take 1–2 weeks to prepare—request it early.


If you plan to leave Thailand: Re-entry permit

If you have a "1 entry" visa or an extension, and you plan to leave Thailand, you must apply for a re-entry permit or your visa/extension will be canceled. A single re-entry permit costs 500THB (about 15€) and a multiple one costs 1000THB (about 30€)


For the re-entry permit, you need to apply at the Immigration Office or airport. No letter is required for this permit. Upon return, you'll receive a new residence permit stamp with a new end date.


For security reasons, please inform your coordinator or KMUTT international relations department when you intend to leave the territory. If you have any problem with your passport or wish to renew your visa, re-enter the territory or other, the University Administration can help you to resolve these problems.


Note: It is advisable to register on the French registry established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform:

https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


Notes from a Previous Student (2022–2023):

  • Visa cost: ~75€
  • Can be done entirely online, depending on your embassy
  • Check visa confirmation carefully — One student had the wrong university listed and had to visit the embassy to correct it
  • Keep your acceptance letter (or a copy) with you when traveling to show at customs
  • COVID test may be required before meeting your buddy — do it within 1 week of arrival
  • International driver’s license is recommended — scooters are very helpful
  1. Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

Please bear in mind that air quality in Bangkok/Pathum Thani can be poor at times—bring masks/monitor AQI.

For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/thailande

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


Campus life

  • Sport facilities: sports hall, fitness center, tennis court, football field, and other sport equipment
  • Meals: the university has a huge canteen (and two small ones located close to the Residence Hall buildings) which is open every day from 6am to 8pm
  • Health service: Medical service for students and staff members (1st floor of Classroom building II CB2) as well as a Counseling and psychological service
  • Learning spaces: library, science learning space, computer center, etc.
  • Transportation to KMUTT: shuttle buses, bikes services
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here and here)

KMUTT has on-campus housing through a hotel-service based house called the KMUTT Heliconia House. It is a cozy, heartwarming and safe environment with a restaurant, a coffee shop, a bank and a post office located in the same building.

Rent goes from 250-350€/month. Resident students are required to pay a damage deposit of 6,000 Baht upon initial entry (330€). The dormitory will refund the deposit at the end of the rental period according to the contract, provided that the resident has returned the room, the room key tag, and the entrance door key tag in good condition.


Off-campus accommodation

  1. Private accommodation

Previous Epitech students have looked for appartments on their own via Facebook groups. The rent can go from 170 to 250€/month.


Additional Notes

  • Water and electricity charges: €25 – €70 (estimate)
  • It is advisable to buy a fan to reduce air conditioning costs
  • These residences generally don’t have kitchens — culturally, most eat outside
  • Meals in street restaurants often cost less than €1

Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).

Other Expenses

  • Insurance: 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage
  • Visa: 60€ in cash (valid for 90 days, compulsory for entry)

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

We advise you to plan a monthly budget of minimum 400€ for your expenses, rent excluded.


Estimated Cost

  • Housing: Around 300€ depending on the room you have if you choose the on-campus housing option
  • Food: €90 – €130 (3000-4500THB)
  • a meal costs about 3 to 4€
  • Transportation
  • Taxi: ~€10
  • Bus: ~€0.30 – €1 (from campus to Bangkok)
  • Approximately 50€/month if you travel a lot
  • Phone, internet

Recommended: Purchase local SIM card and internet plan on-site

→ Unlimited for 1 year, much cheaper than in France

→ All communication typically via 'Line' (not SMS or calls)

  • Leisure: 100€


These prices are indicative and may vary.

schools.name: Korea University Sejong Campus
schools.overview:
The University of Korea Sejong Campus is the second campus of the University of Korea. It was established in the city of Sejong in South Korea in 1980 and is 110 km from Seoul (accessible by train in 90 minutes). The Sejong campus is mainly oriented towards research.


The university has nearly 8,000 students spread over various faculties on a 428,871 m² campus.


It is a prestigious university, ranked 2nd nationally and 86th in 2018 in the QS World's University Ranking.

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

  • Completed application form (hand signed)
  • Copy of passport
  • Motivation letter in English
  • Certificate of education in English (to be requested from your campus administration)
  • Consent for the dissemination of your personal data (personal information consent form hand signed)
  • Transcripts in English (will be provided directly by Epitech IAFF team)
  • Academic recommendation letter (in English)
  • A photo (35mm x 45mm)

  • Bank certificate in English


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Receipt of the admission letter


After submitting your documents, you will receive an Offer Acceptance Form (OAF). Please review this OAF before the date given to the partner university.


Once your application has been accepted by KUS you will receive the necessary documents to apply for a visa:

  • Certificate of Admission (COA)
  • Letter of Acceptance (LOA)
  • Certificate of Business Registration (CBR)


3. Visa and ARC (more information here and here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.


If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2025 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; Keimyung will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, for ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open.


Please click here for more information.


When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


If you choose to live in the dormitory on campus, a Tuberculosis (TB) Test result in English or Korean, taken within 4 weeks before the dormitory move-in date is also required. The test should include student’s name, hospital/clinic name, date of the test, and test results in English/Korean. The test can be conducted in Korea, and in the form of a skin test, blood test, or X-ray. You'll need to bring the original test result to the dormitory move-in.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/coree-du-sud


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5.Prepare your arrival


For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.


Please install KakaoTalk before arriving and bring cash.

For the residents' convenience, there is a laundry service and self-serve coin laundry machines.

Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Your visa allows you to work in South Korea up to 20 hours a week, Monday to Friday, during your study stay. However, to be able to work, you must change your visa to an S3 on site. Please note that it is still very difficult for a foreigner who does not speak Korean to find a part-time job.

schools.overview:
Laurea University is the 4th largest university of applied sciences in Finland. It is divided into 7 clusters, all located in the agglomeration of the capital, Helsinki (25 min from Espoo by car), thus benefiting from the development and competitiveness of the region.

This university has been a pioneer vis-à-vis its new pedagogy and operating modes, such as "Learning by Developing," a method engaging students in a number of projects that the university organizes in collaboration with businesses and other organizations. The proximity to the business world is the real strength of their teaching. This contemporary and future-oriented outlook represents an innovative method that is a source of inspiration to the students.

Laurea has more than 8,000 students and 15 possible courses, including 11 taught in Finnish and 4 in English. Students who choose Laurea will have the opportunity to take the Business Information Technology cursus.

MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION (MAHE Fact Sheet.pdf)


In sixty years, Manipal Academy of Higher Education has become one of the most prestigious private universities in India. It also obtained the status of "deemed university" in 1993, which is a status of autonomy granted to the best performing institutions in the country.


About 20,000 students from 50 countries come to study here each year in one of the Academy’s 20 departments and institutes.


In terms of IT, Manipal has two main institutes: the Manipal Institute of Technology (ranked 6th best engineering college in India in 2011) and the Manipal Center for Information Science, which works closely with industrial giants such as Synopsis Inc, Philips, Whizchip, etc.


One of the Manipal Academy of Higher Education's priorities is to provide its students with the best possible infrastructure. Some of them, like the Innovation Center, serve as a true incubation center for industry and research. The campus also has other impressive infrastructures, notably for sports, of which the largest complex has 5 badminton courts, 4 squash courts, 3 tennis courts, one basketball court, a course track and gym equipment, not to mention the swimming pools as well as the surrounding football and cricket grounds.


The current CEO of Microsoft, Satya Nadella, and the former CEO of Nokia, Rajeev Suri, are all alumni of this university.

http://indianexpress.com/article/opinion/columns/mix-it-like-manipal/


For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here

The steps are also explained in the following document : Steps for Incoming International Student_Application_SII_EVISA

You will need to apply for a Study in India ID (SII ID) via the official website : Studying Abroad Made Easy with Study in India Program

  • You must register on the SII platform, fill in your personal details, and wait for your SII ID to be issued.

Once your Study in India ID process is complete, you can apply for the e-Student Visa online at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/tvoa.html. Be sure to use the official government (.gov.in) website.


All the steps for the visa application are also explained in this document : Study in India (SII ID) and E-Student Visa Application Process

  • Photocopy of your passport

  • Printed copy of the completed online form

  • University details
  • Recent bank statement


Once your visa is approved, you can be processed through the e-Visa counters upon arrival in India, where your biometrics will be taken. Please ensure that you read the information on both websites carefully and complete your applications accurately. Once you submit your visa application, the fee must be paid and will not be refunded, even if your application is rejected. The visa application process is individual and must be completed by each student personally.


Please feel free to check the brochure (Incoming Student Brochure)


Kindly apply for your Accomodation & Transport immediatly on receipt of your visa via https://oiac.manipal.edu/


Students are strongly adviced to stay on campus, but if you wish to stay off-campus, please ensure the property have duly registered Form C with e-FRRO.

The Chief Warden at the University will facilitate Form C online on the day of arrival. Report to the Chief Warden's office (room #105, Level 1, Edu building, MAHE). Soft copy of the complemented Form C will be emailed to the student.


2) If you are staying outside the campusGet the Form C done from the landlord of the apartment/hostel on the day of arrival

  • Visit the e-FFRO portal
  • Submit your application with the mentioned supporting documents (photograph, passport, visa, bonafide certificate (or proof of study), eligibility letter, Form C)
  • Keep a tab on your email for updates

  • Applicant must ensure to leave the country on/before the expiry of the RC/RP depsite of the visa validity period
  • Applicants should carry the RC/RP along with the passport for verification at the airport immigration desk


Upon your arrival:


If you Visa duration exceeds 180 days, students must then, within 14 days of your arrival in India, register with the Foreigners Registration Office (FRO) at the city police station. You will have to complete the e-FRRO registration and the College office will issue you a Bonafide certificate.

Students are advisable to report first to the Office of International Affairs & collaborations (OIAC), 3rd floor, Edu building, Manipal, with their passports for visa verification and to confirm their e-FRRO registration status.


Health and Insurance


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

IMPORTANT - ADDITIONAL PROGRAMME REQUIREMENTS

TOEFL iBT 90 (no lower than 21 on each section) or IELTS 6.5 (no lower than 6 in each section) or Duolingo 115

_________________________________________________________________________________


MCGILL UNIVERSITY

McGill University is an English-language public research university located in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. Founded in 1821 by royal charter granted by King George IV, the university bears the name of James McGill, a Scottish merchant whose bequest in 1813 formed the university's precursor, University of McGill College (or simply, McGill College); the name was officially changed to McGill University in 1885.

McGill's main campus is on the slope of Mount Royal in downtown Montreal in the borough of Ville-Marie, with a second campus situated in Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, 30 kilometres (19 mi) west of the main campus on Montreal Island, and a third francophone medical campus in Gatineau, Quebec. The university is one of two members of the Association of American Universities located outside the United States, alongside the University of Toronto, and is the only Canadian member of the Global University Leaders Forum (GULF) within the World Economic Forum.

McGill offers degrees and diplomas in over 300 fields of study, with the highest average entering grades of any Canadian university. Most students are enrolled in the six largest faculties: Arts, Science, Medicine, Education, Engineering, and Management.


McGill is the most internationally diverse of any medical-doctoral research university in Canada, with international students comprising over 30% of its student population and hailing from more than 150 countries. Additionally, over 41% of students are born outside of Canada. McGill is ranked among the world's top universities by major educational publications and has held the top position in the country for the past 17 years in the annual Maclean's Canadian university rankings.

McGill counts among its alumni and faculty:

  • 12 Nobel laureates and 147 Rhodes Scholars (the most of any university in Canada)
  • 16 billionaires
  • The current Prime Minister, and two former Prime Ministers of Canada
  • Two Governors General of Canada
  • 15 Justices of the Supreme Court of Canada
  • At least eight foreign leaders and more than 100 members of national legislatures
  • 8 Academy Award winners, 10 Grammy Award winners, 13+ Emmy Award winners, 4 Pulitzer Prize winners
  • 121 Olympians with over 35 Olympic medals


The inventors of the game of basketball, modern organized ice hockey, and the pioneers of gridiron football, as well as the founders of several major universities and colleges, are also graduates of McGill.


Notable researchers include Ernest Rutherford, who discovered the atomic nucleus and conducted his Nobel Prize–winning research on the nature of radioactivity while working as Professor of Experimental Physics at the university. Other notable inventions by McGillians include the world's first artificial cell, web search engine, and charge-coupled device, among others.

The application of the Quebec Acceptance Certificate for studies must be done online and it takes approximatively 4 weeks to be issued.


The steps to apply for the CAQ:

Once you have received your admission letter, follow these steps and apply online:

  • Go to www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/electronic-services/caq-electronic/index.html
  • Complete the online CAQ application
  • Print:
  • declaration and commitment form (must be signed) and
  • the personalized checklist
  • Review and ensure you have the appropriate support documents – remember to include ALL pages of your Offer of Admission.
  • We boldly recommend that you mail your application package with all supporting documents by express mail to the address indicated on the personalized checklist.


Note: Whether you apply online or mail your application, you must mail the required documents to MIFI's Montréal office, regardless of your current place of residence. Your application will not be considered until all supporting documents have been received, so don't delay. Processing time is 4 to 6 weeks!

The bank letter in French will be required for the CAQ request (see corresponding paragraph below). As an indication, the amount requested in 2026 is 24 617 $ CAD.

Please follow the sample letter available by clicking here. For the tuition fees, you will pay those of Epitech. There are additional tuition fees on the side of the partner university that you need to take into account: 4200€ for French and Belgian students and 36 100€ for non-French and non-Belgian students.


PLEASE NOTE: if the bank letter is not in your name but that of your parents, for example, you must attach the declaration of financial support (you must also attach it for the CAQ request):

http://www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/publications/fr/etudes/D09.pdf

  • the study permit, issued by Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada - IRCC (Cost to be borne by the student: 150 $ CA + 85$ for biometrics fee). Once you have received the electronic version of your CAQ, immediately apply for your Study Permit.


The application must be done online on the IRCC website.

This study permit application automatically includes a visa or Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) at no additional cost.


Apply online: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/apply.html


The IRCC website allow you to pay fees related to the study permit application, apply for the study permit, verify the status of your application.

The estimated time for the process is 12 weeks.


Go to this website to see the study permit application process:

Guide 5269 – Présenter une demande de permis d’études de l‘extérieur du Canada - Canada.ca


Citizens of all countries except the United States and other minor exceptions have to give their biometrics in order to obtain a visa or permit.


In the hours following submission of your online application, you will receive the 'instruction letter' in your MyCIC account with instructions to submit your biometrics at a collection service point. For more information, just click here:

https://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/information/ou-fournir-donnees-biometriques.asp


Students who reside or have resided for six months or more in the past year in certain countries need a medical exam by a IRCC-approved physician. You should allow at least one month for this process, and you are responsible for the cost of the exam. The embassy that handles your case will contact you and provide instructions as needed.

Citizens of certain countries must obtain a temporary resident visa (TRV) or electronic travel authorization (eTA) from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) to be able to enter Canada. The visa is placed directly in your passport, whereas the eTA is electronically linked to your passport. Your application for a study permit made outside Canada automatically includes a visa or an eTA at no additional cost.


You will receive confirmation that the study permit has been issued, and you will have to queue at the immigration services at your point of entry into Canada to collect the study permit.


Note: when applying for a study permit, you must indicate the number of the designated educational institution (PST) of your university in Canada. You can find the PST for your institution on the following page:

http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/etudier/etudier-etablissements-liste.asp


Regarding the study permit, on the form to be completed (imm1294f) and to be provided on the Quebec immigration site, you are asked the level of study at this university: put 'University Baccalaureate'.


Upon receipt of the document, there you will also thoroughly check your number of Electronic Travel Authorization (AVE) appeared in the second paragraph of the second page. If it does not appear, you will have to make the request online via the following site:http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/visiter/ave.asp


The request is processed in 72 hours and the cost is $7.

Please note: obtaining the CAQ and Study Permit takes several months, which is why it is essential to start applying for the CAQ upon receipt of the letter of admission. In the absence of these documents, entry to the territory may be refused.


3. International insurance

You can find here some information about the health and hospitalization insurance from Laval University for international students


Enrolling in the health and hospitalization insurance plan for international students | Université Laval (ulaval.ca)

  • Basic social protection
  • There is a specific agreement between France and Quebec for basic social protection on site for students of French nationality. This agreement allows you to benefit from on-site support for your health expenses (up to the equivalent of French student social security).
  • The file will be to be created upon receipt of acceptance at the host university. The process can take several months. Proof of your affiliation with student social security in France will be required.


Before departure:

You will need to ask your health insurance company for the necessary supporting documents and the SE 401-Q-106 form. This form, already completed by the international relations department, can be found in the media of your international relations intranet. You must then send it to the CPAM of your residence in order to have it signed. The validated form which will be returned to you by the CPAM will certify that you will be insured under the social security system in France and will allow your affiliation in Quebec. (NB: upon receipt of the form, remember to check the validity period which will have been indicated by the CPAM. Any form which will not cover you for the full duration of your stay will imply a renewal of the process during the year).


Upon arrival in Quebec:

You will need to register with the Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ) by submitting this form.

You will therefore be able to access RAMQ health care benefits and benefit from health and maternity insurance. In the event of a work accident or occupational disease, you will be covered by the Commission de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CSST).


Please note: it will be important to present the RAMQ affiliation certificate to the Bureau du Registraire. Otherwise, the university will be legally required to bill you for its own international health insurance. Late fees may also be imposed on you if you do not send the affiliation certificate before the deadline given to you.


Social protection and complementary health

  • You must also take out international insurance (covering your medical and hospital costs on site, as well as repatriation).
  • The market is quite open, among our privileged partners:
  • At ACS, contact Sandra Zagzag: szagzag@acs-ami.com / 01.40.47.91.02
  • At AVI, contact Afida Koucha: akoucha@avi-international.com / 01.44.63.51.32
  • At ISIS, contact Christine Barrat: christine.barrat@creassur-adc.com
  • At Worldpass, contact: grady@worldpass.fr / 09 71 09 10 15 (promo code: 9EPITECH – allows you to benefit from a tariff reduction of 20%)
  • Chez Chapka, contact: info@chapka.fr / 01 74 85 50 50 (promo code: EPITECH10)


Make it clear to each contact that you are a student at EPITECH and that you will benefit from a preferential rate.


Foreign students (other than French) must take out insurance for international students from McGill.


4. Help on arrival

If you arrive at Montréal-Trudeau airport in August (between August 4 and September 1), you can inquire about the "Accueil Plus" service, which allows you to reduce the waiting time for recover your study permit: http://www.accueilplus.ca/?lang=fr

schools.name: Monash University
schools.overview:
IMPORTANT: Additional Program Requirements


Students must have at least a 850 Tepitech score at the moment of the International Jury in order to be considered for this program.


Monash University was established in Melbourne, Australia in 1958.

It is Australia’s largest university with a total enrolment of 83,560 students, from which 27,403 are international students (based on 2018 full-year data).

Monash University is a member of Australia’s prestigious Group of Eight universities and is regularly ranked as one of the top universities in Australia, Asia, and the world.

Monash was ranked 84th best university in the world by The Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2019.

Monash offers a huge range of study options divided in 10 faculties across:

  • Five campuses in Australia
  • A campus in Malaysia
  • A study centre in Prato, Italy

Click here to have more information on the host country. The travaler's advice is issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs.
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier

Epitech international mobility coordinator will nominate you and create your application session for you on my.application, the online portal for students.

You will then have to complete and submit your application via this portal.

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Application form completed
  • Passport copy
  • Tepitech score certificate: minimum required 850 – ask the administrative assistant of your campus to send it to you
  • Transcripts in English: will be provided directly to the university by the IAFF team on my.application. Do not upload it yourself.

Later in the process, you will be required to create a study plan.

Your study plan is the list of units (or classes) you plan to study while on exchange/study abroad, and forms part of your application.

This is a key element on which Monash University emphasizes. You can be asked to justify your choices or show your capabilities.

After you apply, your application form will be assessed by Monash Abroad and the relevant faculties.

Follow the link to find out more about our approval process.

To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.

This information is subject to change by the partner university.

They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Reception of the letter of admission

Once your application has been accepted, you will receive your acceptance letter from Monash University.

The letter of acceptance is required by the Australian Immigration Office to proceed with your visa application.


3. Visa

When you receive your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), you can apply for a student visa (subclass 500), Non-Award Sector.

It is your responsibility to get your visa in a timely manner and to understand fully your obligations and responsibilities when applying for a student visa.

Students are advised not to book a non-refundable travel ticket until their visa has been issued.

https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500#Overview

The cost for this visa is AU$ 2000 (2025)


4. Insurance & Health

The mandatory Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is insurance to assist international students in meeting the costs of medical and hospital care that they may need while in Australia.

OSHC will also pay limited benefits for pharmaceuticals and ambulance services.

It is a condition of student visas that visa-length OSHC be purchased and maintained for the duration of that visa.

Failure to purchase OSHC will result in students being non-compliant with their student visa requirements.

Students will be required to purchase OSHC when accepting their offer for Exchange or Study Abroad.

More information will be provided with the offer.

The yearly cost for the OSHC is approximately AU$ 762.

We boldly encourage students to take out comprehensive travel insurance before they leave for Australia, as their OSHC will provide only basic medical and hospital cover whilst in Australia and does not cover any travel-related claims. The OSHC does not cover students while travelling to or from Australia, their personal belongings, or if they have an emergency and need to return home urgently.

All exchange students coming to Monash must have health insurance as required by the respective governments. Health insurance is organised by Monash, so please do not apply online.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform:

https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.

For more information, please check the country's health forms here: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/australie
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation:

Living in the halls of residence gives you the chance to become immersed in campus life at Monash and get to know local students. Monash Residential Services runs the halls of residence. Please check their website for more information.

Exchange students are given priority when applying for accommodation at the Clayton campus. Make sure you apply as early as possible as accommodation is not guaranteed to all students that apply.

There are two types:

  • the traditional dorms (Clayton residential village) with common areas (kitchen, bathrooms). All room types are single occupancy only. Prices: 353.15-426.65$/week depending on refurbishment and private bathroom (2026 prices) to live in the halls of residence; 342-353$/week for shared flats. A former student from Epitech chose this option in 2022-2023.
  • the studio apartments (Clayton urban community). Prices: 378-420$/week (2026 prices).

Monash Residential Services makes life in the halls fun with tons of social events and activities for you participate in. You can also take advantage of free TV, internet and Foxtel (pay-tv), and support programs. You may need to buy your own kitchen utensils and bedding.

Most Study Abroad and Exchange students apply to live on the Clayton campus, as availability at the other Australian campuses is limited. Clayton is 20km from the Melbourne CBD and provides lots of options for housing.

Off-campus accommodation:

Monash has a list of preferred off-campus accommodation providers which include:

  • Mannix College - 50 metres from the Clayton campus
  • Iglu South Yarra - 20km from the Clayton campus

Some other options that you could consider when looking for student and share accommodation include:

  • FlatmateFinders
  • Student Housing Australia
schools.courses:
Credits

You will have to validate 48 credits at Monash University over the year; i.e. 24 per semester to validate 60 ECTS.


Academic calendar

The language of instruction at Monash is English. Classes start at the end of July for the fall semester and at the beginning of March for the spring semester. We recommend you arrive in Australia at the beginning of July (especially for students with an on-campus residence) to be able to participate to the orientation week in mid-July.


Fall Semester/Semester 2 at Monash (2026)

  • Orientation: 20-24 Jul
  • Semester 2 teaching period: 27 Jul-18 Nov
  • Mid-semester break: 28 Sep-2 Oct
  • Exams: 2-18 Nov

Spring Semester/Semester 1 at Monash (2026)

  • Orientation: 23-27 Feb
  • Semester 1 teaching period: 2 Mar-26 Jun
  • Mid semester break: 6-10 Apr
  • Exams: 8-26 Jun


Department and courses

EPITECH’s students will be studying at the Faculty of Information Technology, taking 3rd year undergraduate units (courses). Most of the units will take place at the Clayton Campus.

Please refer to the list below for the units’ information (this list is subject to changes depending on unit’s availability):

  • Semester 2 = Fall semester
  • Semester 1 = Spring semester

Courses are subject to change every year but some examples that are possible:

  • Introduction to computer systems, networks and security
  • Introduction to programming (advanced)
  • Mobile application development
  • Usability
  • Software security
  • Computer architecture
  • IT strategy and governance
  • Software engineering: architecture and design
  • Parallel computing
  • Fundamentals of Algorithms
  • Databases
  • Modelling for data analysis
  • Business Intelligence and Data Warehouse
  • Data Analytics
  • Advanced Database Design
  • Leadership principles and practices - MGX3991 Caulfied Campus, Semester 2 (July to November)
  • Introduction to management - MGC1010 Clayton Campus, both semesters
  • IT Strategy and Governance - FIT3174, available for all study abroad students
  • Interntional Business - MGF2351 Caulfield Campus, both semesters


Course Format and Workload

The courses are probably going to be more theoretical than at Epitech.

Some units are assessed through continuous assessment and others through final exams. Everything is generally indicated in the unit and upon first reading.

Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
schools.cost:
Financial overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated in the application guide.
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: about 1200€
  • Insurance: 300-600€/year depending on the provider & coverage level
  • Visa: AU$ 2000 (2025)
