You should also prepare for your home set-up costs and allow AU$3,000-$5,000 to cover establishment expenses, such as bond payment, advance rent, furniture, and other household items. Some student apartments come fully furnished, but private rental accommodation are rarely furnished. Consider the deposit and one month’s rent paid in advance: AU$ 600–1,000 each.


Estimated weekly budget (source: Monash University, 2025)

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

You can also use this cost of living calculator in Australia.

Overall, a single international student requires approximately $30,000 – $45,000 for living expenses per year.

  • Housing

On campus: $330 to $399 per week

Shared rentals: $275 to $380 per week (Clayton area)

Homestay: $275 to $430 per week

Rental: $500 to $750 per week (Clayton area)

Phone and internet: $20 to $46 per week

Public transport: $25 to $50 per week

Car (after purchase): $150 to $300 per week

schools.name: Myongji University
schools.overview:
Myongji University, one of South Korea's dynamic institutions, combines academic excellence with a vibrant, forward-thinking campus culture. Established in 1948, it now operates two stunning campuses — one in Seoul, known for its rich cultural heritage, and the other in Yongin, set in a scenic, modern environment. This blend of traditional and contemporary makes Myongji a unique place to study.


The university offers a wide range of cutting-edge programs, particularly in fields like engineering, business, and the arts. It's also renowned for its international focus, with students from all over the world and bold global exchange partnerships, allowing students to experience diverse cultures and perspectives.


What truly sets Myongji apart is its focus on fostering innovation and creativity. With top-tier facilities, active student clubs, and opportunities to engage in projects that connect education with real-world impact, students are prepared to become future leaders.
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier


You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application. When officially nominated by Epitech, students will be working with the host university directly.


The host university may ask you the following documents:

  • Application Form
  • Official Academic Transcript in English (available on intra)
  • Certificate of enrollment in English
  • Copy of Identity page of passport
  • Recent Color Photo (JPG file)
  • Proof of English level (Tepitech available on intra)
  • Bank statement of a minimum of $16,000 (from you or your legal guardian + proof of parent/child relationship)
  • Copy of Certificate of travel insurance


Note: For students who checked the dormitory when submitting the application: the dormitory office will contact you separately for the payment.


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Acceptance letter


Once your application has been accepted by Myongji University, you will receive the necessary documents to apply for a visa:

  • Certificate of Admission
  • Letter of Acceptance
  • Certificate of Business Registration of Myongji University


You will receive those documents around late June / early July — please be patient!


3. Visa and ARC (more information here and here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.


If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2025 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; Keimyung will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4. Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open.


Please click here for more information.


When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/coree-du-sud


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5.Prepare your arrival


For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.


Information given by the host university's Office of International Affairs here and here.


Please install KakaoTalk before arriving and bring cash.


6.Campus life


The student activity fee is a mandatory fee for all incoming international exchange students, collected by the Office of International Affairs on behalf of student governing bodies such as the International Students Outreach Club and the International Students Association to support their activities.

  • Amount: Around 100,000 to 150,000 KRW (60-90€)
  • Payment method: via Flywire (an invoice will be sent before your arrival)


What is included:

  1. Two cultural/historical events (e.g., Everland, Lotte World, Han River Cruise, Taekwondo, Kimchi Class, etc.)
  2. Games Day – Transportation/lunch included (Fall Semester) OR World Food Festival (Spring Semester)
  3. Transportation to the immigration bureau for fingerprint registration
  4. Light refreshment on Closing Ceremony
  5. Welcome Kit on Orientation Day

schools.name: National Chung Cheng University
schools.overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

National Chung-Cheng University

Founded in 1986 following Taiwan's economic boom, Chung Cheng National University is located in Minxiong, Chiayi, in Chiayi County.

The university currently has 7 departments that can accommodate nearly 12,000 students.

Located 250 km south of Taipei, the campus has many green spaces, a lake, and modern buildings in various architectural styles.

"The University Emblem of National Chung Cheng University, designed by Professor Mao-sheng Su of National Normal University, was approved by the First Committee for Faculty Senate on October 18th, 1988. The design of the Emblem includes two parts: the two center characters of ‘Chung Cheng’ and the five pen-pointed tips which symbolize the five founding colleges of the university (College of Humanities, College of Science, College of Social Sciences, College of Engineering, and College of Management). It is our hope that CCU will reach her goal of providing higher education in the areas of humanities, social sciences, and science and technologies through the collaboration of the five colleges. The Emblem signifies the spirit of our perpetual striving for self-improvement."
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier (Warning Chinese passport)

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Fill out the application form online and upload all required documents through the CCU application system at: www026147.ccu.edu.tw/cc_afie_apply/
  • A recent identification photo (JPG format).
  • A copy of your transcripts in English (directly provided to the partner university by the AFFI team).
  • Letter of recommendation in English (ask your DPR).
  • Study plan of at least 300 words in either Chinese or English.
  • Copy of your passport (valid 6 months after the end of the stay).
  • Tepitech score certificate downloadable from the intra.

To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Visa

Once your acceptance letter has been received, you must begin the procedures for obtaining your visa.

You must apply for the 'Resident Visa' at the nearest Taiwan Overseas Representative Offices or Embassy in France.

http://www.roc-taiwan.org/fr_fr/post/8905.html

Students have mentioned it takes about a month.

Once on site, the partner university will guide you to apply for the 'Alien Resident Certificate (ARC)', which you need to obtain within 30 days after your arrival (more information here).


3. Insurance and Health

While applying for your visa, make sure to plan ahead for medical requirements, as you need multiple doses over several weeks (Japanese encephalitis, rabies, hepatitis).

You must subscribe to the insurance provided by the university according to the regulations for welcoming international students in Taiwan (more information here).

All international students are asked to complete a medical exam upon arrival in Taiwan. This includes in particular:

  • a chest X-ray for tuberculosis
  • a measles test
  • a rubella test

If you have been vaccinated against these last two diseases, you will need to provide a certificate of vaccination. For this exam, you will have to pay the sum of NT $750, or about 20 euros.

We also highly recommend you to purchase an international insurance in France that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

After holding ARCs for over six months, students are obliged to carry National Health Insurance (NHI). Fee: about about NT$749/month (20€).

For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/taiwan

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

Do not forget to contact your referent students on site.

Bring 5 passport photos.

Once there, go to the office of the College of Engineering on the ground floor which is in the “Innovation” building.

Please check the university's website here.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Taiwan, click here.


5. Campus life

CCU has a friendly environment for international students. It is well-instructed with facilities and living function. There are high quality sport facilities including indoors and outdoors swimming pool in Olympic standards, rock climbing fields, golf practice field, and other common sport facility.

The campus gives convenient living functions, such as post office, bookstore, a variety of cafeterias, convenient store, supermarket, glass store, computer hardware store and so on.

CCU is also an exemplary site of Green University: Since 2009, the “Green Campus Program” has been funded with the government support to build CCU as an exemplary site of a green campus through solar power.

CCU campus was ranked as the most beautiful university by Taiwan Yahoo website. Several movies and TV dramas were shot in the campus.

There will be events you can attend and be able to mingle with the other international student easily.

You also will be assigned a buddy, they will help you with administrative problems if you have any question but will also help you discover the surroundings of Chiayi and Taiwan.

Please note that the campus is away from the city center, and therefore it is difficult to get around with public transportation. There are only buses or taxis, but you can easily take one with Uber App or local one. The train station is a little far.

Taxi drivers do not speak a single word of English, like most of the Taiwanese population. You will have to be patient, but the people are very welcoming and are always ready to help you.

Student's feedback (2024-2025): "The university life is very diverse, with clubs for everything you can imagine: fire dancing, kung fu, kendo (Japanese martial art), and even a magic club. Taiwanese people are extremely kind, but what makes the experience even better is the campus life itself—you get to meet not only locals but also students from Russia, Indonesia, Korea, and many other countries. There are often events at the university, and the staff are very caring and responsive. Whenever I had a problem, it was handled quickly and kindly. You’re about two hours by train from a large city called Taichung."

schools.overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

National Taipei University

Established in 1949, National Taipei University (NTPU) was preceded by Taiwan Provincial College of Public Administration, Administrative Extension Program, Taiwan Provincial College of Law and Business, and College of Law and Business, Taiwan Provincial Chung-Hsin University. In 2000, the institution made the transition into becoming the National Taipei University, which includes both Taipei (Mingsheng and Chienkuo campuses) and Sanxia campuses.

In February of 2011, NTPU formed the “United Taipei University System” with National Taipei University of Technology and Taipei Medical University becoming the second university alliance system in Taiwan.

Over the past few decades, the NTPU has traditionally played a significant and pivotal role in educating and developing the mid- and high-level talents in the areas of law, business, public administration, as well as social sciences. To date, several hundred thousand NTPU alumni have established themselves in a large number and wide range of important and significant positions with tremendous success, both in the public sector and the private sector of the country. They all indeed act as the major leaders in the areas of their expertise, and have made significant contribution to the country.

Facing the rapid changes in the world and the competitive talents, we continue to advance toward “R&D-based teaching” and “practical application research”, and pursues new ideas of innovative research and development, driving practical innovation teaching and applying innovative teaching, so that students can learn in the learning process. At the same time, master the rapid pulse of society and become the pillar of the country in the future. We have Sanxia and Taipei Campus, own seven colleges including College of Law, College of Business, College of Public Affairs, College of Social Sciences, College of Humanities, College of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and International College of Sustainability Innovations, total eighteen departments, six independent research institutes, twenty-two master programs, nine doctoral programs, eight master’s in-service special programs and nine extension education programs.

  • for the MRT/bus, use your student card (you can recharge it at convenience stores), each travel has a 50% cut (normally a ride costs about 1€ or less)
  • free bike rides (U-bike) under 30 minutes, then it is about 50cents every thirty minutes.
  • Phone, internet; about 25-50€/month (but you will probably need to pay for a few months directly so be prepared)
  • companies like Chunghwa Telecom and Far East Stone have stores at the airport
  • Leisure: 100-180€

Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • You need to have cash on hand because in Taiwan most payments are made by cash.
  • Make sure to check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut (no fees with at Cathay United Bank ATMs).
  • Make sure you pack thick clothes, as it is very humid in Taiwan and can be cold during the winter.
  • It rains a lot in Taiwan, make sure you have an umbrella with you at all times. You can wait until you get there to buy one, they're cheap and get stolen easily!
  • For transport, you have: the HSR (equivalent of TGV in France), the TRA (the local, slower trains), buses (can be less reliable), the MRT, and the bikes. It is easy and inexpensive to travel within Taiwan (e.g., Kaohsiung, Taichung, Chiayi, Hualien) and also to fly to nearby countries such as Vietnam, Japan, South Korea, Thailand...
  • Taiwanese people eat out a lot and you have all sorts of options: night markets, local stalls, breakfast restaurants, buffets, convenience stores, Japanese chains, etc.
  • Scams are quite rare in Taiwan: prices are pretty reliable and it is very safe.
  • Former student's feedback (2024-2025): "Do not plan too much, enjoy the random choices, that is the best way to discover Taiwan. Must visit: Kaohsiung, Keelung, Tainan, Kenting. Okinawa Island isn’t far from Taiwan, may be a good trip in October / November with the weather."

schools.overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

National Taipei University of Technology - Taipei Tech

Founded in 1912, National Taipei University of Technology, commonly known as Taipei Tech, is a national public technology university that has nearly 13,000 students.


Taipei Tech was ranked 108 in Asia in 2019 by QS world University ranking, and is among the top 10 universities in Taiwan.

"Taipei Tech was founded at its present location in central Taipei in 1912, making it one of the first higher educational institutions in Taiwan. Though it then consisted of only three departments (Woodcraft, Metalworking, and Electrical Engineering), the institute pioneered industrial education in Taiwan. Within six years, mechanical engineering, applied chemistry, and civil engineering were added to the programs offered. Today, there are over thirteen thousand students at Taipei Tech, studying in seventy-nine programs at seven colleges: Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Engineering, Management, Design, Humanities and Social Sciences, and iFIRST (the Innovation of Frontier Institute of Research for Science and Technology). Taipei Tech has since produced some of the most influential entrepreneurs, leaders, educators, and researchers in the science and industrial fields, and is known as the birthplace for future entrepreneurs. The University is also engaged in a number of local and international projects related to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and University Social Responsibility (USR). Through making SDGs and USR the key initiatives of Taipei Tech’s medium- and long-term plans, we aim to be one of the world’s greenest, most inclusive, and socially-aware universities."

Once your acceptance letter has been received, you must begin the procedures for obtaining your visa.

You must apply for the 'Resident Visa' at the nearest Taiwan Overseas Representative Offices or Embassy in France.

http://www.roc-taiwan.org/fr_fr/post/8905.html

Students have mentioned it takes about a month.

On their side, NTUT will notify the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) to assist the process of visa application.

Once you arrive there, and within 30 days, you must obtain a residence permit (ARC). You must provide the university with your proof of residence permit (ARC). For more information, click here.

While applying for your visa, make sure to plan ahead for medical requirements, as you need multiple doses over several weeks (Japanese encephalitis, rabies, hepatitis).

You must subscribe to the insurance provided by the university according to the regulations for welcoming international students in Taiwan (more information here).


All international students are asked to complete a medical exam upon arrival in Taiwan. This includes in particular:

  • a chest X-ray for tuberculosis
  • a measles test
  • a rubella test

If you have been vaccinated against these last two diseases, you will need to provide a certificate of vaccination. For this exam, you will have to pay the sum of NT $750, or about 20 euros.


We also highly recommend you to purchase an international insurance in France that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.


To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

After holding ARCs for over six months, students are obliged to carry National Health Insurance (NHI). Fee: about about NT$749/month (20€).

On-campus accommodation

Taipei Tech dormitories include different residence halls that are situated on-campus and off-campus (for off-campus accommodation, see below).


The average traveling time from Taipei Tech off-campus dormitory to the campus is approximately 25-35 minutes via Taipei Metro.

Each room is equipped with a telephone, internet service and basic furniture like desk lamp, desk, chair, and wardrobe. The bed is about 192*95cm. Each room has air conditioner (Need to buy the air conditioner card for using the air conditioner - NTD500 (USD 17) per card) Dormitory fees must be paid at the beginning of each semester.

In general, all rooms are quad rooms.


Dormitory cost for Taipei Tech On-Campus Dormitory :

NTD 9,900 (around USD 320) per person for one semester, plus NTD 1,000 deposit, which will be refunded when checking out. Extra fees will be charged for using AC and laundry machines.


Dormitory costs for summer and winter breaks are charged separately. Please ask the dormitory administrator for rates.


Off-campus accommodation

It is difficult to generalize because comfort and location criteria vary and affect rent prices but monthly rent for a room in a shared apartment can go between 12000NT to 15000NT (335-420€) in Taipei. Make sure to ask for a contract in English. When you sign the lease, in addition to the first month's rent, the landlord will generally ask for two months' rent as a deposit. The deposit will be returned in full or deducted based on the condition of the accommodation at the time of departure. As photos are not always reliable, we suggest you not to sign a long-term lease before you arrive in Taiwan and inspect the accommodation in person. You can book an AirBnb or a hotel room two weeks before school to visit studios.


  • Taipei Tech dormitories off-campus

The average traveling time from Taipei Tech off-campus dormitory to the campus is approximately 25-35 minutes via Taipei Metro. The rooms are the same as the ones on-campus (see above).

NTD 9,000 (around USD 290) per person for one semester, plus NTD 1,000 deposit, which will be refunded when checking out. Extra fees will be charged for using AC and laundry machines.

NTD 7,850 (around USD 253) per person for one semester, plus NTD 1,000 deposit, which will be refunded when checking out. Extra fees will be charged for using AC and laundry machines.


Dormitory costs for summer and winter breaks are charged separately. Please ask the dormitory administrator for rates.

You can also go for co-living spaces like Borderless House and Banana Coliving.

schools.name: North Park University
schools.overview:
North Park University is a private Christian university in Chicago, Illinois. It was founded in 1891 by the Evangelical Covenant Church. It is located on Chicago's north side in the North Park community area and enrolls more than 2,600 undergraduate and graduate students.

Since the early days, the school has developed and changed in many ways. In 1958, North Park Junior College expanded from a two-year college into a four-year program, becoming North Park College. In 1997, the decision was made to change the name of the school again, and North Park University was born.

Though North Park still holds on to its Swedish American past and close ties with the Evangelical Covenant Church, it is now an intercultural institution focused on diversity.

North Park describes itself as a liberal arts university that is Christian, city-centered, and intercultural. North Park University is accredited by the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools and the Higher Learning Commission.

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1/Admission letter and DS 2019 form/I-20 form

Once you are admitted by the host university, North Park will send you your admission package with your acceptance letter and original document for your visa. You can request a visa only after your application has been approved.

When you receive an I-20 for an F-1 student visa or a DS-2019 for a J-1 exchange visa, you must take these forms to a U.S. Consulate to obtain the actual visa.


2/ Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/ Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.

You must have health insurance each semester you are enrolled at North Park. North Park University offers a comprehensive insurance plan for international students, which you are strongly encouraged to purchase.

schools.overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

Northwestern Polytechnical University (NPU)

Northwestern Polytechnical University (NPU), is a renowned university in science and technology in China and internationally, particularly in aeronautics (ranked 2nd in China in the field), astronautics, and maritime engineering. Founded in 1938 and oriented towards research, NPU is among the key universities to receive government support, helping it to develop into a leading institution. NPU has 16 faculties spread over 2 campuses; Youyi Campus and Chang’an Campus. NPU has established partnerships with world-renowned universities such as Harvard University, Pennsylvania State university, University of California, Berkeley, Yale university in the United States, Imperial College London, Queen Mary University of London, University of Oxford in England, INSA Lyon, UTC, Polytechnic School of the University of Nantes, University of Technology of Troyes in France, and many others.


School of Software and Microelectronics (SSM) is a computer science school within NPU. SSM is geared towards practice, innovation and entrepreneurship. It has set up the 'Students Innovation Valley', and invites experts and business mentors to supervise student projects. The School introduced computer courses from Carnegie Mellon University and has close collaboration with business. It won 2nd prize in the national education reform project entitled "The Innovation and Practice of International Engineering Software Talent Cultivation."

NPU is located in Xi’an, the ancient capital of 13 dynasties in Chinese history, and also the starting point of the "Silk Road" connecting East and West in the 2nd century BCE, making this city the cradle of Chinese civilization. Xi’an is thus rich with culture, and the Terracotta Army, located just west of the city, is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, often considered the 8th wonder of the world.

  • Equipped with a bed, air conditioning, bathroom, TV, shared fridge and a washing machine available to students.

  • Equipped with a bed, air conditioning, bathroom, TV, shared fridge and a washing machine available to students.

Some details:

For 11 months, count 9900 RMB (around €1300 to be paid at once at the start of the year, no monthly payment, only in cash or with a Chinese card — no foreign cards).

At this price, these are 2-person apartments with a bathroom, a kitchen (currently undeveloped, the university is studying solutions to remedy this) and 2 single bedrooms.

  • Housing (rent and utilities); about 300€

  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure: 100-200€

Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.

schools.overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

  • Only female students can apply


Ochanomizu University

Established as the Tokyo Women’s Normal School, Japan’s first national institution of higher education for women in 1875, the university will celebrate its 150th anniversary in 2025. Women aspiring to scholarship gathered here from all over the country. Ochanomizy University has blazed a path as a pioneer in women’s education, even when it was difficult for Japanese women to receive a higher education and play an active role in society. Their role has been to educate women who recognize and respect people from diverse backgrounds in gender, age, race, nationality, culture, religion, and social class among others, and help them create a better society. As its name implies, the Tokyo Women’s Normal School was established as an institution for educating future teachers. However, its graduates went on to pursue successful careers not only as educators but also as excellent researchers and leaders in fields including economics, industry, and the media

2. Receipt of the letter of acceptance from OIT

The result of selection will be sent to the partner university around two months after each application deadline.

The university will send you the official letter of acceptance.


3. Visa application & COE

Students who stay more than 90 days require a visa. In order to apply for a student visa, a COE (Certificate of Eligibility) is needed which will be issued by Immigration bureau in Japan. Usually, the process will take about 2 months before the original COE reaches you. Please be patient until receiving the COE.

The last step is to obtain your visa.

Upon your arrival:

  • During your immigration check after the first landing in Japan, show QR codes on the Visit Japan Web screen to an officer and answer questions.
  • Your COE will be exchanged with a “Residence Card” upon your entry into Japan.


4. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

Exchange students who will stay in Japan more than 3 months must join the National Health Insurance (NHI) regardless of the kind of insurance they may already have. This is a strict legal requirement in Japan. Once you arrive in Japan, you must complete the required procedures at your local city/ward office.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/japon

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5. Campus life

  • Facilities

The campus has different facilities. You will have access to the library, the auditorium, the cafeteria, language study commons, learning commons, and an international student plaza.


  • Activities

Ochanomizu University offers a wide range of activities. There are 49 official clubs (33 cultural activities and 16 sports clubs) in total.


  • International

There are more than 200 international students from 28 countries and regions.


The university offers different supports for international students:

Tutor systems: Graduate students will support new international students with their writing and speaking skills when they need to present an assignment for the classes.

Buddy system: International students will have a "buddy" assigned by their supervisors to help them in their daily life and academic matters.

Cultural events: The Center for International Education holds cultural events every semester which are free for the international students.

Volunteer activities: The affiliated schools have activities that allow international students to become teacher assistants to teach English.

Additional Programme Specifics

  • JLPT N2 level or equivalent

Osaka Institute of Technology

Osaka Institute of Technology (OIT) is a private university in Osaka, Japan. It started as “Kansai Engineering Technical School” in 1922, and it gained a 4-year university status and changed its name to “Osaka Institute of Technology” in 1949.

It has three campuses: the Omiya Campus is a main campus located in Asahi-ku, Osaka, the Umeda Campus is a new campus opened in 2017 in Downtown Osaka, and the Hirakata Campus is in Hirakata City on the foothill between Osaka and Kyoto.

In 2016, OIT was selected by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology’s Acceleration Program for University Education Rebuilding for its “quality assurance initiatives aimed at student learning outcomes upon graduation,” and received the highest praise (namely, an “S” evaluation) as a superb example of a pioneering model of adaptation to social demands […].

Currently OIT has four faculties: Engineering, Robotics and Design, Information Science and Technology, and Intellectual Property. In 2021 a fifth department was created in the Faculty of Information Science and Technology - the Department of Data Science.

schools.name: PUC Minas
schools.overview:
Founded in 1958, the Pontifícia Universidade Católica de Minas Gerais (in French "Pontifical Catholic University of Minas Gerais") is the largest private, not-for-profit university in the state and one of the five most prestigious universities in Brazil. Also known as PUC Minas, the latter is included in the country's network of Catholic institutions, as are PUC São Paulo and PUC Rio de Janeiro.

In 2010, PUC Minas was voted best private university in Brazil, which places it at the level of public establishments which are, qualitatively, the best in the country.

With more than 50 years of existence, PUC Minas University is a social and scientific reference in higher education, in addition to being recognized worldwide for the quality of its activities, especially in the field of research. Today, the internationalization of local culture and knowledge is a priority for the university, which always remains in harmony with its national roots.

In total, the university has 5 campuses in major regions of the state and brings together more than 62,528 students from all disciplines. The activities are concentrated on the main Belo Horizonte campus, which is itself divided into 3 units (unidades). Among these, you will have the opportunity to study at Coração Eucarístico and Barreiro. PUC Minas boldly recommends that international students choose the Coração Eucarístico unit, as this is the main unit. The latter has 21,350 students and the Barreiro unit has approximately 5,229 students.

PUC Minas has classrooms but also laboratories, libraries, museums, multimedia rooms, theaters, auditoriums, veterinary hospitals, a TV channel, and various other equipment that integrate theory and practice.

2. Visa

In France: student visa

Once your Application dossier has been accepted by PUC Minas, the last step is to obtain your student visa. Obtaining a visa is not automatic, each embassy being sovereign. If you are not a European citizen, please note that the procedure can take up to 3 months. Please note that a tourist visa CANNOT be changed into a student visa once in the country.

Make sure to follow the steps indicated on the Brazilian Embassy here.

You will need to provide proof of financial capacity to apply for a student visa for Brazil: for scholarship students, you'll need to hand out a certificate of scholarship where the monthly amount received must be indicated and give the duration of the scholarship. For non scholarship students, you need to give proof of your ability to support youself for the entire duration of the stay (pay slip, income tax sheet from parents).


Arrival in Brazil: residence permit

When you arrive in Brazil, you will have to go to the Federal Police to register and obtain a Residence Permit (Registro Nacional de Estrangeiro - RNE)


To do this, you must make an appointment in advance and present yourself in person with the requested documents.

You will also have to pay two taxes, the “Registro de Estrangeiros” — R$ 64.58 (around 24€) and the “Carteira de Estrangeiro de Primeira Via” — R$ 124.23 (around 45€)

You need to have a Tax Identification Number (Cadastro de Pessoas Fisicas - CPF) to be able to open a bank account or buy a phone in Brazil.

You can request it at an agency of the Banco do Brasil, Caixa Econômica Federal, or at Correios (Brazilian postal service).

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation

PUC Rio does not have university accommodation.


Off-campus accommodation

  • Host families (more information here)

PUC Rio University does not have university accommodation, but the accommodation service (housing-ccci@puc-rio.br) is responsible for placing students with host families. We strongly recommend that you choose this option which offers more guarantees than other types of accommodation.


Home-stays are located in the south zone of the city, the same as the university, within 30- 40 minutes distance from campus by city bus. However, many students opt to ride to university by bike.


The host families are recommended by CCCI and represent a wide range of incomes and situations. Each house has their specific rules in terms of hygiene, safety, cooking and bringing friends over etc.


Each student will sign a contract, pay the rent upfront during his/her stay, and abide by the house rules. The rent includes a private room with a bed, a fan, a weekly change of sheets and towels, access to light and gas and a Brazilian breakfast. Access to kitchen and laundry facilities is also included. Telephone use is to be arranged between the student and the family. Not all homes have internet available. Please be aware that some houses have only shared rooms (2 beds). In this case the rental per student will be lower than the private room.


Starting from the 2025-2 semester, the housing fee will be R$2.500,00 per month (400€), and if a meal option is available (lunch or dinner), the cost will be R$2.875,00 per month (455€).


Please note : due to very high demand, places with host families are limited and you must contact the university as soon as possible to apply, you must return the "accommodation form" to PUC Rio as soon as possible and apply online.


  • Student residences (more information here and here)

Some private companies provide housing for university students. Their infrastructure includes fully furnished rooms, communal areas, and study spaces.

Uliving and Co.Vivere are some of PUC Rio's partners.


  • Private accommodation

International students may prefer to rent an apartment near campus. You can check PUC-Rio Facebook groups. Prices are usually around US$1200- $1500 for a one-bedroom apartment in the neighborhoods near PUC-Rio, like Ipanema and Copacabana. The same type of apartment in Gávea, the neighborhood in which the university is located, costs around US$1.000. The student should be prepared to give a down payment in order to guarantee the apartment.

Private apartments are not usually recommended by CCCI. PUC-Rio is not responsible if the student decides to live in risky places (i.e.; slums) instead of living in an accommodation selected by the CCCI.


Important notes:

  • Please be careful when renting apartments found via the internet. We recommend working with apartment locators specialized in renting and selling real state;
  • Be sure that people with whom you will be sharing an apartment are trustful;
  • In Brazil, the lease contracts are usually performed at 3 years or 3 months. There are many fees, deposits and taxes to pay for formal rental contracts;
  • Request a receipt for each payment;
  • Inform your new address to PUC -Rio immediately after you move in.

Department and courses

Classes are taught in Portuguese.

  • Bachelor Ciência da Computação: http://www.puc-rio.br/ensinopesq/ccg/ciencia_computacao.html
  • Bachelor Sistemas de Informação: http://www.puc-rio.br/ensinopesq/ccg/sistemas_informacao.html

Optional Courses Taught in English

  • MEC 2015: SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION (3 credits)/ Mechanical Engineering

Introduction to system identification and state estimation: classes of models, applications, linear and nonlinear methods. Practical system identification: design of excitation signals, residual-based validation: metrics and correlation methods, structure selection. Linear system identification: batch and recursive least squares. State estimation: Kalman filter, receding-horizon approaches. Nonlinear system identification: benchmark problems, classical and machine learning based approaches.


  • ELE2602: Information Theory and Error Control Coding (3 credits) / Electronic Engineering

The objective of the course is to introduce the fundamentals of information theory and error control coding. The focus is on the concepts and algorithms required in several areas of communications engineering.


  • ADM 9983: Valuation and Real Options (4 credits) / Admin/Business

The objective is to introduce and provide the student with the concepts and tools required to price assets, value projects and firms and make capital budgeting decisions under uncertainty. We will discuss how risk analysis and simulation models can be of help in the investment decision, and introduce the concept of real option valuation.


  • ADM 9986: ONLINE AND MOBILE MARKETING (4 credits) / Admin/Business

The objective of this course is to introduce students to the concepts and practices involved in a myriad of different Internet Marketing techniques. The goal is to put students in contact with theory and real world Internet applications. Students will explore the key building blocks of the Web and the many ways it can be used as an effective Marketing tool or media. Upon completing this course, students should have a fairly comprehensive knowledge of Internet Marketing and related techniques, with a deep appreciation of their applications and limitations.


  • ADM 9981 MARKETING STRATEGIES THROUGH CONSUMER BEHAVIOR (4 credits) / Admin/Business

Marketing strategies decisions from a consumer behavior approach. Basic determinants of consumer behavior. The roles of marketing as influence on consumer buying and decision making. Impact of consumer behavior on marketing.


  • ADM 998: International Negotiation (4 credits) / Admin/Business

This course is designed to improve your understanding of and skills in international negotiations. After an introduction to the fundamental principles of bargaining and negotiation (including the definition of negotiation, what is negotiable, the golden rule of negotiation, and the role of communication media in negotiations), the course will focus on the essential elements of international negotiations.


  • ADM 9976: INTRODUCTION TO STRATEGY IN A GLOBALIZED WORLD: Global Strategic Management (GSM) (4 credits) / Admin/Business

Basic concepts and tools for strategic management from a global perspective. Assessing and ensuring strategic fit considering global opportunities and challenges. Shift in paradigm of multinational strategies from national differentiation to globalization. International alliances: focus on joint ventures.


  • ADM 2778: International Marketing (3 credits) / Admin/Business

Concepts and practices related to international marketing. Potential markets and identification of opportunities. Analysis of the external environments: economics, legal, cultural and social. International market entry strategies. International marketing strategies: product, services, price, distribution and promotion.


  • ADM 2675: Intermediate Corporate Finance and Governance (3 credits)/ Admin/Business

Corporate capital structure, leverage and debt maturity. Investment policy. Dividend policy. Financial restrictions. Corporate governance and agency theory, private benefits of control, corporate governance mechanisms (ownership structure, board of directors, compensation, takeover market). Investor protection: shareholder protection and creditors rights, and national institutions.


  • ADM 2466: Strategy in changing environment (3 credits) / Admin/Business

This course addresses firm’s strategic responses to the changing environment. As social, environmental, economic and technological changes impacts business as usual, firms must develop capabilities to respond, adapt and compete successfully. The course will bring integrated analyses of dynamic capabilities, managerial capabilities and adaptation literature applied to contexts of environmental uncertainty and turbulence. Classes will include readings, case studies and discussions to provide deeper understanding of the theoretical frameworks and the applied situations.


  • EMP9505: ENTREPRENEURIAL MINDSET (4 credits) / Admin/Business

The course addresses a selected collection of themes that are crucial for the creation and development of a startup, among which one can find group behavior and performance, leadership, motivation and interpersonal influence, storytelling, gamification and design thinking. Through a series of interactive classes, lectures and exercises students develop competencies in organizational design, human resources management, leadership and organizational behavior in the context of an internal or external new venture.


  • HIS 9827: Brazilian History: an introduction (4 credits)/ CONTEXTE LOCAL

This course introduces students to Brazilian History, focusing especially on the social, economic and political changes which took place after the consolidation of Brazilian Republic. Our goal is providing an overview to a variety of topics to understand the historical roots of Brazil today.


  • ELE2765: Adaptive and Array Signal Processing (3 credits) / Electronic Engineering

The objective of the course is to introduce the fundamentals of adaptive and array signal processing using linear algebra, optimisation and intuition. The main focus is on filtering and estimation techniques and beamforming and direction finding methods and their application in several areas of electrical engineering (communications, control, time-series analysis, sensing, defence systems, etc).


  • ELE2707: Stochastic Processes (3 credits) / Math

This course introduces the fundamentals of probability theory, random variables and stochastic processes, and presents the main tools used in the area along with examples often found in electrical engineering and related areas.

schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation

RMIT does not offer on-campus accommodation.


Off-campus accommodation

You can find information about off-campus accommodation in Melbourne here. RMIT can help you find a place by putting you in contact with a student welfare advisor.


1. Purpose-built student accommodation

These apartment complexes owned by private companies such as UniLodge or Iglu are designed for students and meet RMIT’s quality standards. The properties provide a friendly, community environment with easy access to university supports.  

A variety of furnished rooms are available, from studios to shared apartments, with excellent communal facilities. Rates are all inclusive, which means the cost of utilities, internet and other services are covered by the rent. Rental agreements are clear and transparent. 

These residences are a very popular choice, so there is a high ditalicand for thitalic. Apply as soon as possible.


2. Private rental

Many students choose to rent a house, unit or apartment via the private rental market. Make sure you know your rights and responsibilities if you choose to rent.

Rental properties are usually unfurnished and the cost of utilities (electricity, gas and water) and internet are not included in the rent. 

You will need to budget for the upfront costs of furniture, bond, the first month’s rent, utilities and internet connection.  

Lease agreements are typically 12 months long, but this may be negotiated with the real estate agent or landlord. The rent will be around AU$ 250 to AU$ 350 per week for a studio (charges vary between $ 80 and $ 200 for a single person (internet connection or not, use of water) and AU$ 300 at AU$ 450 for an apartment, not including utilities.

Places to look for private rental properties include:

  • Realestate.com.au
  • Domain.com.au
  • Realestateview.com.au
  • StudentAccommodationOne.com – a housing search website which includes student accommodation, share accommodation and homestay all in one single platform


3. Share houses

Living in a share house offers independence and flexibility, and is generally the cheapest housing option, making it a popular choice for students. In a share house, you will typically have your own room in a rented property, with shared use of the kitchen, bathroom and other common areas. 

Moving into a room in an existing share house is usually easier and cheaper than setting up a new household, as utilities and internet will already be connected, and common areas are likely to be furnished. 

Prices vary between AU$ 140 and AU$ 250 per person per week, depending on the location of the apartment and its quality.

Places to look for existing share houses include:

  • Flatmates.com.au
  • Flatmate Finders
  • Gay Share
  • StudentAccommodationOne.com – a housing search website which includes student accommodation, share accommodation and homestay all in one single platform


4. Homestay

Homestay is where you live with a local family, couple or individual. Your host will provide a supportive environment and can help you transition to Melbourne. 

‘Full board’ homestay usually offers a furnished room and access to shared facilities with meals and utilities included. 

Rents per week are around AU$ 245 (including meals).

The Australian Homestay Network selects hosts that will provide a safe and welcoming home. Student Accommodation One is a housing search website which includes homestay options.


5. Student hostels

Student hostels offer furnished, lockable rooms and shared facilities. These properties are designed for university students and provide a social atmosphere.

Some student hostels offer meal plans while others provide kitchen facilities. Utilities are often included in the overall cost.

You can find more student hostels listed on Rooms International, Student Hostel Network, and Student Accommodation One.


Less than 3 kilometres from City campus

Melbourne City, East Melbourne, Southbank, Docklands, Carlton, North Melbourne, West Melbourne, South Melbourne, Parkville, Fitzroy

- Distance to City campus is 0.5–3 kilometres. Suburbs are either within short walking distance or at most 10–15 minutes travel by tram.

- Accommodation in these suburbs can be expensive.

- Most private hostels and student apartment complexes are located in these areas.


Less than 7 kilometres from City campus

Carlton North, Fitzroy North, Richmond, Abbotsford, Collingwood, Clifton Hill, South Yarra, Prahran, Windsor, Toorak, Albert Park, Middle Park, Port Melbourne, St Kilda, Northcote, Brunswick, Flitalicington, Kensington, Ascot Vale, Footscray

- Distance to City campus is 3–7 kilometres. Travel time is approximately 15–25 minutes on public transport.

- There are very few private hostels or student apartment complexes located in these areas, however most other housing options are available.


Less than 12 kilometres from city campus

Caulfield North, Armadale, Malvern, Glen Iris, Camberwell, Ivanhoe, Fairfield, Thornbury, Croxton, Preston, Coburg, Strathmore, Essendon, Moonee Ponds, Williamstown, Yarraville, Newport, Maribyrnong

- Distance to City campus is 8–10 kilometres. Travel time is approximately 20–35 minutes on public transport.

Department and courses

schools.name: San Francisco State University - Graduate
schools.overview:
Established in 1899, San Francisco State is a premier public university located in the heart of San Francisco, known to be one of the world's most vibrant and beautiful cities, and the epicenter of innovation and entrepreneurship.


San Francisco State University is proud of our diverse student body – the University serves students from the San Francisco Bay Area and all over California, across the U.S. and around the world, with nationally acclaimed programs that span a broad range of disciplines. Nearly 30,000 students enroll at the University each year, and its more than 253,000 graduates have contributed to the economic, cultural and civic fabric of San Francisco and beyond.


San Francisco State University ranks fourth in the nation among master's institutions that host international students. With a diverse range of students from almost every state and nearly 100 countries, the student community is perfect for those looking to experience new cultures. The campus was even recently ranked third among all US universities for diversity by the Wall Street Journal.

Located in one of the world’s most beautiful and culturally diverse cities, San Francisco State University is a public university with approximately 30,000 students.
schools.administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet — please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • The application form completed
  • Proof of English proficiency: a Tepitech score certificate in English
  • Proof of financial eligibility: Students must show proof of funds for education and living expenses for the duration of their studies at SF State.
  • Submit a bank statement, financial statement, or letter from your bank with a minimum balance of equivalent to $20,000.
  • Financial documents must be less than 6 months old.
  • A copy of your passport
  • Complete the peliminary course wishlist form with 10 classes you are interested in taking during your desired SF State semester.
  • Please list the classes in order of preference. Please note, not all classes will be offered every term.
  • Class schedules for Fall will be available in April.
  • Class schedules for Spring will be available in November.
  • See the SF State Class Schedule.
  • You are encouraged to submit a preliminary wish list using the course information in the bulletin or the class schedule, but this is not required for admission.
  • Once we receive your preliminary course wish list, we will provide you with initial advising.
  • You can update your preferences once the class schedule is posted.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech Bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


2. Visa

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website. You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1. Admission letter and I-20 form

Once you are admitted by the host university, SF State University will send us your admission package with your acceptance letter, a DS-2019 form and original documents for your visa. You can request a visa only after your application has been approved. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2.Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3. Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4.Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3. Insurance and Health (more information here)

Students are required to purchase the CSU/SF State sponsored insurance offered by Relation.


You have to pay insurance for each semester: $975 per semester or $1,950 for your year abroad


It is imperative that you take out an additional insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here. 


5. Campus life

There are a lot of student activities you can partake in to meet people. The campus is located in a quiet and safe neighbourhood near the Pacific Ocean.

Address: 835 Market Street, 6th floor, San Francisco, CA 94103
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here and here)

SF State will provide information and assistance on accommodation for students from EPITECH.

Available on a first-come first-served basis. If you are interested in campus housing, please be sure to apply as soon as you are admitted to SF State. These are traditional residence halls. Students will be in double rooms equipped with 2 twin beds and desks. There are shared gender-specific showers and bathrooms located in each wing of every floor. Price is about US $ 15,000 for the academic year (including meal plan & room rates).


Off-campus accommodation (more information here)

  • Campus Apartments

These are 2-bedroom or 3-bedroom apartments with a bathroom, living/dining room, and kitchenette (equipped with refrigerators, sink, stovetop). Students will be in double bedrooms with 2 twin beds and desks. You may choose to rent an apartment by yourself, or to share an apartment with other people.


  • Homestay

Another kind of off-campus housing is a Homestay, which allows you to live with a host family and stay in a room in the family’s home. It costs around $US 300 per week (room and meals included) and you have to pay placement fee.


For more information, check the websites below:

American Homestay Network

Universal Student Housing

International Student Placements

International Student Placements Pricing (per month)


Important Notes: You may need temporary, short-term housing when you first arrive in San Francisco, while you are looking for a permanent place to live. It is important to have temporary housing before you come to San Francisco. Hostels (youth hostels) are cheaper than hotels, but you must share a room with several people. Residence hotels usually require a stay of one week or more and give a furnished room, meals, bed sheets and bath towels. Residence hotels may require that you pay a money deposit in advance in order to save a room.

3. Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4.Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.

You have to pay insurance for each semester: $975 per semester or $1,950 for your year abroad

schools.name: Saxion University of Applied Sciences
schools.overview:
Saxion University of Applied Sciences is a University of Applied Sciences that originated from the rich educational history of the city of books Deventer and from the social initiatives of enterprising textile traders from Twente.

Ever since the 13th century, Deventer has been a bastion of books and knowledge. The roots of Saxion University can be traced back to 1875.

A merger of two educational institutions, the Hogeschool Enschede and Hogeschool IJselland, in 1998 paved the way for Saxion University in its present form. This merger enabled Saxion to build further on its bold position in Dutch higher education and since then Saxion University has come to be recognised as an important center of expertise at regional, national and international level.

It provides more than 100 courses in study fields as archaeology, finance, law, engineering, hospitality, business, IT, broadcasting, health and digital media.

The university has more than 27,000 students over its three campuses, with more than 3,500 international students from 89 different nationalities.

Saxion is one of the largest institutions of higher education in the Netherlands.

schools.overview:
Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember (ITS) is a public institute in Indonesia located in Surabaya, the second largest city in the country and the capital of East Java.


It is one of the best public institutions in Indonesia with a focus on scientific research and technology. It was ranked the fifth best institution of higher education in all of Indonesia in 2015 (over 20,000 students).

The computer technology faculty offers two specializations: one in computer engineering and one in computer systems. These courses of study aim to give students skills in many areas: Development and analysis of the need for information systems, project development in the context of information systems by combining the aspect of technology information infrastructure (hardware, software, network, Data), organizational hierarchy, process and procedure, human resources and cultures, and policy and regulations.

1.Room in a house


In Indonesia, flats mostly are rented rooms in a house. Flats around ITS spread around campus triangle, namely Mulyosari area, Gebang, and Keputih. Flat prices vary by type. Starting from Rp 300.000,00 to above one also depends on the facilities and location. In addition to ITS triangle area, ITS students can also rent a boarding room in ITS lecturer’s housing with more secure security because it is located inside the campus. Although the price in housing lecturers ITS usually relatively higher price, the proximity to the campus and security guarantees to make room cost inside ITS campus much in demand.


2.Private apartments


A wide selection of apartments also began popping up around the campus of ITS. For more comfortable life, apartments offer security and privacy. Around the ITS there are several apartment options, including East Coast Apartment, Puncak Kertajaya, Grand Dharmahusada Lagoon, Dian Regency Apartments, Manyar Apartment Gunawangsa, Bale Hinggil, Taman Melati Surabaya Apartment and other apartment options.


3. Hotel and guest house


For the purpose of accommodation in a short time especially for parents or relatives, guest house on campus ITS is a good option. Hotel in ITS features guest house concept and is available in two types, namely Guest House Bougenville and Guest House Jasmine. Guest House Bougenville is located at Jalan Teknik Arsitektur Blok H-8, 10, 12 (ITS Lecturer Complex), while Guest House Jasmine is located at Jalan Teknik Sipil Block I No. 19 (also at ITS Lecturer Housing Complex).Each of these guest houses is well supported with adequate facilities for the comfort of guests. In addition, the guest house-guest house is also away from the crowds and noise thus creating a quiet and comfortable atmosphere.

  1. Chinese language (HSK 1-4) - 120 hours, 10 credits, 12 weeks
  2. Chinese Trading & Investment - 36 hours, 3 credits, 12 weeks
  3. Business Data Management - 36 hours, 3 credits, 12 weeks

Semester 2

Students are encouraged to find an internship by themselves. SFB has responsibility in guiding and assisting students during the process, but cannot guarantee any internship position. An internship report must be handed in if students need a certificate to be issued.


Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
