schools.cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 1000€ depending on the company & the dates
  • Insurance from the university: 800yuan for a year - about 100€
  • Registration fee at the university: 450 RMB (all kinds of programs)
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage
  • Visa: between 110-130€
  • Medical examinations in China: about 70€
  • Accommodation deposit: 500 yuan (about 60€)
  • Chinese residence permit: 500 yuan (60€)
  • Your school supplies (textbooks notably)
  • Beddings for the dorms, etc.


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Yuan (RMB or CNY). 1 € = 8.26 RMB (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

  • Housing: about 500€
  • Food: 100-150€
  • Transportation: 40€
  • Phone, internet: 8-16€
  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure: 100-200€
  • For nightlife, if you are European, entry and drinks are usually free
  • For monuments and cultural sites, most have an entry fee
  • In 80% of cases, you get student discounts with your student card

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.

schools.name: Shibaura Institute of Technology (SIT)
schools.overview:
Shibaura Institute of Technology (SIT) has firmly maintained “learning through practice” as the philosophy in education of engineers ever since Tokyo Higher School of Industry and Commerce, the predecessor to SIT, was established in 1927. In response to the recent progress in the globalization of the economy, SIT is providing an up-to-date framework for “learning through practice” including intensive English Language programs, Project Based Learning programs under multicultural environment, along with many Hands-on subjects that has been preserved through SIT’s 91 years of history.

The initiative for educational reforms are supported by Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology and implemented in collaboration with other technical universities both in Japan and other countries, Japanese industries, and local communities in Tokyo and Saitama where our campuses are located.

SIT now aims to foster scientists and engineers who can contribute to the sustainable growth of the world by exposing our students to culturally diverse environments where they learn to cope with, collaborate with, and have ever-lasting friendships with fellow students from around the world.
schools.administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Only after you have been appointed by Epitech, you can start the application procedures, that is to say, your nomination and application.

Unlike other Epitech students, you will have to do your own nomination (the nomination is the process during which someone proposes a student as a candidate).

Steps:

  1. Please, use this link to start the nomination process.
  2. Nominate the International Mobility Coordinator at Epitech as your nominator, between April 1 and 30, and apply for the Sandwich Program.
  3. Once the International Mobility Coordinator at Epitech has approved your nomination, you will be able to start your application.

All the documents to submit will be specified in your Shibaura user session.

Your transcripts will be directly uploaded on Shibaura's platform by the International Mobility Coordinator at Epitech, and you will need to download your Tepitech on Intra and upload it on Shibaura's portal.


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Admission Letter

Once your application has been accepted, you will receive your acceptance letter signed by SIT.

The letter of acceptance might be required by the Japanese Immigration Office to proceed with your visa application.


3. Visa application after COE (Certificate of Eligibility) and Certificate for Completion of Registration to the ERFS System (Entrants, Returnees, Follow-up System)

In August, you will receive electronically your Certificate for Completion of Registration to ERFS system, and by post your Certificate of Eligibility.

After receiving these two required documents, you will be able to start applying for your visa.

Students who stay more than 90 days require a visa.

SIT assists by providing the necessary documents (COE - Certificate of Eligibility) for visa application.

For more information on the visa application process, click here.


Upon your arrival:

During your immigration check after the first landing in Japan, show QR codes on the Visit Japan Web screen to an officer and answer questions.

Your COE will be exchanged with a “Residence Card” upon your entry in Japan.


4. Insurance and Health

SIT covers the fee for the insurance which is university insurance for injuries or accidents related to education and research activities at SIT, called Gakkensai and Gakkenbai.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

Exchange students who will stay in Japan more than 3 months must join the National Health Insurance (NHI) regardless of the kind of insurance they may already have. This is a strict legal requirement in Japan. Once you arrive in Japan, you must complete the required procedures at your local city/ward office.

For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/japon

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


Campus life

SIT has 3 campuses: Toyosu, Shibaura, and Omiya.

The campus you attend will depend on the course you register.

Please check and consider the campus location for the courses you are willing to take and the distances of each campus when you register for the courses.

Please consider distances among campuses if you wish to take courses in different campuses.

Travel times:

  • Between Shibaura and Toyosu campuses: 30 minutes
  • Between Shibaura or Toyosu and Omiya campus: 1 hour 30 minutes
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

SIT has an international student dormitory on the Omiya campus. This is a dormitory for International students and Japanese students. It is not only a place to live but also a community that encourages international exchanges. There are common rooms and shared kitchens on each floor. Each private room is approximately 17 square meters and is equipped with a modular bathroom with a toilet with a warm-water bidet, bed, desk and LAN access, convenience and comfort for studying and hobbies. A supervisory staff is always available to respond to needs for residents.

It is very competitive to enter the dorm, so please look for an alternative options in case you failed to stay in.


Rent: JPY 35,000/month(excluding meals and utilities), so about 200€

*One month’s rent is needed as a deposit upon entry to the dormitory

If you choose this option, please consider distances between campuses!


Off-campus accommodation (more information here)

There are several options for the housing: student dormitories, apartments, shared houses, and homestay. SIT supports entering the dormitories but even if you cannot get into a dorm due to capacity issues, SIT will introduce a private agent for looking for housing such as shared houses, apartments and homestay. Students will have a great deal of support and will have no trouble finding housing.


  • Shared house

One of the most popular housing options among the students is a “shared house”. A “shared house” is a property where the kitchen, living room, bathroom, etc. are shared with other residents.

Companies include: Frontier Co, Ltd balance plan, Borderless House, etc.


  • Apartments

If you want complete privacy, you can also sign up for an apartment on your own through a real estate agency. However, the cost will be a bit higher, and you may need to furnish the room yourself in some cases.


  • Homestay

If you want to experience the Japanese life style, a homestay may be an option for you. We will share a homestay agent’s contact information to assist you in arranging this option.
schools.courses:
Credits

Students must take a total of 30 local credits, so 15 credits per semester to obtain 60 ECTS for the year, not counting EIP credits.


Academic Calendar

Spring semester: April to July

Fall semester: September to January


Department and courses

You will be doing what is called the Course-Taking Sandwich Program (more information here). Students have a wide range of study options from all departments and colleges. Classes are taught in English and Japanese language lessons are also available.


For Epitech students, you will have access to graduate and undergraduate Computer Science courses and Japanese language courses.

The following courses are the ones that have been approved by Epitech's pedagogical team. This list, however, only adds up to 26 local credits, this means you can take a free course each semester.


Japanese language: 2 credits (Omiya, Toyosu campus) Fall

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Embedded system (32P5): 2 credits (Omiya campus) Undergraduate level, Fall

Learn and understand the fundamentals of embedded systems. Learn and understand both hardware and software of embedded systems and their real-time constraints. Building the knowledge how to develop embedded programs using a toolkit.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Robotics (43B5): 2 credits (Toyosu campus) Undergraduate level, Spring

A robot is a system consisting of basic technologies such as mechanism, control, material, electrical and information. To apply the robot technology to the target work, it needs to design the system according to the objective. We will study how to systemize the basic technologies and how to find a solution for the social problem. In the class, we will discuss the actual problems and their solutions in the practical use of a robot to acquire the ability of solving a problem.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Introduction to Advanced Science and Technology (15M1): 2 credits (Toyosu campus) Undergraduate level, Fall

In order to become an excellent engineer or researcher, it is effective to learn about the most advanced science and technology. The scope of this course is to learn about cutting edge technologies in various research fields. This course follows an omnibus

style and is given by the teaching staff from various foreign countries. Many topics from various fields are involved such as progress in computer technology, Environmental problems, Natural disaster prevention, Advanced materials in functional or construction materials, Bio-chemistry, New Energy. The specific content of each lecture will be explained in the first class. Students will be able to study cutting-edge research in various fields and make study plans that lead to their specialized fields

in the future. You can also learn how to write basic reports.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Topics in Numerical Analysis (44V3): 2 credits (Omiya campus) Undergraduate level, Fall

Errors in numerical computation, Floating-point number, Newton’s method, contraction mapping, iterative method, simultaneous linear equation, numerical derivative, initial value problems for ordinary differential equation (ODE), Euler’s method, Runge-Kutta method.

Objectif: To be able to understand errors and error propagation in numerical computation.To be able to use several basic approaches and algorithms in numerical computation. To be able to analyze error estimation and convergence of established algorithms.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Computer Simulation 2 credits

This course introduces the fundamental and practical concepts of computer simulation as well as how to use MATLAB tool for handling and analyzing the simulation data. The topics include MATLAB programming, queue theory, etc. Assignments require an understanding of network problems and MATLAB programming.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Robot Task & System 2 credits

This lecture treats the task execution methods by the robot, and its system configuration. To achieve the desired task, advanced skills same as humans are required to the robot system. Moreover, the automatic generation ability of the task sequence according to the situation is also required. In this class, many case examples of the robot systems are introduced and explained. Understand the task execution methodology by the robot. Understand the configuration of the robot system to execute several tasks. Understand the methodology of the robot system which generates task sequence automatically, according to the situation. Acquire ability to design robot system for realizing desired task by using learned knowledge.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Human-Machine System (4567): 2 credits (Toyosu Campus) Graduate level

This course focuses on the relationship between the human and the mechanical systems. The mechanical system should have a safety and useful functionality for the human. This course includes the below topics to understand the design method of the human machine system. Topics is (1) the characteristics of the perception and the recognition, (2) design of driver assist systems, (3) the characteristics of the control action, (4) HMI (Human Machine Interface) for the mechanical system.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Advanced Computer Architecture (1511): 2 credits (Toyosu Campus) Fall

CPU chips are the most important components in computer systems and their performance has been continuing to grow. In this lecture, we study representative computer architectures that are actually used in high performance processor chips. Furthermore, through designing hardware components (i.e. function units) and simulations, we analyze and discuss how the hardware structure influences the performance. The material to read is provided in pdf at Scomb and Reading Assignments are directed in advance. To help understanding in reading, several basic questions are also provided about the contents of the pre-directed reading material. At every class, students are divided into groups and discuss what he/she understood through the reading material and his/her answer to the questions. Discussion is made in each breakout room of Zoom. Then, students give presentations in group order. The instructor checks the presentations and gives lecture/comments to make up for missing content in their presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Management of Innovation: 2 credits (Toyosu Campus) Graduate Level, Fall

This course will start from providing basic understanding of innovation from view points of history of society, economics, technology and corporate management. Then participants will obtain practical knowledge of innovation to apply for business cases to develop business strategy by understanding real examples. This course will discuss innovation with global view point. After the guidance and introduction of innovation concept in the first lecture, participants are requested to chose own innovation topic to study. In each ecture participants need to prepare short presentation according to the subject provided in the previous lecture. Discussion after each presentation participants obtain deeper understanding of innovation aspects with real examples

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Advanced Robotic Manipulation: 2 credits (Shibaura Campus) Graduate level, Fall

This lecture gives advancesd mathematical introduction to robotics. Robotic engineering consistes of basic theory and practice. The basic theory begins with mathematical definition related to position, orientation, and coordinate frames. Furthermore, they are led to robot's rotation, transformation, and control technologies. Meanwhile, the practics includes mechanism, motor drives, electrical hardware, and software design. They assist mutually and the both are indispensable. The former theory has been evolved

and changed gradually. Therefore, if students who want to master advanced robotics, they need to learn the advanced theory.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Embedded Systems Engineering: 2 credits (Omiya Campus) Graduate level, Fall

The main purpose of this class is to understand and execute systems engineering in embedded system and M2M(Machine to Machine) system. Requirement analysis, modeling, system architecture design, and project management in embedded system and M2M system are introduced and discussed.The purpose of this class is to understand and execute systems engineering in embedded system, IoT(Internet of Things), and M2M(Machine to Machine) system. To understand technology, requirement, and architecture of embedded system. To understand life cycle of embedded system, requirement analysis, architecture design To understand system architecture and networks for M2M system.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Bionic and biomimetic system engineering: 2 credits

The purpose of this course is to learn basics of biology and physiology, measuring biological signals, signal processing, information processing, system integration, biomimetic technologies, and ethics. Through learning the topics, students acquire wide view required for developing biomedical systems.


Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
schools.cost:
Financial overview (4th yeat at Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees at the partner university.
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Visa: 18€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage (same as above)
  • Deposit for room if you live in the dormitory
  • Registration fee at SIT: 170€ (30 000 yen)


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Japanese yen. 1 € = 176¥ (rate in October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

When coming to Japan, you should estimate that you will be spending every month between 1000€ to 1500€.


  • Housing & utilities

250 to 500€ + 40€ of utilities. The price of an apartment in the city center is approximately the same as a mid-size city in France.


As SIT has two campuses located one hour and half from each other, with one located in inner Tokyo (Toyosu) and the other on the outskirts of the capital (Higashi-Omiya), prices can be very different.The closer you try living to the Toyosu campus, the more rent will be expensive, while the rent near Higashi-Omiya is more affordable. This marks a problem as most of the classes about computer science are in Toyosu with the Omiya campus offering close to none. You should therefore try choosing with care where you decide to live.

Rent in cities close to the Toyosu campus: 500€ - 800€

Rent in cities close to the Omiya campus: 350€ - 600€


  • Food & eating out ~150-300€

Around 6 euros for a meal in a basic restaurant

Around 15 euros for a meal in a mid-range restaurant

The price of basic food is about the same as in France (Paris), except for imported products which will be more expensive and local products which will be cheaper.


  • Transportation ~100€

Expect to pay anything between 100€ to 300€ depending on how much you travel in a month.


The distance between the Omiya campus and the Toyosu campus is one hour and a half. There is no direct train line to join the two. It will cost about 7.50€ to go from one campus to the other, so a 15€ round trip. While it will be rare to have to do the trip every day of the week, expect to do it at least twice. Depending on where you live in Tokyo, you will pay at least 100€ a month for travelling.

You can get a commuter pass which will reduce the price of transportation; however, this pass is only applicable to one route and that route only, back and forth.

To take the example of the trip from the Omiya campus to the Toyosu campus:

  • Start from the Higashi-Omiya station > Get down at the Ikebukuro Station > Take the metro from Ikebukuro station > Get down at the Toyosu station


Same trip backwards to go from the Toyosu campus to the Omiya campus.

You will pay only once when you get the commuter pass (about 90€ for one month), and won’t pay anything more when travelling between those stations.

You can get down at any stop on that line between Higashi-Omiya and Ikebukuro, and Ikebukuro and Toyosu, but you will pay extra cost if you get out of a station after those. For example, if you go to the station after the Ikebukuro station, you will pay the normal fare between those two stations. You can get a student discount for the shikansen via a machine in the university.


  • Health insurance ~12€
  • Phone, internet ~20-50€

We recommend you to make a mobile contract at one of discount mobile phone companies in Japan, for example: "Rakuten Mobile", "UQ mobile" provided by KDDI, "Y!mobile" by SoftBank, and Sakura Mobile. With a new SIM card, you can use your own smart phone in Japan. A previous student has recommended Rakuten for the phone plan because it is the cheapest for a good amount of data.


  • Leisure ~80-150€


The prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

Students can find the government-approved information site for studying in Japan operated by the Japan Student Services Organization through the link here.

Please note that you can work within a limit of 28 hours per week. The university can help you with your job search, however, it is important to note that it will not be in the IT field.

schools.name: Southern Illinois University Edwardsville
schools.overview:
Southern Illinois University Edwardsville (SIUE)

Accredited by the Higher Learning Commission of the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools, SIUE is a university offering more than 350 undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral areas of study.


The campus is located in Edwardsville, Illinois, and is well-known for its welcoming and friendly environment. Spread over 10 square kilometers, the campus provides every necessary commodity on site.


Located in the Midwest, SIUE is only 25 minutes from St. Louis and within reach of Chicago, making it conveniently situated for accessing major city centers.


Nationally recognized for its excellence:

  • SIUE is listed as one of the top business schools in the US.
  • It has received the Higher Education Excellence in Diversity Award, which is of particular interest to international students.
schools.administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents must be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline. (See the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline.). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet — please be patient.


In the past, the partner has requested the following:

  • The completed application form
  • Proof of English proficiency: A Tepitech score certificate in English
  • Proof of financial eligibility:
  • Students must show proof of funds for education and living expenses for the duration of their studies at SF State.
  • Acceptable documents:
  • Bank statement, financial statement, or letter from your bank
  • Must reflect a minimum balance of $20,000 USD
  • Documents must be less than 6 months old
  • A copy of your passport


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to the Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • The EPITECH re-registration dossier


2. Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website. You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1. Admission letter and I-20 form

Once you are admitted by the host university, SIUE will send you your admission package with your acceptance letter and original documents for your visa. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2. Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3.Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4.Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3. Insurance and Health (more information here and here)

SIUE has secured a medical health insurance policy for all international students. This is the only acceptable health insurance plan for international students attending SIUE. The University Student Insurance Committee coordinated the premium and plan benefits through Academic Health Plans. 


All international students are required to enroll in the plan if they are enrolled in (1) or more credit hours or are enrolled in University 500. The credit hours can be on-campus or off-campus. Your Bursar bill will automatically include this fee. Insurance cost for international students per semester: $1,200


Additionally, specific immunizations are required for all international students (notably for Tuberculosis (TB).


It is recommended that you complete them before arrival. If your immunization records are not in English, they must be accompanied by a certified translation. Immunizations required upon arrival will cost $75–$200.


4. Prepare your arrival

Read more about the university here.

Check the International Student Checklist provided by the university here.
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

Students may live in on-campus housing. Two main options are available:

  • Website: siue.edu/housing/housing-options/evergreen/index.shtml

The Preferred Application Deadlines are the following:

schools.overview:
Sripatum University (SPU), one of the oldest and most famous private universities in Thailand, was founded in 1970 by Dr. Suk Phukayaphon under the name “Sripatum College” with the determination to create a quality educational institution to produce graduates with knowledge and ability to serve society. We received the grace of Her Royal Highness Princess Srinagarindra, the Princess Mother, who bestowed the name “Sripatum” with the meaning “a source of knowledge that blooms like a lotus flower”.


Sripathum College was approved to change its type to a university by the University Council on November 6, 1987 and has been known as “Sripathum University” since then. The university has expanded into various campuses as follows:

  • Chonburi Campus was established in 1987 to respond to the needs of people in the Eastern Region and support the current Eastern Seaboard and East Economic Corridor (EEC) policies.
  • Khon Kaen Campus was established in 2013 to provide higher education services to people in the Northeastern region and to support the expansion of business in the ASEAN region.

The main goal of the university is to develop students to become graduates with quality and morality to be an important force for the industrial business sector to create added value for the Thai economy. Currently, Sripatum University offers 10 faculties, 5 colleges, 36 bachelor’s degree programs, 10 master’s degree programs, and 8 doctoral degree programs, producing more than 120,000 graduates and currently has more than 25,000 students.

TECHNOLOGICAL UNIVERSITY DUBLIN


Technological University Dublin (TU) was founded in 1992, but had already existed under another name and structure since 1887.

Nearly 22,000 students attend TU Dublin, which offers four distinct fields of study through four different colleges:

  • College of Arts & Tourism
  • College of Business
  • College of Engineering & Built Environment
  • College of Sciences & Health


Each college has been recognized as a center of excellence in its field.


Campus and Location


Each department has its own premises, all dispersed within Dublin city center.


The building for Tech 4 students is located in the city center, just a 5-minute walk from lively areas filled with:

  • Bars
  • Restaurants
  • Shopping, etc.

Our three campuses are equipped with modern laboratories to ensure the learning and practical experience of our students.

Tecsup is accredited by ASIIN and ICACIT, representing a seal of higher education quality.

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Visa application (more information here)

Tecsup will request the student visa for each exchange student. For an exchange student visa application at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Peru, the student will typically need to present the following documents:

  • Valid passport
  • Proof of financial means (bank statements of the financial sponsors with a minimum of USD 3,200 per semester)
  • Health insurance certificate
  • Flight Itinerary or travel plan
  • Passport-sized photos


You can also arrive in Peru as a tourist but after 90 days, you are legally required to change your status from tourist to student (also known as "Calidad Migratoria de Formacion"). You must begin the process within your first few weeks in Peru, ideally within 30 days of arrival. If you wait too long, you could lose the chance to apply or need to pay fines.


Before applying for the process, make sure you have:

  • Valid passport and copy of Bio page & Latest Peruvian entry stamp
  • Acceptance letter from TECSUP
  • Completed application form (F-004), signed.
  • Criminal background certificate from your home country (apostilled and translated if needed).
  • Ficha de Canje Internacional INTERPOL
  • Health insurance certificate
  • Proof of financial solvency (e.g., bank statement or scholarship letter)


Note: Any documents not in Spanish must be translated by an official translator in Peru.


3. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out an international insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. 

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information. 


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/conseils-par-pays-destination/perou/

schools.name: Thammasat University
schools.overview:
Thammasat University, the 2nd oldest university in Thailand, is one of the most famous and prestigious institutions in the country. Among its former students are prime ministers, politicians, and governors of the Bank of Thailand.

Founded in 1934, Thammasat University offers more than 243 programs in 23 different faculties.


Sirindhorn International Institute of Technology (SIIT), which welcomes our students, was created in 1992. Its main objective is to train engineers and qualified technology experts to be:

  • Proficient in advanced technologies
  • Fluent in English
  • Capable of managing and driving engineering and technology research


Thammasat University has several campuses:

  • Main campus: Tha Prachan, located in Bangkok, in the heart of the old city
  • Second campus: Rangsit, located 40 km from Bangkok. Houses various faculties including SIIT (Architecture, Medicine, Languages, etc.). The Rangsit campus is very large. There are free minibuses throughout campus, minivans go to downtown Bangkok in 30 minutes for less than 1€. There are also many facilities (bookstores, gymnasiums, restaurants, hospitals, banks, post offices, grocery stores)
schools.administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.*


Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Application form
  • Letter of Application (Motivation Letter)
  • Regulations for exchange students with a signature of the applicant
  • Resume
  • Transcripts in English (will be provided by the IAFF team)
  • Tepitech (downloadable from the intra)
  • Recommendation letter from an academic advisor
  • A copy of passport


Important: Thammasat University may require you to bring the original documents with you. Therefore, you must keep the original documents safe.


Thammasat will process your application during May.


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Admission Letter

Around June, Thammasat University will send acceptance letters electronically to the Epitech IAFF office, who will then forward them to you.

This letter of acceptance is your proof of official admission to Thammasat University.


3. Visa

In France: getting an ED visa

The SIIT International Affaires and Corporate Relations Division will foward the acceptance letter to the student's home university. This letter, along with other necessary documents, must be presented at the Embassy of Thailand in France to apply for a Non-Immigrant Visa "ED" (Student Visa). This visa is generally valid for 3 months. Check out the necessary documents for the application here.

For the following steps, SIIT International Affairs and Corporate Relations Division provides support with documentation.


Arrival in Thailand: Stay Permit PAD

Upon arrival in Thailand, an immigration officer will provide a permit stamp with the mentions "Admitted": Date of arrival and "Until": Date of validity (typically 3 months).

This "until" date might differ from your visa’s printed date, and it will determine when you must apply for an extension.


During your stay in Thailand: Extension

If staying longer than the "until" date, apply for an extension at the Immigration Office (Soi Suan Plu, next to Sathorn Road). You need to bring: 2000THB, your passport, and a letter from SIIT/Thammasat confirming study dates. The letter can take 1–2 weeks to prepare—request it early.


If you plan to leave Thailand: Re-entry permit

If you have a "1 entry" visa or an extension, and you plan to leave Thailand, you must apply for a re-entry permit or your visa/extension will be canceled. A single re-entry permit costs 500THB (about 15€) and a multiple one costs 1000THB (about 30€)

For the re-entry permit, you need to apply at the Immigration Office or airport. No letter is required for this permit. Upon return, you'll receive a new residence permit stamp with a new end date.

Inform your coordinator or the Thammasat IR department if you plan to leave the country.


Notes from a Previous Student (2022–2023):

  • Visa cost: ~75€
  • Can be done entirely online, depending on your embassy
  • Check visa confirmation carefully — One student had the wrong university listed and had to visit the embassy to correct it
  • Keep your acceptance letter (or a copy) with you when traveling to show at customs
  • COVID test may be required before meeting your buddy — do it within 1 week of arrival
  • International driver’s license is recommended — scooters are very helpful


4. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

Please bear in mind that air quality in Bangkok/Pathum Thani can be poor at times—bring masks/monitor AQI.

For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/thailande

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.



Prepare your arrival

The SIIT International Affairs is a good resource that you can check out here.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Thailand, click here.


Campus life

A 3 to 4-day welcome week is organized for exchange students, which includes orientation day, a campus tour, and a Thai study day, ensuring a warm introduction to SIIT and Thai culture.

Each exchange student is paired with at least one SIIT student. The buddy helps with various arrival needs such as airport pick-up, dormitory check-in, shopping, and campus tours.

Exchange students enjoy free access to various university facilities, including a gym, swimming pool, badminton court, and tennis court.

Each semester, SIIT arranges cultural activities for international students, such as cultural trips, Thai Cooking Day, and International Night, to immerse students in the rich Thai culture.

On-campus accommodation

SIIT does not provide on-campus accommodation but there are many dormitories around campus.


Off-campus accommodation (more information here)

Exchange students should notify the institute of their arrival date at least one month in advance to facilitate dormitory reservation close to campus.

SIIT is located in Thammasat University, Rangsit Campus, in the province of Phathumthani, 40 km north of Bangkok. However SIIT recommends all exchange students to stay at dormitories around the campus because it is more convenient to go to classes. We do not recommend staying in Bangkok and will not give support on finding your room. Traffic jams do happen every morning and classes can be held in other campus. Please be reminded that you have to attend at least 70% of classes. An excuse because of traffic is not an option.


  • Dormitories

The SIIT International Affairs team has provided a document listing all the dorms near campus (see link above).

A room at the off-campus dormitories, are for 2 people. It is your choice if you want to stay alone or with a roommate. Most of dormitory is located not far from the campus. Most of students who stay at the off-campus dormitory can walk to SIIT. SIIT also provide a free shuttle bus between campus in case you have classes at Bangkadi. Interestingly, you will see that a lot of Thai students love to take a motorbike taxi on campus. It cost 10-15 baht/journey.

Please plan 170-600€/month for rent.


  • Private accommodation

Previous Epitech students have looked for appartments on their own via Facebook groups. The rent can go from 170 to 250€/month.



Additional Notes

  • Water and electricity charges: €25 – €70 (estimate)
  • It is advisable to buy a fan to reduce air conditioning costs
  • These residences generally don’t have kitchens — culturally, most eat outside
  • Meals in street restaurants often cost less than €1

schools.name: The Catholic University of Korea
schools.overview:
The Catholic University of Korea began as the first Western-style educational institution in Korea with the establishment of "Saint Joseph's Seminary" by Father Maistre in Baeron, Jecheon, Chungbuk, in 1855. Since then, it has played a significant role in promoting education that respects human dignity in this land.


The history of the Catholic University of Korea is closely intertwined with the introduction of Catholicism to Korea, a period when Confucian ideology was the dominant value in the Joseon Dynasty. In the late 18th century, Joseon scholars began to academically study Catholicism, then known as Western Learning (Seohak). They formed faith communities and dedicated themselves to recruiting and educating leaders and priests.


Despite ongoing persecution of Catholics, in 1836, three young boys, including Choi Yang-up, Choi Bang-geo, and now Saint Andrew Kim Taegon, were sent to study in Macao; Kim Taegon was ordained in Shanghai in 1845 and returned home, only to be martyred soon after.


In response to continued persecution, in 1854, three more boys were sent to study in Penang, Malay Peninsula, while efforts to train clergy and start Western-style education were initiated in various locations.


Finally, in 1855, Father Maistre founded a seminary in Baeron, Jecheon, Chungcheongbuk-do, dedicated to Saint Joseph. This institution, offering courses in Chinese, Latin, philosophy, and theology, became the first Western-style educational establishment dedicated to modern humanities in Korea. It laid the foundation for what is now the


Catholic University of Korea, originally known as St. Joseph's Seminary.

3. Visa and ARC (more information here and here)


You will have to apply for a D-2-6 visa.


If you are French, all applications must be submitted to the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC). If you are not French, additional documents might be required. (Some documents can be prepared in advance.)


Visa application particularities:

  • Price in 2025 (application fee + visa fee + optional postal delivery ): about 126€
  • If you live in France, the visa application documents must be sent to Paris by registered mail (enveloppe en recommandé). IMPORTANT: The original passport must be sent, not a copy
  • There is NO in-person meeting at KVAC or the Embassy for this process


How do you collect your documents? (2 options):

  • Pay additional mailing costs to receive the visa and passport to the address indicated on the KVAC Waiver Courier document (delivered by La Poste Registered Mail Service)
  • OR
  • Apply by mail and collect them on-site at KVAC Paris after being contacted by KVAC


From 30 days after your arrival, you must apply for the Alien Registration Card (ARC), the identification card necessary for any stay longer than 90 days. This is a Korean official procedure; Keimyung will assist you when the semester begins.

  • Cost: about 20€
  • Issuance time: Approx. 2 months (you cannot leave the country before receiving the card)
  • You should always carry your ARC with you (you need it to open a bank account, for ID checks, online shopping, etc.)
  • Important: You cannot leave South Korea and travel around Asia without your ARC – it is essential to exit the country.


4. Insurance and Health

International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. When you receive your ARC, a Korean insurance account will automatically be created for you (approximately $70/month). You can choose to cancel and just count on your own international insurance, but please note that you will face disadvantages (deferred reimbursements, etc.).


If you choose to live in the dormitory on campus, a Tuberculosis (TB) Test result in English or Korean, taken within 4 weeks before the dormitory move-in date is also required. The test should include student’s name, hospital/clinic name, date of the test, and test results in English/Korean. schools.name: The Chinese University of Hongkong - Shenzhen campus
schools.overview:
Founded in 2012, the Chinese University of Hong Kong Shenzhen Campus has over 3,300 students. It is a renowned institution and ranks first places in:

  • QS ranking: 49 Global World Ranking
  • 10 Asian University ranking
  • 28th worldwide in Computer Science and Information Technology.


Nicknamed the "Chinese Silicon Valley," Shenzhen is located in the north of Hong Kong and is the seat of many multinational high-tech companies including Huawei, ZTE, Tencent, and TCL. This dynamic metropolis is based on the economic and social development of Hong Kong, Macau, and the Pearl River Delta region, and enjoys a spirit of innovation and high quality creative talent, thus providing a modern, cutting-edge university setting.

Ideally located between Longxiang Boulevard (Longgang District) and Dayun Park, the campus offers a pleasant environment for students who can enjoy an area surrounded by hills and a lake. A real city, the Shenzhen campus has restaurants and cafeterias, mini-markets, a gym, a bank, a clinic, etc.

Credits

You must complete 30 local credits in order to validate Tech 4 internationally.


Academic calendar

You will have to arrive at the end of August to start your year (especially for getting accommodations).

Classes start early September and run until mid-May.


Department and courses

You will take courses within the Bachelor - Computer Science & Engineering program, and will also have access to some business classes in the School of Management & Economics.

Below is a list of courses offered by the university and validated by Epitech.


In the Computer Science & Engineering Program:

  • CSC 1001 - Introduction to Computer Science: Programming Methodology
  • "This course introduces the basics of computer programming using Python. Students will learn the basic elements of modern computer systems, key programming concepts, problem solving and basic algorithm design. The key topics include the basic Python language syntax, data types, operators, flow control, defining and using function, I/O, data structure and algorithms, and the basics of object oriented programming. This course provides a foundation to further study in advanced computing topics."
  • CSC 3001 - Discrete Mathematics
  • "This course introduces the relevant mathematical concepts and techniques in computer science with emphasis on proofs and rigorous reasoning. Topics include: logics, methods of proofs, recursion, elementary number theory, graph theory, counting."
  • CSC 3050 - Computer Architecture
  • "Introduction of the major components of a computer system, including instruction set architecture (ISA), CPU datapath, control unit design, pipelining, memory hierarchy, peripheral interfaces, and multiprocessor architecture. RISC-V architecture will be used as a reference architecture."
  • CSC 3150 - Operating System
  • "To introduce the basic architecture and functions of operating systems. By looking at the overall architecture and individual components of different types of operating systems, major design issues, algorithms and design trade-off are discussed."
  • CSC 3185 - Introduction to Multimedia Systems
  • "This course is to study the fundamental multimedia concepts. Topics include multimedia data representation and operation, multimedia data compression, JPEG and MPEG compression standards, multimedia communications, and multimedia system. In this course, students will learn the principles of multimedia technologies, and will gain hands-on experience in applying various medias in the application."
  • CSC 4005 - Parallel Programming
  • "This course introduces concepts of parallel programming. Topics include parallel computer architectures, parallel programming languages, data structure designs for efficient parallel processing, synchronization controls, and applying parallel programming to high performance computing and AI/Machine Learning."
  • CSC 4160 - Cloud Computing
  • "Topics covered include principles of cloud computing, cloud systems architecture, virtualization techniques, cloud services, big data analytics, cloud programming toolkits, and specific cloud applications. We will study some public or private clouds and application tools; such as the AIRS cloud built on CUHK-SZ campus, Amazon AWS, and Aliyun, etc. Cloud programming tools are introduced with Python, Hadoop, Spark, TensorFlow, etc. We emphasize the interactions between existing clouds, Internet of Things, mobile networks, edge clouds, machine learning, and artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) applications."
  • CSC 6001 - Analysis of Algorithms
  • "This is an intermediate algorithms course with an emphasis on teaching techniques for the design and analysis of efficient algorithms, emphasizing methods of application. Specifically, the topics include recurrence relation, divide-and-conquer strategies, dynamic programming algorithms, greedy algorithms, theoretical complexity analysis, approximation algorithms, trees-based algorithms, string processing algorithms, and graph-based algorithms and algorithms."
  • CSC 6032 - Advanced Operating System
  • "This course will present an overview of some advanced operating systems and their underlying design principles. Issues discussed will include virtualization techniques for virtual machines and containers, memory management on GPU, I/O management for GPU, and file systems for GPU. Each enrolled student will be asked to design an OS for such systems."
  • CSC 6051 - Image Processing and Computer Vision
  • "A picture is worth a thousand words. How does a computer 'see' and 'understand' a picture? This course is an introductory graduate level course to answer such questions. We will first cover principles of image formation, operations to alter images, feature extraction and other image processing methods to turn images into abstract descriptions. We will then turn to computer vision topics that discuss how to perceive the structure and semantics of the world, including multi-view geometry, structure from motion, and visual localization and recognition. We will also touch upon related topics in machine learning which are widely used in computer vision."
  • CSC 6105 - Computer and Network Security
  • "This course aims to introduce important topics in computer and network security from an applied perspective. Topics include: (i) applied cryptography (e.g., cryptographic primitives, programming with OpenSSL), (ii) network security (e.g., unauthorized accesses, large-scale network attacks, firewall & intrusion detection systems), (iii) web security (e.g., HTTP session management and web attacks), and (iv) system security (e.g., buffer overflow, passwords, file system security), and (v) wireless security (e.g., WiFi security, wireless broadband network security). The course also discusses latest applied security topics according to the current research trends."
  • CSC 6115 - Parallel Programming
  • "This course trains students to understand how to program a distributed and parallel computing system. Student will be familiar with parallel and distributed languages such as MPI, Pthread, OpenMP, etc., and use them to design parallel and distributed programs and applications."
  • CSC 6118 - Information Theory
  • "After introducing some classical information theory results, e.g., the source coding theorem and the channel coding theorem, this course covers various research topics that are closely related to information theory, including modern coding theory and network coding theory. This course also discusses how to use these theories for designing network systems."
  • CSC 6129 - Reinforcement Learning
  • "This course offers an advanced introduction to reinforcement learning. Bandit learning and Markov decision processes will be covered. The focus will be on the design, analysis, and application of algorithms for complex reinforcement learning problems. The course will cover some recent developments in the field. Students are expected to have experience with optimization, stochastic processes, linear regression, coding for numerical computation, and writing mathematical proofs."
