schools.cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.)


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Medical insurance: 150€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage
  • Visa: between 110-130€
  • Medical examinations in China: 50-100€
  • Residence permit application: 100€ (one year)
  • School supplies: 150€ (CNY 1,200).


Estimated budget

The local currency is the Yuan (RMB or CNY). 1 € = 8.26 RMB (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

Per month, we advise you to plan a budget of 300€ for your expenses.

  • Accommodation: 300€/year
  • Food: 200€
  • "The food is much cheaper here. Most of us eat at the self-serve cafeteria which costs about (for a hearty dish) less than 2.50 €. Meals off campus cost around 20-25 yuan, depending on what you eat and where you eat."
  • Transportation: 30€
  • Phone, internet ~15-30€
  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure: 100€

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.

schools.name: The College at Brockport
schools.overview:
NOTE: THIS UNIVERSITY WAS PREVIOUSLY A ONE-SEMESTER PROGRAM AND IS NOW ONLY AVAILABLE FOR A FULL ACADEMIC YEAR


Near to the Canadian border, Brockport University is located 30 km from Rochester and 70 km from Buffalo. This school is part of the New York State Universities with 64 campuses scattered across the state. SUNY (State University New York) is recognized as the most comprehensive network of public higher education schools in the United States.

Brockport University has also been named one of the best universities in the North East.

The College at Brockport is located about 15 miles outside of Rochester, NY - the state's third largest city. Rochester is know as the home of some companies like Kodak, Xerox, Bausch & Lomb, and Paychex. With Brockport's small-town location and proximity to a bigger city, you get the best of both worlds. In addition, Brockport is within driving distance to Buffalo, Niagara Falls, and Toronto. The Rochester airport connects you to major hubs, which allows you to discover all that the region (and beyond) has to offer. From the main streets with its quaint shops to the University campus, the village is as attractive for tourism as it is for business. The proximity to Brockport and Rochester and the convenience of access to the rest of Monroe County makes it an ideal opportunity for the development of small industries and other businesses.

2 hours from Toronto and about 30 minutes from Lake Ontario, this small, human-scale sized village of 8000 inhabitants will allow future students to spend a semester in a human-scale sized school while benefiting from Anglo-Saxon teaching methods.
schools.administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet — please be patient.


Prepare the following documents in PDF format and upload them on the host university platform:

  • Online Exchange Student Application
  • Early September, the host university will create an account on their university platform for you. You will receive an email to create a password and answer the demographic application questions. You will also have to upload the different application documents. Please, before entering your GPA, wait for your transcripts to be sent by the AFFI team.
  • Transcripts in English (available on your intra)
  • Photocopy of passport (or residence card)
  • Exchange Visitor Course Request Form (the ISS coordinator at Brockport can assist you in the course selection process)
  • Bank Letter
  • This financial document must be less than 6 months old before your departure. It must show a minimum balance $8,500 (the exact amount will be communicated to you). This will prove that you have sufficient funds to cover the length of your program.
  • The bank letter should be written in English, signed, and stamped by the bank. If the bank letter that you provide is from a relative’s bank account, you must also provide a letter written by the latter attesting the family relationship and mentioning that the amount available will be used for your expenses during your studies in the US.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. VISA application

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.


1. Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to the university, you will receive an acceptance letter and an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2.     Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3.     Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4.     Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out an international insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. 


To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information. 


The university offers insurance costing around $580 (2022) for the semester, you can take out their insurance or choose one that offers the same coverage, however the university boldly recommends taking out the insurance offered by Brockport as it is very difficult to cover all the criteria for a foreign insurance.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file a: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis. You can find information about the required immunizations here (MMR, meningitis, covid-19). The following requirements must be completed before classes begin or you will be deregistered and not permitted to attend classes. In addition, a hold will be placed on your account and you will be charged a fee to re-register for the classes.

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html


4.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the US, click here.

You will also find useful information on Brockport's website here.


5. Campus life

The campus offers access to many indoor and outdoor campus facilities such as a fitness center, a swimming pool, an ice rink, a tennis court, etc. Many extra-curricular activities are also offered.

The International Student Services provides a week-long orientation upon arrival to help you with everything from setting up a bank account to familiarizing yourself with campus and the surrounding areas. 

Additionally, the International Student Services office provides unique trips for international student throughout the semester to professional sporting events, landmarks such as Niagara Falls, and more!
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (compulsory) (more information here)

Public transport is very limited. This is why it is necessary to live on the campus of the College of Brockport which offers all the necessary infrastructure. The university guarantees a room on campus to all students admitted, however it will be your responsibility to apply for a room after final admission and for meals .

Several options are available for "meal plans" (the price will depend on the number of meals you choose to eat per day on campus).


IMPORTANT : student residences do not provide blankets or pillows. You will therefore need to take your own or order them online and have them delivered to Brockport for your arrival (do not order too early!).
schools.courses:
Credits

The Brockport College curriculum provides a maximum of 45 ECTS credits (=12 local credits). The 15 missing credits must be obtained with EPITECH, up to 3 cumulatives options are possible:

  • a part-time job (2 credits/months)
  • a full-time job (4 credits/months)
  • HUB activities / extra curricular engagement
  • up to 3 modules NO-GO on Paris Campus

Send a Zammad ticket to "Direction des études" for all educational questions.


Academic Calendar (more information here)

You will arrive in mid-January and classes will end in mid-May.


Classes

You will complete a semester in the spring by following 4 classes validated by Epitech (each worth 3 local credits) including at least 3 computer courses. The last course must be a business course.


Classes are taught in English.


The course registration for the Spring Semester will happen the first week of December.


  • Computer courses validated by Epitech:


CSC 356 - Life in the Digital Age (A,I,W,Y). (3 credits hours)

Studies the impact of new technologies on a global society. Includes the changing nature of privacy and growing use of government surveillance, ie. national ID cards and RFID tracking. Also considers the Internet's effect on societal communication and differences in gender communication patterns, issues of freedom of expression and censorship, the influence of technology in the workplace and at home, and other relevent topics.


CSC 406 – Algorithms and Data Structures (3 credits hours)

Covers design and analysis of data structures and associated algorithms using object-oriented methods. Includes these topics: complexity measures, pre-and post-conditions, programming to interfaces, union-find sets, hashing, trees (AVL, splay, B-Trees), graphs, recursion, algorithm design strategies and NP-completeness. Extensive programming.

Attention: good level required in math


CSC 421 – Computer and Network Security (3 credits hours)

Studies concepts, techniques, and tools in computer and network security. Includes these topics: security, privacy, information assurance, threats, user authentication and access control; UNIX and Windows examples; logs and intrusion detection; cryptography, public-key and private-key systems, Kerberos, IP security, firewalls, Web and database access control and security issues; ethical issues. CSC 421 uses the UNIX, Linux and Windows operating systems extensively to understand their various security features. Students understand the security features, algorithms, information/file organization and structure, and the various aspects related to network security. The students also work with Digital Signatures, Certificates, Public Keys and other security features in the Internet Explorer and Firefox web browsers. Using the ABI-Coder 3.6.1.4 software, students can encrypt and decrypt files using various popular encryption and decryption algorithms. Students also use John the Ripper 1.7.9 to experiment with software to crack passwords, and to get an understanding of how passwords are stored in password files.


CSC 422 – Relational Database Design (3 credits hours)

Provides a study of the theory and practice of the relational approach to database design. Includes these topics: nature of relational databases, relational algebra, normalization, lossless and/or dependency preserving decomposition, query languages such as SQL and a language that is available on the system, remote connectivity, integrity and security, and database project design and implementation. CIS 422 covers various aspects of relational database design and implementation using the MySQL 5.1 open source version of SQL database. MySQL provides support for many database features such as enforcement of integrity constraints, foreign keys, stored procedures and functions, triggers, and views. In addition, the phpMyAdmin tool written in PHP is used to handle the administration of MySQL over the Web. CIS 422 also uses Java and Java Database Connectivity (JDBC), a Java-based data access technology, to implement database access via a Java program. Students write Java programs with embedded SQL code and transfer that between the Java program and the database. The resulting data set received from database is passed on to the Java program, which will then decide how to display it to the user.


CIS 427 - Project Management and Practice (3 credits hours)

Introduces software development and management of the development process. Includes these topics: managing the software life cycle (requirements definition, logical design, physical design, implementation, testing, system integration, maintenance); design techniques (structured, event-driven, object-oriented); implementation; testing and software quality assurance; delivery and user training; metrics for project management and system performance evaluation; management expectations; personnel management, cost analysis and change management; management of behavioral and technical project aspects.


CSC 429 – Object-Oriented Programming (3 credits hours)

Provides an introduction to OOP concepts and their applications using Java. Includes these topics: review of OOP fundamentals, UML modeling; advanced Java features: interfaces, abstract classes, GUI programming, layout managers, event and exception handlers, etc.; software design principles, cohesion and coupling; detailed coverage of design patterns: model-view-controller, observer, adapter, factory, strategy, singleton, etc.; software quality assurance: testing strategies. Requires extensive programming.


CIS 434 - Decision Support and Expert Systems (3 credits hours)

Covers Decision Support Systems (DSS) and its subsystems. Includes the following topics: DSS overview, modeling and analysis using linear programming, decision tables, trees, AHP, etc., group decision support systems, fundamentals of AI, expert systems, expert system building tools, and validation, knowledge representation. Involves hands-on experience with Excel LP Solver, Scenarios, Goal Seeking, etc., and DSS and ES software tools such as Expert Choice, Expertise2Go, etc.


CSC 486 – Junior/Senior Seminar (3 credits hours)

Provides an overall view of the professional field of computing, emphasizing development of communication skills for the profession. Includes these topics: detailed history of computing technology, social effects of computing, ethics in the field, professional literature, organizations and related activities, current industrial, social, legal governmental and technical developments, and career opportunities. Requires extensive reading and writing, both technical and non-technical, as well as library research, and prepared group discussions and oral presentations.


CSC 483 – Theory of Computation (3 credits hours)

Provides a study of formal languages and theory of automata with an emphasis on Church's thesis and the "algorithm = machine" point of view. Includes these topics: regular expressions and context-free languages, finite and pushdown automata, Turing machines, computability, undecidability, and complexity of problems.


Math 481 – Discrete Mathematics II (3 credits hours)

A second course in discrete mathematics. Includes: study of algorithms, recurrence relations, inclusion-exclusion principle, partial order and equivalence relations, graph theory and trees.


CPS 301 - Issues in Criminal and Forensic Computing (A,I). (3 credits hours)

A discussion of issues related to the use of computers in the criminal justice system. Discussions of growing capabilities in and ramifications of such areas as forensic computing, criminal profiling, fingerprint identification, video image processing, and simulation of crime scenes. In addition, discussions of emerging and future trends in the use of computers as a crime fighting tool.


  • Complementary courses validated by Epitech :

BUS 325 – Principles of Finance (3 credits hours)

Provides a foundation in corporate financial decision-making. Covers the corporate environment, time value of money, risk and return, diversification, market efficiency, and valuation. Applies these concepts to financial analysis and planning, capital budgeting and financing.


PLS 111 – International Relations (3 credits hours)

Studies the macro international political system, traditional power politics and theories, emerging global interdependence, and the challenge represented by terrorism and globalization.


ECN 201 – Principles of Micro-economics (3 credits hours)

Covers issues of scarcity and choice; determination of prices, demand and supply, production, cost, behavior of the firm, and the role of government.


ECN 202 – Principles of Macro-economics (3 credits hours)

Covers problems of the aggregate economy and the policies used to control those problems.


ACC 281 – Introduction to Financial Accounting (3 credits hours)

Provides an introduction to generally accepted accounting principles used to classify, value, and record assets, liabilities, stockholder equity, revenues and expenses. Preparation, interpretation and analysis of financial statements are discussed. Also, the importance of accounting information for interested parties outside the enterprise is addressed. Ethical codes and professional conduct of accountants are examined.


BUS 335 – Principles of Marketing (3 credits hours)

Examines the business function that identifies current unfilled needs and wants, defines and measures their magnitudes, determines which target markets the organization can best serve, and decides upon appropriate products, services, and programs to serve these markets. Topics include product development and test-marketing, product planning and new product introduction, and methods of product promotion and service marketing.


BUS 345 – International Business Environment (3 credits hours)

Analyzes the environmental aspects of foreign countries, the ability to promote trade with other countries, and the sovereign rights of other nations and their people.


BUS 365 – Principles of Management (3 credits hours)

Discusses the relationship of the management function with other functional areas, and provides an overview of the full span of managerial responsibilities in business organizations.


BUS 368 - Project Management Skills (3 credits hours)

This course continues to develop knowledge and skills that are key to success as a manager, with emphasis on knowledge and skills associated with project management. Students will utilize project management tools, including PERT/CPM, Gantt charts, and Project Management Software as well as continue to develop their ability to work in teams, effectively communicate, and manage deadlines and resources.

schools.overview:
The Hague University of Applied Sciences (in Dutch: De Haagse Hogeschool) was founded in September 1987.

It has four campuses located in the south of the country in The Hague, Delft, Zoetermeer, and Laan van Poot.

The main campus is in The Hague.

The university includes several faculties and research groups, and more than 23,400 students are enrolled in Bachelor or Master programs on its campuses.

The university offers its students the possibility to follow, in particular, the programs of:

  • 42 full-time Bachelors
  • 21 work-study Bachelors
  • 10 dual-component Bachelors
  • 7 Masters

This university has both a theoretical and a practical approach.

The Bachelors and Masters programs are regularly reviewed and tailored to be in tune with the current job market.

The international aspect is an important element for the University of Applied Sciences in The Hague, and students come from all over the world to enroll in its programs.

THE HONG KONG UNIVERSITY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY

In 1989, the leaders of Hong Kong recognized a growing need: to build a research-driven university that would empower the city’s future not only as a financial hub of Asia, but also as a center of innovation, knowledge, and regional influence. Positioned at a pivotal moment when China had just opened to reforms, Hong Kong’s unique role in the Pearl River Delta Region made it the ideal ground for such an institution.

Thus began the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST)—a bold vision brought to life by a community of high-spirited scholars from around the globe who embraced the challenge of building a world-class institution from the ground up.

“I am proud to see that HKUST has not diverted from the mission its founders have bestowed upon it – to create, and not to replicate; and to assist in the economic and social development of Hong Kong and beyond.”

— Professor Wei SHYY, President, HKUST


A Legacy of Excellence

Today, HKUST stands as a global powerhouse in higher education, consistently recognized for its innovation and academic excellence. The university has left a significant mark across a range of disciplines, including:

  • Life Sciences
  • Engineering
  • Business Education
  • Humanities and Social Sciences


Innovation is embedded in HKUST’s DNA. The institution is home to bold thinkers, trailblazers, and passionate changemakers dedicated to improving lives and defying limits.


Rankings & Recognition

  • #17 Worldwide in Computer Science
  • #2 in Greater China
  • #1 in Hong Kong
  • — Times Higher Education World University Rankings by Subject (2020)

Additional Programme Specifics

  • Students with a Chinese passport are not allowed to apply to this university


The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

Officially established in June 2022, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) is a legally-independent educational institution co-established by the Mainland and Hong Kong. HKUST(GZ) will explore new frontiers in cross-disciplinary education and innovate pedagogies. By doing so, HKUST(GZ) will play a constructive role in cultivating forward-looking talents with global vision, promoting the higher education reform at a national level, and accelerating educational collaboration between Hong Kong and Mainland as well as the development of the Greater Bay Area (GBA).

  • College System

HKUST (GZ) adopts the collegiate system for its undergraduate education, where colleges and hubs collaborate with each other

  • Innovative Teaching

Inline with the individualized approach, undergraduate teaching has been transformed from a traditional teaching model into an innovative modular one.

  • Multi-modal Learning

The "immersive teaching" and "group project-based learning" models reshape the teacher's role from a traditional lecturer to an actual coach and mentor.

  • Intergrating Ressources

Under the Unified HKUST-Complementary Campuses framework, HKUST and HKUST (GZ) share resources with each other such as laboratories, libraries, courses and teachers, etc.

schools.name: The University of Osaka
schools.overview:
The University of Osaka, founded in 1931, is one of Japan's leading research and higher education institutions. Located in the heart of the dynamic Kansai region, it stands out for its commitment to innovation and academic excellence. With 11 faculties, 16 graduate schools, and numerous specialized research centers, the university offers a wide range of programs covering natural sciences, engineering, social sciences, and humanities.

The University of Osaka is characterized by its international and collaborative environment, welcoming students and researchers from around the world. The institution places a particular emphasis on interdisciplinary research and sustainable development, preparing its students to tackle the global challenges of the 21st century. In addition to its rigorous academic programs, the university offers opportunities for personal and professional development, creating an ecosystem conducive to innovation and leadership.

With a rich tradition of excellence and a forward-looking vision, The University of Osaka is a pillar of education and research, significantly contributing to scientific advancements and social progress.

Food

The price of food will vary depending on whether you wish to cook for yourself or not. Japan has a great system of readymade meals prepared at supermarkets and convenience stores that are very cheap. You can therefore pay around 8€ a day for eating your lunch and your dinner from there. You can sometimes pay even less as some supermarkets put discounts on meals after a certain hour. It is entirely possible to eat a lunch and dessert for 4€ in Japan by waiting for those discounts. It is popularly said that those meals go bad after one day and you must eat them the day they are made.

If you have a fridge, you can store them for up to two weeks. It is therefore possible to eat for 40€ a week in Japan.

Vegetables, fruits, and rice is very expensive in Japan. A kilo of rice itself costs between 4€ and 5€. Anything meat related is mostly cheap.

It would overall cost as much as to eat readymade meals or cooking for yourself depending on how you eat.

Tongji University

The history of Tongji University can be traced back to 1907 when the Deutsch Medical School was founded by Erich Paulun, a German doctor in Shanghai.

In 1996, Tongji merged with the Shanghai Institute of Urban Construction and Shanghai Institute of Building Materials and was listed later in Project 211. In 2000, the expanded Tongji merged again with Shanghai Tiedao University and developed into the new Tongji. Then, in 2002, it was listed in Project 985 and took charge of the administration of the Shanghai College of Aviation Industry in 2003. In May 2007, Tongji celebrated its Centenary Celebration. Since 2013, Tongji has established the goal to be a Sustainability-Oriented World’s Top University.

Tsinghua University

When it was created in 1911, Tsinghua was initially a preparatory school for Chinese students wishing to do a second cycle at American universities. In 1925, it developed into a full-fledged university and now offers undergraduate and graduate degree programs.

For decades, Tsinghua University has been considered the "MIT of China." Beginning in the late 1980s, the state began to design a new Tsinghua that included more diverse disciplines. By April of 2005, the university was able to develop 13 faculties, 54 departments, 41 research institutes, 35 research centers, and 171 laboratories; including 12 national laboratories and 15 laboratories of the Ministry of Education.


Currently, among the 7,800 teachers at Tsinghua, there is a Nobel Prize winner (Zhenning Yang), a Turing Prize winner (Qizhi Yao), thirty-five members of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and thirty-one members of the Chinese Academy of Engineering.

Many students study at Tsinghua: 13,000 undergraduates, 13,000 masters, 5,000 doctoral, 1,700 foreigners from 46 countries and 9,000 through correspondence education courses.


For Chinese high school students, Tsinghua is one of two mainland universities with the most selective admissions process. Each year in all provinces, those admitted are only those with the best marks. After studying for the bachelor's degree, a considerable part of Tsinghua's students will pursue their doctoral work at American universities.


At Tsinghua, "Action is more important than words," and the school motto emphasizes everyone's constant efforts and high moral standards.


Among the eminent alumni of Tsinghua we find political leaders, great scientists, and the leaders of important companies. For example, Xi Jinping, the current President of the People's Republic of China; Jiaxian Deng, "the father of China's two nuclear bombs"; and Zhang Chaoyang, the creator of the Sohu website and the CEO of Sohu, one of the first Internet portals in China.

  • 180 ECTS certificate document (ask the AFFI team)
  • Copy of your passport

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


2. Acceptance letter

Once you've submitted your application, your host university will review your documents.

You will then receive an acceptance letter (might take a few weeks), mandatory to apply for a visa.


3. Visa application

You must take the necessary steps in obtaining a study visa type X1 upon receipt of the letter of admission and the form JW202 (sent to you by email). Please check this site for more information. Price: between 110 and 130€ (2025). You can also entrust the file to an agency by clicking here.


The X1 visa is an entry visa valid for 3 months from the date of entry into China. After your arrival, you must obtain a Chinese residence permit within 30 days of entering China.


The host university will assist you with visa conversion procedures, medical examinations, and obtaining the resident permit.

Related costs are the responsibility of the students (see estimated budget at the bottom of the page).


Please note:

  • For the latest information regarding visa application, you should contact your nearest Embassy/Consulate of China.
  • After you arrive in the Chinese mainland, the X visa for single entry cannot allow you to exit and re-enter the Chinese mainland. You must stay in the Chinese mainland until the Residence Permit is granted.


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "For the Visa, I got my visa in less than a week after making my demand by going to the Chinese Visa center of Marseille which has a usual delay of < 1 week, with no need to book a meeting in advance. I would not recommend going to the Visa center of Paris, as the delay is much higher (expect at least 2 weeks in addition to having to book a meeting with them ahead)."


4. Insurance and health

You will be asked to undergo medical examinations after arriving in Beijing.

The results must be presented to the Beijing Bureau of Exit and Entry Administration of the Ministry of Public Security when you apply for a residence permit.


The costs of these exams will be borne by the student (see “Estimated Budget”).


According to the regulations made by Chinese Ministry of Education, all the international students in China are required to purchase comprehensive insurance and the valid period should cover the duration of their studies.


In order to be fully covered for medical care, we recommend that you take out international insurance as well. It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "Although Tsinghua requires a medical certificate along with blood test and vaccines to be done ahead of arriving in China, nearly every foreign student needs to undergo another medical test upon arriving, which leads me to believe that doing the medical exam before arriving in China is not mandatory and is not taken into account."


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/chine

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on China, click here.

Student's feedback regarding what to anticipate for your arrival at Tsinghua (2024-2025): "When arriving in Tsinghua University, foreign students will need to register. To do that, they will go in front of Building 23 where all other foreign students will also be, that way, you just have to follow the others. There will a be quick lesson on how to prevent fires, use an extinguisher and what practices are forbidden in order to avoid a fire. After finishing that test, you will need to bring the documents you had to prepare (such as a photocopy of your passport, some cash for the administrative fees) and that were mentionned in the mails you received. Some documents will have to be obtained directly on site.


The medical certifiate is not mandatory to start registering and obtain your dormitory room key. It will however, be needed to finalize the registration later on. To obtain your dormitory room key, simply go to the the building you booked a room in and present your registration documents to the reception.


It is not possible to go to the campus restaurant without a student ID. If you want to eat and don't know any student that can help you, you can still go to the multiple supermarkets on campus and pay either by cash or WeChat/Alipay.


After the first day, you will need to go the health center to undergo the medical exam. There are two days, generally the first Thursday and first Friday, where all foreign students will go to the center. You can organize between students to take a taxi or didi (chinese equivalent of uber).


It will also be from Thirsday to Friday that the course registration platform will open. Bear in mind that slots go extremely fast and are limited. Be prepared to be in a place with a good connection and on your computer at the exact time the platform opens.


Classes only start the second week. You have one week to accommodate and adapt to the Chinese lifestyle before starting to study. During week one, a​ big meeting will be organized on campus where all foreign students must go. They will communicate informations relative to campus life. Do not worry, all these informations will be communicated either by the management team the first day, or via wechat in the groups they will have make you join."
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

Accommodations are provided in an on-campus dormitory. Due to limited space in campus dorms, rooms on campus are reserved only for those who have applied directly to the university before the stated deadline.


Booking instructions are provided in the admission package sent by Tsinghua.


You can choose between three types of rooms:

  • Single room (bathroom and private toilet)
  • Room AB (bathroom and toilet shared with the flat mate)
  • Double rooms (bathroom and toilet shared).

In each room you will find sheets, color TV, air conditioning, telephone and internet access.


Plan 300 euros per month for a single room (with private bathroom) with cleaning service and bedding. You can find Information on the dormitory here: http://ac.cs.tsinghua.edu.cn/accomodation.html

Student's feedback (2024-2025): "Foreign students and Chinese students are not in the same building, except for some very special cases.


There are two types of room : AB room and double rooms.

Double rooms contain 2 people and is a single room. There is a big shower room per floor shared by all people from that floor.

AB Rooms have a bathroom in them, and separate bedrooms. They contain 2 people. This type of room is not going to exist for a long time as they are getting replaced by double rooms. They also cost twice as much as Double rooms.

Depending on the building, some double rooms have sinks in them and bunk beds, while other have distinct beds, but no sinks.

Building 23 : Mixed building with men on floor 1 to 6 and women on floor 7 to 12. Distinc beds, no sink.

Building 22 : Only men. Bunk beds, sink.

Building 21 : Currently on renovation.

Building 20 : AB rooms.

Building 19 : Same as building 21, only women


I would recommend taking a double room for economic reason, and because double rooms are visually more pleasant than AB rooms, except for people that specifically cannot withstand having a shared room.

For the building, I would recommend taking building 22 or 19 as having a sink is very useful to brush your teeth and other things without having to go out. But for those that prefer separate beds and more space, then building 23 is the best option."


Off-campus acommodation (more information here)

Due to limited amount of accommodation available on campus, some students will need to live off-campus and arrange accommodation in advance. 

Notes:

  • always keep copies of all payments and the contract
  • always sign a contract. Without a contract you have no legal rights
  • when you live off-campus, never forget to register at your local police station to obtain a Registration Form of Temporary Residence within 24 hours after your arrival in China or signing of the rental contract.


Finding accommodation via reputable rental agencies

Due to its close proximity to Tsinghua University, many students living off campus choose to live in apartment blocks located in the Wudaokou and Liudaokou areas


Below are the main rental agencies in China. Before your arrival, you can first access their websites to learn of their accommodation options. Then once in China, you can go to their neighborhood shopfronts to request to view properties.


  • Ziroom is a popular choice for foreigners renting in Beijing. They have an easy-to-use app that also has an English interface for searching for accommodation. Once securing accommodation via Ziroom, on the app you can find the details of your accommodation, including the contract and details on your payments made. Included in the contract is a service fee, which includes regular cleaning of the public spaces of the apartment, and also easy servicing for repairs. You will also be advised to add your agent on WeChat for ease of contact.
  • Lianjia
  • 5i5j

Credits

Students must validate 15 local credits for the 1st semester and 12 local credits for the 2nd semester among the courses below.


Academic calendar (2025-2026)

Fall semester: Sept 15-Jan 19 or 22

Spring semester: Feb 15-June 30


Department and courses

Tsinghua University offers 2 programs to our students and will decide in which program you will be accepted according to the profile of each applicant.


Epitech students admitted as "visiting students" will take classes in the Master in Advanced Computing program of the Computer Science and Technology department.

  • Chinese Language (2 credits)
  • Overview of China (2 credits)
  • Combinatorics and Algorithms Design (4 credits)
  • Advanced Machine Learning (3 credits)
  • Web Information Retrieval (3 credits)
  • Future Internet (3 credits)
  • Distributed Database Systems (3 credits)
  • Human Computer Interaction Technologies (3 credits)
  • Fundamentals of Computer Graphics (3 credits)
  • Topics in Advanced Multimedia Technologies (3 credits)
  • Process and Methods of Software Project Management (3 credit)
  • Introduction to big data systems (3 credits)
  • Advanced Network Management (3 credits)
  • Distributed Systems (3 credits)
  • Network Security (2 credits)
  • Natural Language Processing (3 credits)
  • Deep Learning (3 credits)

You will find the list of courses here.


Course format and workload

The mathematics courses are very high level, and we urge each candidate to take this element into account when choosing Tsinghua University.


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "Courses in Tsinghua can be overwhelming or relatively easy based on what kind of classes you take. It is true that the expected math level is high, but definitively not out of range for a dedicated student (I am talking about students that want to learn and improve, not necessarily the students with a social life). Chinese classes are available for different levels--from beginner (A1 / HSK1), intermediate (B1 / HSK 3) to advanced (A1~A2 / HSK5).

The first week, you can register and unregister from any class you want, as long as it has enough slots. This way, you can try classes you are not sure to be fit for, and even go to classes you are not registered for.


Past that delay, you will need to make a special demand to register to some courses, which is done via the same platform, altough this time, the teacher will need to manually accept your demand instead of being registered right away.


If you want to register for a class that has no more slots, you can go to the FIT building in Tsinghua, and go talk to the foreign students manager, and give her your name and student ID, so that, if any slots is free, you will automatically be registered.

The hardest classes in Tsinghua are definitively the ones about AI (Machine Learning, Deep learning, NLP, ...). These will need a lot of investment and the homework will take a lot of time. I do not recommend taking 2 or more, except if the classes didn't seem overwhelming during the first week.


Most classes take ~2h30 per week, so to get the number of credits required by Epitech, you will usually just go to class in the morning and have a free afternoon. This is because Chinese teachers expect you to work much more out of class than during class. Some classes will have homework, some will have projects, and they will either have a final exam and mid-term exam, or have a final project (like Epitech)."


Example of two schedules for the two semesters (2024-2025):


Monday: no classes

Tuesday: Natural Language Processing (9:50-12:15)

Important notes

  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.

Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Insurance from Tsinghua: 78€, 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage
  • Visa: between 110-130€
  • Administrative fees and other expenses: at least 800yuan in cash (100€) according to a former student (2024-2025), etc.


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Yuan (RMB or CNY). 1 € = 8.26 RMB (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

  • Housing: 600€/semester (double rooms), 1200€/semester (AB rooms)
  • Food : 70€ / month (only eating at campus restaurants), 100€ / month (campus restaurants most of the time + some restaurants outside)
  • Transportation: 25-30€ for a second-hand bike
  • Phone, internet: 16€ internet/ 6€ phone
  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure: 200€ (1-week trip with normal trains, restaurants, museums, etc.) or 500€ (1-week trip with plane or high-speed train)

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.

schools.overview:
IMPORTANT - Additional Programme Requirements


Students must submit the following test results with choices in order to be eligible for this destination:


TOEFL: 90 (at home test accepted) IELTS or Academic Format: 7 or DAAD: C1 or Cambridge C1 Advanced or TEM-4 or TEM-8: Level 70 or Duolingo: 125


___________________________________________________________________________________________


University of California, Berkeley

UC Berkeley is the first campus of the University of California. It is the only campus authorized to use any of the names: University of California, Cal or Berkeley. Among the alumni, professors and researchers associated with the University, there are 65 Nobel Prize winners, 19 Oscars winners and 11 Pulitzer Prize winners.

The institution is ranked among the top 5 universities in the world alongside Harvard, Cambridge, Oxford, and Stanford. The University of Shanghai ranked it, in 2007 and 2008, in 3rd place among the best universities in the world.

Founded in 1891, UC Berkeley Extension is the continuing education branch of the prestigious University of California Berkeley. The school is spread over three campuses (Berkeley, San Francisco and Belmont) and offers students from around the world nearly 75 professional certificates and specialized programs. Its HAAS Business School is one of the best in the country.

Its diplomas and certificates are issued by professionals accredited by Berkeley and adhere to the quality and teaching standards defined by the university. At UC Berkeley Extension, you will be immersed in an active and diverse student community in the heart of San Francisco Bay, a region known for its entrepreneurial dynamism. Many of its programs are developed by experts in the field, who constantly adapt their lessons to the needs of the job market.The program at this university emphasizes entrepreneurship and innovation in digital and global markets.

1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

2. Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.


1/Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to UC Berkeley Extension, you will receive an I-20 form allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

Mid-August to mid-May


Department and Courses

The program will be taught in English and is not a diploma. It will focus on pre-selected business areas, such as entrepreneurship, leadership innovation / management, and new product development, and will include activity-based teaching.

You will find the details of the program here (Graduate Track):

https://extension.berkeley.edu/international/academic/bhgap/curriculum/#!#entrepreneurshipS22CG


Berkeley Haas Global Access Program (BHGAP) Curriculum

Graduate Track – Fall 2024 – Spring 2025


To earn the BHGAP Diploma Certificate (2 semester program), students must complete the following:

  • Students must enroll in at least 12 units and not more than 15 units per semester in all courses taken at the University of California
  • Students must complete a minimum of 9 units of BHGAP Curriculum (core and electives) each semester
  • Students will be automatically enrolled in BHGAP core courses
  • Students must complete at least 18 units of BHGAP curriculum over the duration of the program
  • Courses will not be counted twice for credit
  • Students must complete a minimum of 1 unit through the concurrent enrollment system each semester enrolled
  • Students must complete a minimum of 24 units of courses taken at the University of California


Additional requirements:

  • Students must successfully complete all courses with a grade of C or better
  • Students must earn a final program GPA of 2.5 or higher based on all courses taken

The University of Cadiz (UCA) is the public university of the Spanish province of Cadiz. It includes more than 1,500 teachers and welcomes around 20,000 students from many countries.


The University of Cadiz was founded in 1979, although several of its faculties already existed previously as schools or faculties independent of the University of Seville.

Its motto is "Sapere Aude", or: "Dare to know."

schools.name: Universidad de Monterrey
schools.overview:
Universidad de Monterrey, acronym "UDEM", is a private Catholic-inspired educational institution, open to all creeds and conditions, founded in 1969.

The UDEM Campus is located in the municipality of San Pedro Garza Garcia belonging to the Metropolitan Area of Monterrey, Nuevo Leon, Mexico.

It is home to about 16,000 students, primarily in undergraduate programs. The campus is nestled in the mountains, just outside of the city of Monterrey.

UDEM was founded by the Daughters of the Immaculate Mary of Guadalupe, the nuns of the Sacred Heart, the Marist Brothers, and the La Salle members, supported by an association of Catholic citizens.

The idea originated from a recommendation given by the Second Vatican Council to use educational activities in favor of teaching the principles of the Catholic doctrine.

1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application.

All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline).

If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet — please be patient.

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Visa

In France: student Student Temporary Resident Visa (more information here and here)

Once you receive the acceptance letter from the partner university, you will be able to apply for a visa. Please refer to the Mexican Embassy or Consulate closer to you to ensure you have the proper documentation before arriving in Mexico.


General requirements:

  • Original passport that is valid for at least three months longer than your intended stay in Mexico. Photocopies of the main pages (personal data, expiration date, and photograph).
  • Visa application form, duly completed and bearing your signature. The application form is available at the website of the corresponding embassy or consulate.
  • Acceptance letter from UDEM. Sometimes you will be asked to submit a photocopy and sometimes they will keep the original document. Because of this, we suggest that you always keep a copy.
  • You must prove financial solvency and that you can provide yourself with at least USD$300 per month.
  • If the holders of the bank account that you will be using for proof of financial solvency are your parents, you must submit the banking certificate and a letter of promise from your parents in which they pledge to support you financially during the duration of your stay in Mexico. If you have a scholarship, you must submit a letter of proof that includes the amount of your scholarship.
  • Photographs (the format and number vary in each embassy and consulate).


Arrival in Mexico: Residence Card (more information here and here)

Your pre-approved visa is valid for entry into Mexico only 1 time and you must enter Mexico within 180 days of issuance. Once in Mexico you have 30 days to apply to your local National Migration Institute (INM) for the residence card that accredits their legal stay in the country and allows them to remain in Mexico.


Notes:

  • The process must be carried out in the city of your campus.
  • The INM closes at 1:00 p.m. We recommend that you arrive on time for your appointment.
  • Make the appointment as soon as you arrive to Mexico, because sometimes the waiting time may exceed the 30 days you have to make this process.
  • Write exactly the full names and surnames with which the person is being identified foreigner in the processing request. (Regardless of the number of names and surnames).


3. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out an international insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. 

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information. 


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/mexique


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html


4.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Mexico, click here.

Facilities include: a library, a bookstore, computer labs, workshops, a cafeteria, coffee shops, a gymnasium, football and tennis courts, banks, a medical clinic, etc.

Number of local credits to be earned per year: 72 (approximately 36 per semester).

Students must take 36 credits per semester in order to obtain 60 ECTS for the year.

Courses are worth 6 Mexican credits each

Fall semester: Early August - Early December

Spring semester: Mid January - Late May


Department and Courses

Students may take courses from one of the following programs in Engineering and Technologies:

  • Electronic Technology and Robotics (3rd year courses or higher)
  • Computer Science (3rd year courses or higher)

Some Computer Science, Engineering, Graphic Design, and Business courses are available in English.

You can see the English courses available on UDEM’s website, but keep in mind that these could change from year to year. Students may also take beginner courses in business, finance, economics, etc.

It is possible to take courses in English and in Spanish. However, the choice of courses in English is somewhat limited.

If you are interested in taking courses in Spanish, you must have at least a B1 level, which will be checked by the partner university via a Spanish proficiency test during orientation.

Courses includes additional independent work (practical work, tutorials, fieldwork, homework, individual study, and other assessment activities)

schools.overview:
Created in 1997, the University of Vic – Central University of Catalonia is a Catalan university with campuses in Vic, Manresa, and Granollers. It is a private institution, managed by the private Balmes University Foundation. There are nearly 5,000 students enrolled at the university.


The University of Vic keeps alive the values of:

  • The unity of knowledge
  • Human training through the acquisition of science
  • The practice of research and technological innovation
  • — in the service of progress and quality of life


Why Choose Vic


Choosing to study in Vic means investing in the quality of education and the quality of life in a university city on a human scale.


This medieval city is accessible by train from Barcelona


Allow a good hour, €13 one-way ticket.

For European students


The European Health Insurance Card (CEAM in French) is nominative and individual.


This card certifies your rights to the Health Insurance in Europe.


To obtain your card, log in to your Ameli account at least two months before your departure.


It is free of charge and will be sent to your place within two weeks.


You can also download it online.

You must register for a private health insurance to cover your full stay.

schools.accomodation:
Campus life


Located one hour from Barcelona, discover the city of Vic here!


Halfway between the Pyrenees mountains and the Mediterranean, Vic is a main administrative, population and service center with an area of influence that includes 150,000 inhabitants.


Means of transport to get to Vic:


Barcelona airport - Sants - Vic (train: http://www.renfe.com/viajeros/cercanias/barcelona/)
schools.courses:
You must obtain 30 ECTS credits per semester, i.e. 60 ECTS credits for the year among the courses in the link below (see syllabus tab):


https://www.uvic.cat/en/international/exchange-programmes/courses


The courses are in English and you will find that they are more multimedia-oriented.


You can find the academic calendar here.


You will study in the 'Faculty of Science and Technology'.


Look in the Communication and Engineering sections.


The University of Vic is a public university under private management. This makes the school a lot more open and welcoming to international students.


In terms of courses, as an Epitech student, it is quite the opposite of the usual project and topics proposed in the first 3 years. The engineering campus offers most mechatronics courses, usually for bachelor's degree students. Nonetheless, it requires a lot of knowledge in applied Mathematics and Physics that can be challenging. Otherwise, there are also courses in Multimedia which include a variety of video game development and game design courses. The consensus is that there is not as much programming in the proposed courses, however, there is much knowledge to gain about the hardware part of a machine system.


Evaluation:


Each course has a maximum of 4-5 assignments during the semester as well as a partial exam that happens mid-semester.

Depending on the course there will also be an exam at the end or a submission of a project.

All the above contribute to the final grade which should be above 5/10 to pass the course.

If a class is not passed, there is a chance of doing a recovery exam.


It is important to note that the University has a good number of courses taught in English for international students.

Students can also choose to do courses in Spanish or Catalan depending on their level of fluency.

The level of English of the professors is quite good and in addition to that there are some professors that are not originally from Spain.


Talking about language, the university offers Spanish and Catalan classes with validation credits of 3 each.

It would be a good idea to take the classes since they not only teach about the language but also about the culture in Catalunya as well as what to expect.


Attendance:


As for attendance in classes, it is as strict as the professor; in some cases, it contributes to the overall grade; in others, certain absences can be tolerated.

We remind you that attendance is compulsory, under penalty of exclusion from the university.


Campus life is dynamic since there is a lot of activities organised by the school, ranging from concerts to expositions.

The University is situated in city of Vic which is in the province of Barcelona.

The city is not very big therefore most students will venture to Barcelona for weekends of partying and exploring.

Overall life in Vic is pretty serene with great access to nature as well as the city.


The course list is given to you for information purposes. It can change from year to year.

If a class is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible.


EIP: Any tech4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance them.

schools.overview:

Finis Terrae University is a private Chilean university based in the capital Santiago. It was founded in 1988. It is one of the best universities in Chile with its Master Cycle accredited by the Chilean Ministry of National Education. This university has more than 4,000 students on an American-style campus in an upscale residential area of Santiago.

Santiago offers a unique mix of mountains, sea, and city life. In just one day, you can go skiing to the Cordillera de los Andes and later enjoy water sports at the beach—only 1.5 hours away! You can also go trekking or try paddleboarding on nearby lakes. There are amazing nature trails just outside the city.

As the capital, Santiago has great flight connections, making it easy to travel around Chile and South America quickly and easily.

If your studies in Chile will last more than 6 months, you must apply for a Student Visa (Temporary Residence Permit – Student Subcategory). If your stay is less than 6 months, we still recommend applying for the student visa, but it's up to you.

Once you receive an acceptance letter from the university, you can start applying for a student residence visa according to the instructions given to you on the website of the Consulate of Chile in Paris, accessible here.


Chilean authorities generally require proof of sufficient financial means to cover the stay; as a reference, it is recommended to demonstrate access to at least 500 USD per month of stay (6,000 USD for 12 months).


Important notes:

Finis Terrae University will assist you in this procedure.

In Chile, healthcare is not free. Medical services are private and often very expensive.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

Universidad Nacional de Colombia (UNAL)

The National University of Colombia was founded in 1867.

It is the largest Colombian university. The main campus is located in the city of Bogota. It has become the most significant and representative university in Colombia because of its rich tradition, prestige, and quality. It is connected to the history and academic achievements of both the country and Latin America. It is in this university that almost 90% of the country’s scientific research is carried out.

In 2017, its engineering faculty was recognized nationally and internationally for its academic excellence and the professional competence of its graduates.

The latter, in addition to mastering a foreign language, are noted for their leadership and their entrepreneurial spirit in the fields of:

  • Sustainable development
  • Innovation
  • Economic and social development of the country

Upon arrival in Colombia, you will need to apply for a residence permit (Cédula de Extranjería). Your passport including the visa and your residence card will be presented to the International Relations Office of UNAL (ORI) upon orientation to be able to finalize your registration.

For more information on visa procedures, visit the embassy website here.


3. Insurance and Health


It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

UNAL insists that you be covered on the following points:


General or Natural Illness and Personal Accidents:

  1. Medical assistance due to an accident
  2. Medical assistance due to a non-existent illness
  3. Medical assistance due to a pre-existing illness
  4. Special illness
  5. Emergency dentistry
  6. Ambulatory medication
  7. Medication in the event of hospitalization
  8. Psychological assistance (mental health crisis) during the period of validity of the insurance


Other Hospital Services:

  1. Health transfers
  2. Prostheses (without exception)
  3. Osteosynthesis equipment
  4. Orthosis


Excess Coverage of Hospital Services:

  1. Hotel costs for convalescence (depending on network availability)
  2. Emergencies without internment (emergency hospital care without hospitalization)
  3. Diagnostic aids (specialized diagnostic tests)


Other Advantages for the Insured:

  1. Transfer of the family member for hospitalization of the insured
  2. Return trip due to the death of a parent
  3. Advice in the event of loss of documents and luggage
  4. Compensation for loss or damage to luggage
  5. Trip interruption due to disaster
  6. Accompaniment of children or adults
  7. Travel time
  8. Legal assistance for road accidents
  9. Transfer of funds for legal deposit
  10. Medical repatriation or death of the insured in the event of illness or accident


Special Conditions

The insurance must include the following compulsory minimum clauses:

  1. Minimum and maximum age for granting coverage: from the first day of birth until the age of 75
  2. Insurance operation: must operate from the moment the student approaches the means of transport to reach the country of destination, and also during the period of cover required in number of days, up to a year of coverage with automatic renewal
  3. Non-application of the surcharge by trade or activity: the insurer will not apply a surcharge for trade or activity to the insured
  4. No condition of affiliation to the compulsory health scheme: the insurer will not require affiliation to the Colombian social security system
  5. Scope of the network: coverage should be available nationally, in all major cities and capitals (Leticia, San Andres, Tumaco, Arauca)
  6. Automatic recovery of the insured value without additional premium: in the event of an incident due to illness or accident

Your international insurance certificate must be presented to ORI (with visa and residence permit) during orientation to finalize your registration.

For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/colombie

Through this program, we’ll have all sorts of fun activities for integration and cultural exchange.

The National University of La Plata (UNLP) is a public university located in La Plata, capital of the province of Buenos Aires, Argentina. According to the prestigious Shanghai ranking in 2018, it is elected 2nd university of Argentina after the University of Buenos Aires.

It was founded in the 19th century with the intention of creating a university bringing together innovative training in science, technology and culture, in a new city in full development. It is made up of 17 faculties, 10,900 academic members and more than 120,000 students.

La Plata is a beautiful town near the Rio de la Plata, whose name it inherited when it was founded. It is one of the rare cities entirely conceived and built on the basis of an ideal city project. It is a city that offers large green spaces, where it is good to stroll, and whose many museums bear witness to an important cultural life.

Universidad Panamericana

Universidad Panamericana was founded in 1967 as a business school. The original group of scholars and business people who founded the Pan-American Institute of Top Business Management (IPADE), soon began promoting what is today Universidad Panamericana.

The Pan-American Institute of Humanities (IPH), precursor to Universidad Panamericana, was founded in 1968. In 1978, IPH was elevated to the rank of university, and took the name Universidad Panamericana, even though both IPADE and IPH had initially conceived knowledge as being unitary and universal—that is, a university.

Universidad Panamericana has four campuses which give service to almost 12 thousand students in 33 degree programs. The first campus was inaugurated in Mexico City in 1968, the second in Guadalajara in 1981, and a third in Aguascalientes in 1989. Campus Santa Fe, also located in Mexico City, was inaugurated in 2011.

As one university with one spirit, UP works daily on three foundational pillars:

  • teaching
  • research
  • transmission of culture

In virtue of an agreement between the Governing Board and the Prelature of Opus Dei, Universidad Panamericana has entrusted to that Prelature the spiritual attention and doctrinal guidance of all its activities.

The University, in its few decades of life, has come to occupy a place as one of the top universities in Mexico.

Universidad Peruana de Ciencias Aplicadas

Universidad Peruana Ciencias Aplicadas is a large private university located in Lima, Peru. They have around 80,000 students enrolled in approximately 46 different programs or majors.

The Universidad Peruana de Ciencias Aplicadas has a main campus in Santiago de Surco, Lima, Peru. It is known as el Campus Monterrico, which has a size of 3 hectares.

Lima, the capital of Peru, lies on the country's arid Pacific coast. Though its colonial center is preserved, it's a bustling metropolis and one of South America’s largest cities. Founded in 2002, Universidad Tecmilenio was created to meet the changing demands of the new millennium. Their aim is to empower students to develop their own life purpose and to take charge of their own learning.

They are known for the flexibility and empowerment that they give to their students, giving them the freedom to choose their own educational program, according to their self-defined life purpose.

Based on the science of positive psychology, their university model ensures their students’ ability to compete in the global market economy and promotes the well-being and happiness of the members of our community.

Currently, with 29 campuses located in 18 states of Mexico and Tecmilenio Online®, they offer:

  • 2 high school programs
  • 28 undergraduate careers
  • 8 executive careers
  • 7 master's degree programs

The Community is Composed of:

  • 81,000 graduates
  • More than 56,000 students
  • More than 4,600 teachers
  • 1,700 employees

Tecmilenio is based on the city of Monterrey in the north of Mexico.

Monterrey is the capital of the state of Nuevo Leon and it has 1.1 million inhabitants.

schools.overview:
UNIMORE has a longstanding tradition (it was founded in 1175) and is considered one of the best universities in Italy for teaching and research. It is ranked among the top 10 large-sized Italian universities by the Censis University Ranking 2023.

UNIMORE, which has just over 28,000 students including 3,500 postgraduates, is large enough to offer all the facilities one would expect from a major university (well-stocked libraries, computer rooms, free internet connection and study support services) but small enough to retain a personal and friendly learning environment.

UNIMORE is composed of 13 Departments, 1 School of Engineering and 1 Faculty of Medicine, offering a wide range of degree programmes at undergraduate level, right up to doctoral studies in most disciplinary areas, from the humanities and social sciences to engineering and technology, and from physical and natural sciences to medicine and life sciences.

UNIMORE is located in the heart of one of Europe's wealthiest and most dynamic regions, which is world-renowned for its production of mechanical parts, engines, sports cars (e.g. Ferrari and Maserati) as well as for its agro-food sector, ceramic tiles and manufacturing industries.

UNIMORE is located in two cities with the highest quality of living standards in Italy. Both Modena and Reggio Emilia are considered important cities of art and culture.
