On-campus accommodation

You can check the following page: https://www.uqar.ca/services/services-a-l-etudiant/logements

If you wish to apply for accommodation on the Rimouski campus, you can do so upon admission to university at http://residencesuqar.com/

For a room, expect to pay about 250 euros. UQAR offers a formula with 4 bedrooms per apartment. The rooms are 9m² and are considered quite spacious. The apartment has a functional kitchen (oven/hob/fridge/freezer/storage), bright and furnished common rooms (tables/chairs/sofas)

Please note, you will be asked to send an international money order corresponding to the amount of the first month's rent (by your bank, or by post where you must fill out a form and send the amount in cash) so that your reservation can be taken into account.

The cancellation and reimbursement conditions for this amount are indicated on the residences website.

With regard to the Lévis campus, there are no residences like in Rimouski, contact the UQAR student services, they can answer you regarding accommodation in Lévis.https://www.uqar.ca/services/student-services/accommodation? slider=campus-de-levis


Off-campus accommodation

We recommend that you do not confirm an accommodation reservation or rent payment before their arrival in Rimouski. Once there, your students will be able to visit the accommodation they have pre-selected and then sign a rental contract. Student Services will be able to support them in their efforts. However, they will have to pay for temporary accommodation the time it takes to find alternate accommodation.


To start the search, we recommend the following link : https://uqar.ca/services/services-a-l-etudiant/logements


Here are some basics about housing:

  • Housing division:

The number before the “½” indicates the number of rooms making up the accommodation and the “½” represents the bathroom. For example, for your family, explore the prices of housing types 4 ½ and 5 ½. Housing 4 ½ = 4 rooms (2 bedrooms, 1 kitchen and 1 living room) + 1 bathroom.

Housing 5 ½ = 5 rooms (3 bedrooms, 1 kitchen and 1 living room) + 1 bathroom.


  • Heating and electricity:

In the ad, if it says "n-ch, n-é" it means that neither heating nor electricity is included in the monthly payments and therefore, that you will have to pay your electricity bill. You can therefore assess an additional 80$ to 120$ per month which will be added to your monthly fees.

Some units include heating and electricity, which means that the rent is fixed and includes these services.

Always ask the landlord if lighting and heating (electricity) costs are included in your rent.


  • Furniture:

In Quebec, a “semi-furnished” type apartment only includes a stove and a refrigerator (appliances). You will then need to find a table, a bed and other furniture.

Most Rimouski apartments are "unfurnished". You will then have to furnish it entirely.

It is very rare to find furnished apartments in Quebec.


  • Telecommunications

In Quebec, telecommunication services operate on a flat rate basis and are usually the responsibility of the tenant. You should allow 100$ to 120$ per month for a basic trio. The basic trios include a landline, internet connection and cable TV. Telephone calls operate on a flat rate basis. Local calls (from Rimouski to Rimouski) are free, but long distance and overseas calls are charged. Telecommunication services are much more expensive than in Europe and some cell phones in other countries do not work in Quebec.


For the Lévis campus, we also invite you to view the announcements on https://www.kijiji.ca/b-immobilier/grand-montreal/c34l80002

Here is the list of courses available for EPITECH students : UQAR courses.


1. Major in Computer Science

Possibility of obtaining a certificate. The course description can be found here for the major


Requirements to validate the major:

  • Satisfy the general regulations of the University of Quebec and the regulations of the University
  • Validate the 30 credits of the program. You must take a maximum of 10 modules over the year (5 per semester) totaling 30 local credits to obtain 60 ECTS credits.
  • Plan on having a consequential workload (2 to 3 practical works + 2 exams per course)
  • Have a 2.0/4.3 GPA (only calculated on the grades obtained at the university)
  • No outstanding fees due to the University

Goals:

Acquire or consolidate knowledge in general, from the design, development and management of IT projects. The technologies seen depend on the subjects and the teachers, their preferred fields generally being the Web (Asp.net, Java), databases (all types) and system software (C ++, Java, C #, Erlang, etc.). Mobile applications are not part of the program.


2. Certificate in Computer Science

Possibility of obtaining a certificate. The course description can be found here for the certificate.


Conditions for obtaining the certificate:

  • Satisfy the general regulations of the University of Quebec and the regulations of the University
  • Validate the 30 credits of the program
  • Have no outstanding fees due to the University
  • Have 2.0/4.3 GPA (only calculated on the grades obtained at the university)


Goals:

Acquire knowledge related to the fields of programming, software engineering and databases.

Develop skills related to the design, development and deployment of distributed systems.


Internship

It is not possible to do an internship, but it is possible to meet companies during a forum. There are also visits organized by the university and by the organization of Québec International and its 10X10 program.


Campus Selection

Students may choose between the Rimouski or the Lévis campus. The Epitech International Relations office will ask you to indicate your choice after you are placed at UQAR.


Attendance and Course Availability

Please note: Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits). The courses are much more theoretical and based on classical instruction than at Epitech.

The course list is given to you for information. It can change from year to year. If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.


Application and Program Allocation

During the selection in January, the student must apply directly to the destination and not to a specific program. The University of Quebec at Rimouski remains the decision-maker on the allocation of students to the programs after studying their application.

UQAR accepts students with a GPA between 2 and 2.49 for the certificate and a 2.5 GPA and above for the major.


Tuition Fees

Epitech will pay the tuition fees at UQAR to the extent of the 10 modules required per year (i.e. 5 per semester) to allow you to acquire the necessary credits. Any additional module you wish to take will be at your expense.


EIP

Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of your free time to work on this.

  • Paris–Quebec round trip flights: 800 euros

  • Or round trip flights Paris–Montreal: 800 euros

  • Study permit: 150$ CA

  • 370$ CA (room on the Rimouski campus)

  • Rimouski students have nearby facilities and their transportation costs amount to 0 $CA.

  • Outings/leisure (optional): between 100/200$ CA/month

1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline).

If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


Documents you will need to take with you:

- Certified copies of the bachelor's degree and the transcript of the bachelor

- CAQ and proof of obtaining a study permit


Please note : upon arrival, you will be asked to provide official copies of all transcripts and diplomas obtained (i.e. your baccalaureate diploma and transcript) at the Office of the Registrar.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.

Additionally, please note that there are additional tuition fees on the side of the partner university that you need to take into account: 2 900€ for French and Belgian students and 15 000€ for non-French and non-Belgian students.


2. Visa

The steps must be taken at the green light from the University, because the procedures can take a long time. Check out updated information directly on the university's website. Once you have your admission letter in hand, you must obtain:

  • the Quebec Acceptance Certificate for studies (CAQ) , issued by the government of Quebec (At the expense of the student : 124$ CA). The application of the CAQ for studies must be done online and it takes approximatively 6 weeks to be issued.The steps to apply for the CAQ:
  • Once you have received your admission letter, follow these steps and apply online: www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/electronic-services/caq-electronic/index.html
  • Complete the online CAQ application
  • Print: declaration and commitment form (must be signed) and the personalized checklist
  • Review and ensure you have the appropriate support documents – remember to include ALL pages of your Offer of Admission.


We boldly recommend that you mail your application package with all supporting documents by express mail to the address indicated on the personalized checklist.

Note: Whether you apply online or mail your application, you must mail the required documents to MIFI's Montréal office, regardless of your current place of residence. Your application will not be considered until all supporting documents have been received, so don't delay. Processing time is 4 to 8 weeks!


  • The bank letter in French will be required for the CAQ request (see corresponding paragraph below). As an indication, the amount requested amount is around 24 617$ CAD in 2026.
  • Please follow the sample letter available by clicking here . For the tuition fees, you will pay those of Epitech.


PLEASE NOTE: if the bank letter is not in your name but that of your parents, for example, you must attach the declaration of financial support (you must also attach it for the CAQ request): http: // www .immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca / publications / fr / etudes / D09.pdf


  • the study permit, issued by Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada - IRCC (Cost to be borne by the student: 150 $ CA + 85$ for biometrics fee). Once you have received the electronic version of your CAQ, immediately apply for your Study Permit. The application must be done online on the IRCC website. This study permit application automatically includes a visa or Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) at no additional cost. Apply online: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/apply.html


  • The IRCC website allow you to pay fees related to the study permit application, apply for the study permit, verify the status of your application.
  • The estimated time for the process is 12 weeks.


  • Go to this website to see the study permit application process : Guide 5269 – Présenter une demande de permis d’études de l‘extérieur du Canada - Canada.ca


  • Citizens of all countries except the United States and other minor exceptions have to give their biometrics in order to obtain a visa or permit.
  • In the hours following submission of your online application, you will receive the 'instruction letter' in your MyCIC account with instructions to submit your biometrics at a collection service point. For more information, just click here: https://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/information/ou-fournir-donnees-biometriques.asp


  • Students who reside or have resided for six months or more in the past year in certain countries need a medical exam by a IRCC-approved physician. You should allow at least one month for this process, and you are responsible for the cost of the exam. The embassy that handles your case will contact you and provide instructions as needed.


  • Citizens of certain countries must obtain a temporary resident visa (TRV) or electronic travel authorization (eTA) from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) to be able to enter Canada. The visa is placed directly in your passport, whereas the eTA is electronically linked to your passport. Your application for a study permit made outside Canada automatically includes a visa or an eTA at no additional cost.


  • You will receive confirmation that the study permit has been issued, and you will have to queue at the immigration services at your point of entry into Canada to collect the study permit.


Note: when applying for a study permit, you must indicate the number of the designated educational institution (PST) of your university in Canada. You can find the PST for your institution on the following page: http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/etudier/etudier-etablissements-liste.asp


  • Regarding the study permit, on the form to be completed (imm1294f) and to be provided on the Quebec immigration site, you are asked the level of study at this university: put 'University Baccalaureate'.


  • Upon receipt of the document, there you will also thoroughly check your number of Electronic Travel Authorization (AVE) appeared in the second paragraph of the second page. If it does not appear, you will have to make the request online via the following site: http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/visiter/ave.asp The request is processed in 72 hours and the cost is $7.


  • Please note: obtaining the CAQ and Study Permit takes several months, which is why it is essential to start applying for the CAQ upon receipt of the letter of admission. In the absence of these documents, entry to the territory may be refused.


3. International insurance

You can find here some information about the health and hospitalization insurance from Laval University for international students


Enrolling in the health and hospitalization insurance plan for international students | Université Laval (ulaval.ca)


Basic social protection

There is a specific agreement between France and Quebec for basic social protection on site for students of French nationality. This agreement allows you to benefit from on-site support for your health expenses (up to the equivalent of French student social security).

The file will be to be created upon receipt of acceptance at the host university. The process can take several months. Proof of your affiliation with student social security in France will be required.


Before departure: You will need to ask your health insurance company for the necessary supporting documents and the SE 401-Q-106 form . This form, already completed by the international relations department, can be found in the media of your international relations intranet. You must then send it to the CPAM of your residence in order to have it signed. The validated form which will be returned to you by the CPAM will certify that you will be insured under the social security system in France and will allow your affiliation in Quebec. (NB: upon receipt of the form, remember to check the validity period which will have been indicated by the CPAM. Any form which will not cover you for the full duration of your stay will imply a renewal of the process during the year ) .


Upon arrival in Quebec: You will need to register with the Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ) by submitting this form.

You will therefore be able to access RAMQ health care benefits and benefit from health and maternity insurance. In the event of a work accident or occupational disease, you will be covered by the Commission de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CSST).

Please note: it will be important to present the RAMQ affiliation certificate to the Bureau du Registraire. Otherwise, the university will be legally required to bill you for its own international health insurance. Late fees may also be imposed on you if you do not send the affiliation certificate before the deadline given to you.


Social protection and complementary health


You must also take out international insurance (covering your medical and hospital costs on site, as well as repatriation). The market is quite open, among our privileged partners:

ACS, contact Sandra Zagzag: szagzag@acs-ami.com / 01.40.47.91.02

AVI, contact Afida Koucha: akoucha@avi-international.com/ 01.44.63.51.32

ISIS, contact Christine Barrat: christine.barrat@creassur-adc.com

Worldpass, contact : grady@worldpass.fr / 09 71 09 10 15 (promo code: 9EPITECH - allows you to benefit from a tariff reduction of 20%.)

Chapka, contact: info@chapka.fr / 01 74 85 50 50 (promo code: EPITECH10)


Make it clear to each contact that you are a student at EPITECH and that you will benefit from a preferential rate.


4. Help on arrival

If you arrive at Montréal-Trudeau airport in August (between August 4 and September 1), you can inquire about the "Accueil Plus" service, which allows you to reduce the waiting time for recover your study permit: http://www.accueilplus.ca/?lang=fr


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane
schools.accomodation:
University residences

You can book a room in a residence at: http://www.residences.ulaval.ca/

Please note, reservations must be made upon admission to Laval, contact: sres@sres.ulaval.ca


Note : The reservation is made from the start of the program. If you arrive before, you will be asked to pay an additional fee for each night you stay

For further information, see https://www.residences.ulaval.ca/futurs-residents/chambres-et-tarifs/


Off-campus accommodation :

If you prefer to live off campus, you can find ads at : https://www.bve.ulaval.ca/etudiants-etrangers/vivre-a-quebec/logement/logement-hors-campus/


Here are some basics about housing :

  • Housing division :

The number before the “½” indicates the number of rooms making up the accommodation and the “½” represents the bathroom. For example, for your family, explore the prices of housing types 4 ½ and 5 ½. Housing 4 ½ = 4 rooms (2 bedrooms, 1 kitchen and 1 living room) + 1 bathroom.

Housing 5 ½ = 5 rooms (3 bedrooms, 1 kitchen and 1 living room) + 1 bathroom.


  • Heating and electricity :

In the ad, if it says "n-ch, n-é" it means that neither heating nor electricity is included in the monthly payments and therefore that you will have to pay your electricity bill. You can therefore expect an additional 80$ to 120$ per month which will be added to your monthly fees.

Some units include heating and electricity, which means that the rent is fixed and includes these services.

Always ask the landlord if lighting and heating (electricity) costs are included in your rent.


  • Furniture :

In Quebec, a “semi-furnished” type apartment only includes a stove and a refrigerator (appliances). You will then need to find a table, a bed and other furniture.

It is very rare to find furnished apartments in Quebec.


  • Telecommunications :

In Quebec, telecommunication services operate on a flat rate basis and are usually the responsibility of the tenant.

You have to plan 100$ to 120$ per month for a basic trio.

The basic trios include a landline, internet connection and cable TV.

Telephone calls operate on a flat rate basis. Local calls are free, but long distance and overseas calls are charged.

Telecommunication services are much more expensive than in Europe and some cell phones in other countries do not work in Quebec.


A good piece of advice to give is to take an Airbnb on site before finding accommodation so that you can visit it in person (if you do not decide to stay on the Laval student campus). And beware of bus subscriptions between the north and south banks, know that it is much more expensive than in France.


Campus Life

Located in Quebec City, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the University of Laval offers a lively cultural, sporting and social life with many activities and amenities.


The campus, which is 1.8 km square wide, is dotted with great architecture, greenery and woods. It has a modern sports complex, among the most impressive in the country, as well as numerous hiking trails and underground walkways.

The university has nearly 40,000 students from over 110 countries. It is ranked among the ten largest research universities in Canada and is the first French-speaking university in America. It’s a very prestigious university.


It has over 500 different programs for all kind of studies and is one of the hearts of the intellectual ecosystem of Québec.
schools.courses:
Academic calendar

  • Fall semester: from the beginning of September to mid-December
  • Winter semester: from the beginning of January to the end of April


Take into account the possible course requirements for the next semester when you enroll for the first semester courses (which one you need to take on the 1st semester to be able to take one on the 2nd semester).


Program


Tailor-made certificate in information technology - diploma program (30 local credits), 1st cycle 


The program is made up of 21 local credits from block 1 (7 courses) in computer science (IFT and GLO) and 9 local credits (3 courses) of elective courses, ie 30 local credits over the year, therefore 15 local credits per session. Two distance learning courses are authorized per session.   


To obtain the diploma certificate, you must validate 30 local credits AND have a minimum average of 2*. Please note, the course requires a lot of personal work and few students manage to validate the certificate (around 20 to 25 percent generally speaking).


* The average of all your courses must be equal to or greater than 2. So, it is possible to obtain a D in a course, but still have a general average greater than 2 if the other grades are good. 

 

PLEASE NOTE: if you choose the diploma program, you cannot take master's level courses.


Credits

For EPITECH, if a student (diploma course) has obtained 12 local credits per session, i.e. 24 local credits, this is equivalent to 60 ECTS. However, if you have not obtained the 30 local credits required by Laval, you will not obtain the diploma.


Fall 

• Diploma program: take 5 classes (15 credits) 

Winter 

• Diploma program: take 5 classes (15 credits) 

 

Courses

You will have access to the following courses: 

• all IFT and GLO courses from 2000 to 5999   

• Management and Marketing courses and Organizational Information System. 1000 level 

• For those who take master's courses, they will have access to all the classes mentioned from 6000 except the following courses:   

IFT 7014 Directed Readings 

IFT 7026 Experimental project 

IFT 8002 Basic Knowledge Exam 

IFT 8003 Research project proposal 

IFT 8004 Thesis project proposal 

These courses are all 3 credits.


Please note: the course "GLO4001 introduction à la robotique" is complicated and requires a very good level in mathematics (theoretical mathematics).

Please note, for both programs, you are limited to 2 distance courses per session maximum.     

 

Concerning the preferences that are made in January, students must choose between taking the diploma program or not. Epitech will cover tuition fees in Laval to the extent of the credits required to obtain 60 ECTS credits. Any additional module you wish to follow will be at your expense.

You cannot change programs once there. 

Important: All courses are taught in French and theoretical. Presence in class compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits). The courses are most likely more academic than at Epitech . 

The course list is given to you for information. It can change from year to year. If a course is not available when you arrive, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
schools.cost:
Estimated Budget :

Take into account you have a tuition fee for French & Belgian students or 15 000€ tuition fee for non-french & non belgian students.

Departure and costs relative to settling in : 

  • Paris - Quebec round trip flights (YQB) : around 800 euros (during back-to-school periods, the university sets up a shuttle system to the campus) 
  • CAQ :120 $ CA 
  • Study permit : 150 $ CA 
  • Adapted clothing for winter in Quebec : 500 $ CA 
  • Arrival (travel, temporary accommodation, restaurants) : 450 $ CA 
  • Moving in costs (housing equipment, deposits ...) : 600 $ CA 
  • University pass : 147.60 $CA per semester. It offers unlimited access to the regular services of the Capitale Transport Network (RTC) and the Société de transport de Lévis (STLévis), including the services of the Société des traversiers du Québec (Québec / Lévis), for Fall and Winter sessions. 

In total, about € 2,000 

You can also look here to get an idea of the budget. 


Living expenses : 

  • Accommodation on campus : from 382 $ CA /month without bedding and 550$ CA (for rooms in the largest houses) https://www.residences.ulaval.ca/futurs-residents/chambres-et-tarifs/ 


  • You can have access to an ethernet connection for 10 $CA/Month for 100 Go   

or Off-campus accommodation : count 500 $ CA/ month depending on the location and sharing of accommodation (the city center of Québec city can be really expensive) 


  • Food : 350 $ CA / month 

You should know that the bus network (including the ferry north of Quebec connecting old Quebec & Lévis) is maintained by two companies: one on the north shore (Quebec) & one on the south shore (Lévis). Paying just one of the two river banks is about 60$ a month (we have a reduction of 6$ thanks to Laval), paying both is more than 100$ a month. It is entirely possible to live on the south bank and pay only for the south bank : a single line goes up on the north bank & goes around the Laval campus. Without a monthly pass, the price of a trip (only one bus, no change) is 3.50$ per trip, whether on the north shore or the south shore. 


  • Telephone, Internet, etc. : 40 to 70$ CA / month 
  • Personal expenses, leisure, clothing, etc. : around 400 $/ month 
  • Books, school materials and furnitures : From 250$ to 450$ per semester depending on the courses taken. (Please note : a specific calculator can be requested). Certain subjects (in particular optional courses) require compulsory books (which are sometimes rarely used) which are quite expensive (over 100$ per book) and may be diffcult to find in time 
  • International medical insurance : 350$CA per semester for non-French students 
  • Edition of transcript : 10$ 


Please note : the university will offer you various medical, dental and other insurance options during your orientation week. If you do not wish to subscribe to it, you must let the university know. Otherwise these costs will be billed directly to you. They will not be supported by Epitech. 

These prices are for information only, they may vary.

  • You will receive confirmation that the study permit has been issued, and you will have to queue at the immigration services at your point of entry into Canada to collect the study permit.


Note: when applying for a study permit, you must indicate the number of the designated educational institution (PST) of your university in Canada. You can find the PST for your institution on the following page: http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/etudier/etudier-etablissements-liste.asp


  • Regarding the study permit, on the form to be completed (imm1294f) and to be provided on the Quebec immigration site, you are asked the level of study at this university: put 'University Baccalaureate'.


  • Upon receipt of the document, there you will also thoroughly check your number of Electronic Travel Authorization (AVE) appeared in the second paragraph of the second page. If it does not appear, you will have to make the request online via the following site: http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/visiter/ave.asp The request is processed in 72 hours and the cost is $7.


  • Please note: obtaining the CAQ and Study Permit takes several months, which is why it is essential to start applying for the CAQ upon receipt of the letter of admission. In the absence of these documents, entry to the territory may be refused.


3. International insurance

You can find here some information about the health and hospitalization insurance from Laval University for international students


Enrolling in the health and hospitalization insurance plan for international students | Université Laval (ulaval.ca)


Basic social protection

There is a specific agreement between France and Quebec for basic social protection on site for students of French nationality. This agreement allows you to benefit from on-site support for your health expenses (up to the equivalent of French student social security).

The file will be to be created upon receipt of acceptance at the host university. The process can take several months. Proof of your affiliation with student social security in France will be required.


Before departure: You will need to ask your health insurance company for the necessary supporting documents and the SE 401-Q-106 form . This form, already completed by the international relations department, can be found in the media of your international relations intranet. You must then send it to the CPAM of your residence in order to have it signed. The validated form which will be returned to you by the CPAM will certify that you will be insured under the social security system in France and will allow your affiliation in Quebec. (NB: upon receipt of the form, remember to check the validity period which will have been indicated by the CPAM. Any form which will not cover you for the full duration of your stay will imply a renewal of the process during the year ) .


Upon arrival in Quebec: You will need to register with the Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ) by submitting this form.

You will therefore be able to access RAMQ health care benefits and benefit from health and maternity insurance. In the event of a work accident or occupational disease, you will be covered by the Commission de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CSST).

Please note: it will be important to present the RAMQ affiliation certificate to the Bureau du Registraire. Otherwise, the university will be legally required to bill you for its own international health insurance. Late fees may also be imposed on you if you do not send the affiliation certificate before the deadline given to you.


Social protection and complementary health


You must also take out international insurance (covering your medical and hospital costs on site, as well as repatriation). The market is quite open, among our privileged partners:

ACS, contact Sandra Zagzag: szagzag@acs-ami.com / 01.40.47.91.02

Chapka, contact: info@chapka.fr / 01 74 85 50 50 (promo code: EPITECH10)


Make it clear to each contact that you are a student at EPITECH and that you will benefit from a preferential rate.


4. Help on arrival

If you arrive at Montréal-Trudeau airport in August (between August 4 and September 1), you can inquire about the "Accueil Plus" service, which allows you to reduce the waiting time for recover your study permit: http://www.accueilplus.ca/?lang=fr

University residences

Please note, reservations must be made upon admission to Laval, contact: sres@sres.ulaval.ca


Note : The reservation is made from the start of the program. If you arrive before, you will be asked to pay an additional fee for each night you stay

For further information, see https://www.residences.ulaval.ca/futurs-residents/chambres-et-tarifs/


Off-campus accommodation :

If you prefer to live off campus, you can find ads at : https://www.bve.ulaval.ca/etudiants-etrangers/vivre-a-quebec/logement/logement-hors-campus/


Here are some basics about housing :

  • Housing division :

The number before the “½” indicates the number of rooms making up the accommodation and the “½” represents the bathroom. For example, for your family, explore the prices of housing types 4 ½ and 5 ½. Housing 4 ½ = 4 rooms (2 bedrooms, 1 kitchen and 1 living room) + 1 bathroom.

Housing 5 ½ = 5 rooms (3 bedrooms, 1 kitchen and 1 living room) + 1 bathroom.


  • Heating and electricity :

In the ad, if it says "n-ch, n-é" it means that neither heating nor electricity is included in the monthly payments and therefore that you will have to pay your electricity bill. You can therefore expect an additional 80$ to 120$ per month which will be added to your monthly fees.

Some units include heating and electricity, which means that the rent is fixed and includes these services.

Always ask the landlord if lighting and heating (electricity) costs are included in your rent.


  • Furniture :

In Quebec, a “semi-furnished” type apartment only includes a stove and a refrigerator (appliances). You will then need to find a table, a bed and other furniture.

It is very rare to find furnished apartments in Quebec.


  • Telecommunications :

In Quebec, telecommunication services operate on a flat rate basis and are usually the responsibility of the tenant.

You have to plan 100$ to 120$ per month for a basic trio.

The basic trios include a landline, internet connection and cable TV.

Telephone calls operate on a flat rate basis. Local calls are free, but long distance and overseas calls are charged.

Telecommunication services are much more expensive than in Europe and some cell phones in other countries do not work in Quebec.


A good piece of advice to give is to take an Airbnb on site before finding accommodation so that you can visit it in person (if you do not decide to stay on the Laval student campus). And beware of bus subscriptions between the north and south banks, know that it is much more expensive than in France.


Campus Life

Located in Quebec City, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the University of Laval offers a lively cultural, sporting and social life with many activities and amenities.


The campus, which is 1.8 km square wide, is dotted with great architecture, greenery and woods. It has a modern sports complex, among the most impressive in the country, as well as numerous hiking trails and underground walkways.

The university has nearly 40,000 students from over 110 countries. It is ranked among the ten largest research universities in Canada and is the first French-speaking university in America. It’s a very prestigious university.


It has over 500 different programs for all kind of studies and is one of the hearts of the intellectual ecosystem of Québec.
schools.courses:
Academic calendar

  • Fall semester: from the beginning of September to mid-December
  • Winter semester: beginning of January to the end of April.


Take into account the possible course requirements for the next semester when you enroll for the first semester courses (which one you need to take on the 1st semester to be able to take one on the 2nd semester).


Program


Tailor-made certificate in information technology - non-diploma program (24 local credits), 1st cycle. 


Please note : registration is done in the tailor-made Certificate in Technology program for billing reasons by the partner university. You will therefore have access to both certificate and master's courses. The courses are at a high level (BAC + 6/7) only a dozen students with an advanced profile can be selected after stating their requests to access these courses. These are 2nd cycle courses. If you are interested in master's courses, please let us know by ticket help.epitech.eu when you apply.  

Only the best students will have access to these master's courses as they are very difficult. These courses correspond to a Research Master level, while all the undergraduate courses correspond to Engineering level courses. 

Please note that you will be in the non-graduate path of the certificate, but will have the opportunity to take up to 2 graduate classes, without being at the master's level.

Depending on the profiles, the partner university will authorize a few students to take 2 classes/sessions within the master's degree in computer science. Please note, these courses require a very high level in mathematics and a significant workload. 


Credits

Students with a non-diploma certificate must take 24 credits over the year, i.e. 12 local credits per session in order to maintain their visa and obtain the equivalence of 60 ECTS credits. 


They must take 4 lessons per session, making a total of 8 lessons per year. Two distance learning courses are authorized per session. 

 

Fall 

• Non-degree program: take 4 classes (12 credits)

Winter 

• Non-degree program: take 4 classes (12 credits) 

 

Courses

You will have access to the following courses: 

• all IFT and GLO courses from 2000 to 5999   

• Management and Marketing courses and Organizational Information System. 1000 level 

• For those who take master's courses, they will have access to all the classes mentioned from 6000 except the following courses:   

IFT 7014 Directed Readings 

IFT 7026 Experimental project 

IFT 8002 Basic Knowledge Exam 

IFT 8003 Research project proposal 

IFT 8004 Thesis project proposal 

These courses are all 3 credits.


Please note: the course "GLO4001 introduction à la robotique" is complicated and requires a very good level in mathematics (theoretical mathematics).

Please note, for both programs, you are limited to 2 distance courses per session maximum.     

 

Concerning the preferences that are made in January, students must choose between taking the diploma program or not.


Epitech will cover tuition fees in Laval to the extent of the credits required to obtain 60 ECTS credits. Any additional module you wish to follow will be at your expense.

You cannot change programs once there. 


Important: All courses are taught in French and theoretical. Presence in class compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits). The courses are most likely more academic than at Epitech . 


The course list is given to you for information. It can change from year to year. If a course is not available when you arrive, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.

schools.name: University of California. Los Angeles - Extension
schools.overview:
The University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is a public land-grant research university in Los Angeles, California. UCLA’s academic roots were established in 1882 as a teachers college then known as the southern branch of the California State Normal School (now San José State University). This school was absorbed with the official founding of UCLA as the Southern Branch of the University of California in 1919, making it the second-oldest of the 10-campus University of California system (after UC Berkeley).

UCLA is considered one of the United States’ Public Ivies, and is frequently ranked among the best universities in the world by major college and university rankings

UCLA student-athletes compete as the Bruins in the Pac-12 Conference. The Bruins have won 119 NCAA team championships, second only to Stanford University's 128 team titles. In total, 410 Bruins have made Olympic teams, winning 270 Olympic medals: 136 gold, 71 silver, and 63 bronze. UCLA has been represented in every Olympics since the university's founding with one exception (1924) and has had a gold medalist in every Olympics the U.S. participated in since 1932.

2. Visa

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.


1/ Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to the university, you will receive an acceptance letter and an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/ Pay the SEVIS fees

You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3. Insurance and Health

UCLA requires students to purchase the university health insurance, unless your health insurance meets the criteria for a waiver.

More information, including rates, policy details, and criteria for exemptions can be found on this website.

You must demonstrate proof of health insurance coverage before arriving to the U.S., as part of your I-20 application.

In order to be fully covered in the event of an accident (especially outside the region), we recommend that all students take out international insurance during their Tech 4 abroad. It is imperative that you take out an international insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. 


To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information. 


For more information, you can consult the country's health file a: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis.

Students must take a total of 36 local credits per semester to obtain 60 ECTS for the year, not counting EIP credits.

Most courses are 4 credits, and UCLA functions on a trimester system, so this means 3 courses per trimester.


Epitech will cover the tuition fees at UCLA Extension to the extent of the credits required according to the program followed. Any additional module you wish to take will be at your expense.


Academic Calendar (more information here)

  • Fall Quarter: September – December
  • Winter Quarter: January – March
  • Spring Quarter: March – June


Department and Courses

Students will complete a dual certificate in Data Analytics and Cybersecurity.

Students will be enrolled in the program Data Science with Concentration in Cybersecurity (see details here), for a total of 32 credits (8 classes). The remaining class (4 credits) can be chosen from any course in the Machine Learning course listed below.


Course Format and Workload

As the curriculum at UCLA Extension is more theoretical than that at Epitech, you should expect:

  • have homework to do
  • current presence is required
  • theoretical teaching
  • lecture

The grading system is based on a scale from 1 to 100. In order to pass a class, you must receive at least 70.

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.

schools.name: University of California, Santa Barbara
schools.overview:
The University of California, Santa Barbara (UC Santa Barbara or UCSB) is a public land-grant research university in Santa Barbara, California with 23,196 undergraduates and 2,983 graduate students enrolled in 2021-2022. It is part of the University of California 10-university system. Tracing its roots back to 1891 as an independent teachers' college, UCSB joined the University of California system in 1944, and is the third-oldest undergraduate campus in the system, after UC Berkeley and UCLA.


Located on a WWII-era Marine air station, UC Santa Barbara is organized into three undergraduate colleges (College of Letters and Science, College of Engineering, College of Creative Studies) and two graduate schools (Gevirtz Graduate School of Education and Bren School of Environmental Science & Management), offering more than 200 degrees and programs. The university has 10 national research centers, including the Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics and the Center for Control, Dynamical-Systems and Computation. UCSB has various organized research units (ORUs) researching evolutionary psychology, neuroscience, marine science, and more. According to the National Science Foundation, UC Santa Barbara spent $235 million on research and development in fiscal year 2018, ranking it 100th in the nation. UCSB was the No. 3 host on the ARPAnet and was elected to the Association of American Universities in 1995.


Current UCSB faculty includes six Nobel Prize laureates, one Fields Medalist, 39 members of the National Academy of Sciences, 27 members of the National Academy of Engineering, and 34 members of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. UCSB is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity" and is regarded as a Public Ivy. The faculty also includes two Academy and Emmy Award winners, and recipients of a Millennium Technology Prize, an IEEE Medal of Honor, a National Medal of Technology and Innovation and a Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics.
schools.administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • Photocopy of passport / Residence permit (valid more than 6 months after return)
  • Registration forms for UCSB (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)
  • A letter from the bank with a provision of $20,000 dated less than 6 months
  • If the bank letter is from a parent's bank account, it must attest to the relationship and mention that the amount available may be used for your expenses during your year abroad in the United States.
  • Course selection form for UCSB (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)
  • University insurance subscription consent form (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


2. Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website. You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1/Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to UCSB, you will receive an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3.Insurance and Health

University health insurance

UCSB requires students to purchase the university health insurance, unless your health insurance meets the criteria for a waiver.

You must demonstrate proof of health insurance coverage before arriving to the U.S., as part of your I-20 application.

The insurance brochure summarizing what is covered and not (typically dental and vision are NOT covered and you need to make your own arrangements for these) for 2025 can be found at: student.jcbins.com/1479.

You will first receive an email from the insurance and then you can register so do not try and register before receiving emails from them.

If you have any questions about insurance, please have them contact JCB directly at GGB.JCB.Studentservices@ajg.com


Please also note the following important info: In the US, medical coverage does not usually cover 3rd party liability (it is a separate insurance contract that does), which means the UCSB insurance Anthem is a medical-only insurance.

Coverage is only in the USA but you can also subscribe to a worldwide insurance at: geobluestudents.com


International insurance

In order to be fully covered in the event of an accident (especially outside the region), we recommend that all students take out international insurance during their year abroad. It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


In addition, all incoming students must complete a five question Tuberculosis Screening Questionnaire which is located on the Clearances tab in your MyHealth portal. For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

You have the option to take an Airbus from LAX to SB. To book tickets, visit: sbairbus.com The one-way fee per person is approximately $55.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here.
schools.accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

They cannot predict nor guarantee that there will be vacancies on campus and the Fall quarter is the one where the probability for international students to get campus housing is the most challenging but this year many international students could secure campus housing. For Winter and Spring quarters there are typically more vacancies.

That said, you can apply for UCSB campus housing as soon as you receive your UCSB NetID which should be by early September 2025 or immediately thereafter. To do so, please visit this link once you have your NetID. 

We should know if there are places left about 2 to 3 weeks before the quarter starts. 

See also this website to see where there might be vacancies


IMPORTANT - For those of you who are interested in applying for campus housing but are only staying for one semester and therefore reluctant to take those contracts on campus (which are are typically for one year), please see below the important information: If students give 30 days or more notice there is a $250 fee to cancel. It increases to $350 if they inform the UCSB Housing in less than 30 days. In the contract there is a clause about it, so depending on the contract they sign, it should indicate the cancellation fee. Put briefly, it would not cost you so much to break/cancel the contract after 3, 6 or even 9 months as this is apparently common practice. 


Off-campus accommodation

International students typically live off campus, usually in privately owned residence halls, homestays, or furnished apartments. Off-campus, non-UCSB housing is available year-round; students make reservations directly with housing providers.  

First, please join the official UCSB WhatsApp group as it will also help you with acaditalicic or housing questions.

Second, the idea is that some of you - when possible at all - may want to take over the lease of those currently in SB who are away for the Fall quarter only. Those staying for the full year may also know of some vacancies so please do not hesitate to post a message asking for help. Finding accommodation at Santa Barbara can also be challenging and requires some research (and resilience) so they are sending informations to recommend the best sites and courses of action for you to start with your research as soon as possible.


1. Facebook groups

Make sure you join the FB groups IV Housing UCSB and UCSB Housing as there are lots of subleasing offers already there for one quarter.


2. Appartment listing websites

  • SBCC (Santa Barbara Community College) Housing list  
  • Student Roomstay - https://studentroomstay.com/abrego 
  • Coral Group - https://www.coralgroupsb.com/ 
  • Roomster - https://www.roomster.com/en-GB/haveshare/santa-barbara-ca-usa 
  • Craiglist Santa Barbara (this is a peer-to-peer website, equivalent to French Le Bon Coin, if you are French). Check their housing section and within that:
  • the room and share section here 
  • the sublets and temporary section here 

You can also look at their sublet/temporary link if you come to SB a little before your program starts for the orientation and for exploring housing options that are not offered online.


There will be different prices for different locations there too so do spend enough time exploring and visit regularly for updates.

  • St George's Associates - https://www.stgeorgeassociates.com/ (for full year singles)
  • The Loop Isla Vista - https://www.theloopiv.com/ 

This person who works at UCSB also typically has a couple of rooms to rent every quarter on a first-come-first-served basis: sofiamuller@ucsb.edu


 Important Notes:

  • Subleasing is a normal practice at UCSB. This is often because UCSB full -time students who leave UCSB to go abroad for one or more quarters will be looking to sublease/rent out their apartments/rooms for the duration of their study abroad and to get their rooms back when they return to Santa Barbara. You will find many of these on the FB groups mentioned above. This is a good way to find your accommodation but there can be scams.
  • If the offers sound too good to be true, be careful. 
  • Always ask the people who propose to sublease to have a video conference on WhatsApp or Telegram so you can see the house and room at the right address.
  • Never pay a deposit before seeing the apartment for yourself.

Visa

The offer of admission to the UM mobility program DOES NOT come with the Student Visa which is strictly required by the Malaysian Immigration Department (MID) for students to enter and study in Malaysia. Failure to adhere to the visa application procedures may result in the delay of admission to the University or retraction of admission. Processing time for the visa takes about eight (8) weeks upon submission of complete document.

Please note that you should avoid entering Malaysia during your visa process, to avoid any delay and queries from Malaysian Immigration. It is required that the student is outside Malaysia while the visa is processed and Visit Visas at the same time could result in rejection of your Student Pass Application. Transfer Students may process their application while being in Malaysia; however they will need to apply for a Special Pass for this process and is subject to Malaysian Immigration Approval.

This foundation course is designed to help students discover useful insights from data of various domains. It incorporates the fundamental principles that underlie the algorithms, processes, methods, ethics, and data-analytic thinking in a data science life cycle. The role of data scientist, the knowledge and skills required is also presented. Diverse technologies, programming languages as well as tools in data science are discussed. Students will acquire practical knowledge through hands-on projects to come up with data science solutions and develop data products.

WQD7003 — DATA ANALYTICS

Postgraduate Level — English

This course aims to develop students’ ability to describe, explore and analyze data using suitable data analytics techniques.

WQD7004 — PROGRAMMING FOR DATA SCIENCE

Postgraduate Level — English

This course covers programming languages that are relevant to data science. The course provides students with the necessary programming skills for statistical analysis, exploration of datasets and predictions. These include understanding structures for data organization such as vector, list, matrix, and data frames; basic programming blocks such as operators, control structures, and subsetting; using various libraries for data visualization; running prediction models using various models; and other algorithms.

WOX7001 — Research Methodology

Postgraduate Level — English

This course gives an overview of the dimensions of research in computer science and information technology. Major considerations and tasks in conducting research in the areas such as review of literature, identify problem statement, formulate research questions and objectives

FACULTY OF COMPUTER SCIENCE & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY — Undergraduate

WIG3002 — Rendering and Animation

Undergraduate Level — English

At the beginning of this course, students will be exposed to the development, technology and computer animation applications. Next, students will be taught about the main phases in the development of computer animation which include aspects such as modelling, animation, texturing, lighting, compositing and rendering. At the end of this course, students will be equipped with the knowledge pertaining to the job opportunities and future of computer animation and rendering.

WIG3005 — Game Development

Undergraduate Level — English

This course will give an introduction to computer game development starting from concept development to implementation of a playable game prototype. Both the aesthetic and technical aspects of game development will be covered.

The aesthetic component focuses on story and character development, game mechanics, game play and interface design and content creation for games. The technical component focuses on programming tools and concepts for games, including data structures & algorithms, computer graphics, human-computer interaction, collision detection and AI.

Common topics include project management, prototype development and play testing. Students will work in groups and go through the complete pipeline starting from a basic game idea all the way through developing a playable prototype.

Students must submit the following with their choices in order to be eligible for this destination


TOEFL iBT 61, IELTS 5.5, or Duolingo 95


__________________________________________________________________________



University of Nebraska Omaha (UNO)

Established in 1869, the University of Nebraska Omaha is a public research university located in the heart of Omaha, the largest city of the U.S. state of Nebraska, situated on the west bank of the Missouri River. Then, in 1908, the Omaha Presbyterian Theological Seminary faculty was founded.

As a private non-sectarian college, the university was originally known as the University of Omaha, a place meant to provide Christian-based education free from ecclesiastical control. Indeed, UNO used to serve as a bold alternative to the city’s many successful religiously affiliated institutions.

Ranked as 151 top national universities through the Lincoln’s ranking, the university has increased its students' numbers by opening new dormitories and academic space. It has also recently constructed modern facilities for its engineering, information technology, business, and biomechanics programs.

UNO currently offers more than 200 programs of study across 6 different colleges, with student, athletic, and research facilities spread between 3 campuses.

Today, more than 24,000 students study at UNO, including more than 1,600 international students. UNO is committed to welcoming international students as part of its global mission.

2. Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website. You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1/ Admission letter and I-20 form

Once you are admitted by the host university, UNO will send us your admission package with your acceptance letter and original documents for your visa. You can request a visa only after your application has been approved. After the visa application, proceed to the course enrollment and housing applications on your MavLINK student account.

Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/ Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3.Insurance and Health (more information here)

International J-1 scholars and their dependents must have health insurance from a U.S.-based medical insurance company that pays for health care in Nebraska to maintain nonimmigrant status. UNO has a few specific health insurance options for scholars to meet these federal requirements.


Health insurance coverage for J-1 and J-2 visa holders must include:

  1. Medical benefits of at least $100,000 per illness or accident.
  2. Deductible not to exceed $500 per accident or illness.
  3. Medical evacuation benefit in the amount of $50,000.
  4. Payment for repatriation of remains in the event of death in the amount of $25,000.


The insurance corporation underwriting the insurance policy must meet or exceed the following ratings:

  • A.M. Best or Insurance Solvency International rating of A-
  • Standard & Poor’s claims-paying ability rating of A-
  • Weiss Research, Inc. rating of B+


In addition, UNO requires international students to submit an official copy of the required immunizations and complete a tuberculosis test.

For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

When arriving to Omaha, transportation from the airport is available upon request at: go.unomaha.edu/gettingstarted

International students must attend the orientation day.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here.

schools.name: University of Regina
schools.overview:
The University of Regina (U of R) has campuses located in Regina and Saskatoon, on Treaty 4 and Treaty 6 territories. These are the ancestral lands of the nêhiyawak (nay-hi-yuh-wuk, Cree), Anihšināpēk (uh-nish-i-naa-payk, Saulteaux), Dakota, Lakota, Nakoda, and the homeland of the Métis/Michif Nation.


As a comprehensive university, the U of R traces its roots back to Regina College, a small residential high school established by the Methodist church in 1911. The College grew in size and significance, becoming a campus of the University of Saskatchewan and, ultimately, an independent degree granting university – the University of Regina – in 1974.


Regina is the capital of Saskatchewan and the 16th largest city in Canada with a population of 226,404. Regina is located in the south central area of the province. The city covers an area of 182.42 square kilometers. It is in the middle of the Prairie Provinces with Alberta to the west, and Manitoba to the east. It borders the American states of Montana and North Dakota.
